children.translated_text: That [smoke], existing [where fire is present], would, in the absence of that [fire], violate its being caused. //34//

For that [impermanence], arising later in an entity that has already come into being, from something else—how could it be its cause? Even of an effect, there is not necessarily existence in the cause, and therefore the reason that establishes being of that nature would be inconclusive. Therefore, a property caused by something else is not necessarily present in an entity, and hence it cannot be inferred. If then observation and non-observation are not the basis for [ascertaining] positive and negative concomitance, how is it known that smoke does not deviate from fire? Because:
Smoke is the effect of fire, from the invariable concomitance of the properties of effects. That which, when the conditions for apprehension are fulfilled, is not apprehended when even one [of its causes] is absent—that is its effect. And that [relation] exists in smoke.

children.text:
02206 sakṛd api tathā adarśanāt kāryaṃ siddhaḥ / akāryatve akāraṇāt
02207 sakṛd apy abhāvāt / kāryasya ca sva-kāraṇam antareṇa bhāve
02208 ahetumattā eva syāt / na hi yasya yam antareṇa bhāvaḥ sa tasya
02209 hetur bhavati / bhavati ca dhūmo agnim antareṇa tan na tad-hetuḥ
02210 anya-hetukatvān na ahetukatvam iti cet / na / tatra api
02211 tulyatvāt / tad-abhāve apy agnau bhavati iti / kathaṃ vā tato
02212 anyato vā ataj-janana-svabhāvād bhavet / svayam atat-svabhāvasya
02213 ajananāt tasya ahetutā syāt / na vai sa eva bhavati tādṛśasya
02214 bhāvāt / anya-adṛśād bhavan kathaṃ tādṛśaḥ syāt / tādṛśād hi
02215 bhavan tādṛśaḥ syāt / anya-adṛśād api tādṛśo bhāve tac-śakti-niyama-
02216 abhāvān na hetu-bhedo bhedaka iti akāraṇaṃ viśvasya vaiśvarūpyaṃ
02217 syāt / sarvaṃ vā sarvasmāj jāyeta / tasmāt kāraṇa-
02218 bheda-abhedābhyāṃ kārya-bheda-abhedau / tan na dhūmo arthād dṛṣṭa-
02219 ākāra-vijātīyād bhavaty ahetukatva-prasaṅgāt / tathā ca /
02220 nityaṃ sattvam asattvaṃ vā ahetor anya-anapekṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: There would be permanent existence or permanent non-existence, because without a cause, there is no dependence on anything else.

children.text: 02221 apekṣāto hi bhāvānāṃ kādācitkatva-sambhavaḥ //35//
children.translated_text: For it is due to dependence [on causes] that the occasional occurrence of entities is possible. //35//

It is established as an effect from its non-observation even once in such [absence]. If it were not an effect, [it would be] without a cause, because of its absence even once [without fire]. And if the effect existed without its own cause, there would simply be no causation. For that without which something does not exist is not its cause [if it can exist without it]. And if smoke exists without fire, then [fire] is not its cause. If [one says] that it is not uncaused because it has other causes—no, because the same [argument] applies there too: it exists even in the absence of that [other cause]. Or how could it arise from that [fire] or from something else, when [that other thing] does not have the nature of producing it? Since what is not of that nature does not produce, it would have no cause. Indeed, it is not the very same [thing] that arises, since what arises is of a specific nature. How could something arising from an unseen other be of that specific nature? For it would be of that nature [only] by arising from something of that nature. Even if [it is said that it is] of that nature [though] arising from an unseen other—since there is no restriction of the capacity of that [other cause], the difference of cause would not be a differentiator, and without cause, the whole universe would be uniform. Or everything would arise from everything. Therefore, from the difference and non-difference of causes [arise] the difference and non-difference of effects. Therefore, smoke does not arise from what is dissimilar in appearance to what has been observed—because of the unwanted consequence of causelessness. And thus:

children.text:
02222 sa hi dhūmo ahetur bhavan nirapekṣatvān na kadācin na bhavet /
02223 tad-bhāve vaikalya-abhāvād iṣṭa-kāla-vat / tadā api vā na bhavet /
02224 abhāva-kāla-aviśeṣāt / apekṣayā hi bhāvāḥ kādācitkā bhavanti /
02301 bhāva-abhāva-kālayos tad-bhāva-yogyatā ayogyatā-yogāt tulya-yogyatā
02302 yogyatayor deśa-kālayos tadvattā itarayor niyama-ayogāt / sā ca
02303 yogyatā hetu-bhāvāt kim anyat / tasmād eka-deśa-kāla-parihāreṇa anya-
02304 deśa-kālayor vartamāno bhāvas tat-sāpekṣo nāma bhavati /
02305 tathā hi / tathā vṛttir eva apekṣā tat-kṛta-upakāra-anapekṣasya tan-niyama-
02306 ayogāt / tan niyata-deśa-kālatvād dhūmo atra dṛṣṭaḥ sakṛd
02307 vaikalye ca punar na dṛṣṭaḥ taj-janyo asya svabhāvaḥ / anyathā
02308 sakṛd apy abhāvāt / sa tat-pratiniyato anyatra kathaṃ bhavet /
02309 bhavan vā na dhūmaḥ syāt / taj-janito hi svabhāva-viśeṣo dhūma
02310 iti / tathā hetur api tathābhūta-kārya-janana-svabhāvaḥ / tasya anyato
02311 api bhāve na sa tasya svabhāva iti sakṛd api na janayet /
02312 na vā sa dhūmo adhūma-janana-svabhāvād bhāvāt / tat-svabhāvatve
02313 ca sa eva agnir ity avyabhicāraḥ /
children.translated_text: then that is fire itself—thus there is no deviation.

children.text: 02314 agni-svabhāvaḥ śakrasya mūrddhā yady agnir eva saḥ /
children.translated_text: If the head of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) has the nature of fire, then it is indeed fire;

children.text: 02315 atha anagni-svabhāvo asau dhūmas tatra kathaṃ bhavet //36//
children.translated_text: but if it has a non-fire nature, how could smoke exist there? //36//

For that smoke, being a non-cause, due to its independence, would never not exist. In its presence, due to the absence of deficiency, [it would exist] like at the desired time. Or even then it would not exist, because there is no distinction between the time of absence [and presence]. For things become occasional through dependence. In the times of existence and non-existence, due to the conjunction of fitness and unfitness for that existence, there is equal fitness—in the fit times and places, there is the possession of that; in others, there is no restriction [of occurrence]. And what is that fitness other than the state of being a cause? Therefore, a thing existing in some places and times while avoiding other places and times is said to be dependent on that. For thus: such occurrence itself is dependence, because without consideration of the benefit produced by that, there is no restriction to it. Therefore, since smoke is restricted to [particular] places and times, it is seen here once, and when there is deficiency, it is again not seen—its nature is produced by that [fire]. Otherwise, [it would not be seen] even once, because of [its] absence. That [smoke], being restricted to that [fire], how could it exist elsewhere? Or if it does exist [elsewhere], it would not be smoke. For the specific nature produced by that [fire] is called 'smoke.' Likewise, the cause also has the nature of producing such an effect. If that [cause] exists from something else, then it is not its nature, so it would not produce [that effect] even once. Or it would not be that smoke, because the thing has a nature that does not produce non-smoke. And if it has that nature,

children.text: 02316 dhūma-hetu-svabhāvo hi vahnis tac-śakti-bhedavān /
children.translated_text: Fire has the nature of being the cause of smoke, possessing distinct capacities for that;

children.text: 02317 adhūma-hetor dhūmasya bhāve sa syād ahetukaḥ //37//
children.translated_text: if smoke existed from a non-cause of smoke, it would be causeless. //37//

children.text:
02318 iti saṃgrahaślokau / kathaṃ tarhi idānīṃ bhinnāt sahakāriṇaḥ kārya-
02319 utpatter yathā cakṣū-rūpa-āder vijñānasya / na vai kiṃcid ekaṃ
02320 janakaṃ tat-svabhāvam / kiṃ tu sāmagrī janikā tat-svabhāvā / sa eva
02321 anumīyate / sa eva ca sāmagrī svabhāva-sthity-āśrayaḥ kāryasya /
02322 ata eva sahakāriṇām apy aparyāyeṇa jananam / yad api kiṃcid
02323 vijātīyād bhavad dṛṣṭaṃ gomaya-ādeḥ śāluka-ādi / tatra api tathā abhidhāne
02324 apy asty eva sva-bīja-prabhavāt svabhāva-bhedaḥ / hetu-svabhāva-bhedāt /
02325 yathā kadalī bīja-kanda-udbhavā / sphuṭam eva
02326 tādṛśaṃ loko vivecayaty ākāra-bhedāt / tasmān na suvivecita-ākāraṃ
02327 kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ vyabhicarati /
children.translated_text: does not deviate from its cause.

children.text: 02401 anvaya-vyatirekād yo yasya dṛṣṭo anuvartakaḥ /
children.translated_text: That which is observed through positive and negative concomitance to follow something—

children.text: 02402 svabhāvas tasya tad-hetur ato bhinnān na sambhavaḥ //38//
children.translated_text: that nature is its cause; therefore, [its] arising from something different is impossible. //38//

These are the summary verses. But how then does an effect arise from a distinct cooperating cause, as in the case of consciousness [arising] from the eye, form, and so forth? It is not that any single producer has that nature. Rather, the aggregate is the producer, having that nature. It is that [aggregate] which is inferred. And it is that [aggregate] which is the basis for the essential nature and continuity of the effect. For this very reason, even the cooperating causes produce without alternation. As for what is seen to arise from something of a different kind, such as a lotus root from cow dung—even there, despite such description, there does exist a distinction of essential nature due to origination from its own seed, because of the distinction of the nature of the cause. Just as the banana plant arises from seed and bulb. Clearly, the world discriminates such [cases] from the distinction of form. Therefore, an effect whose form is well-discriminated

children.text:
02403 iti saṃgrahaślokaḥ / tasmāt sakṛd api darśana-adarśanābhyāṃ
02404 kāryakāraṇabhāva-siddher bhavati tatas tat-pratipattiḥ / na anyathā /
02405 anvaya-vyatirekayor niḥśeṣa-darśana-adarśana-āyattatvāt / kvacid
02406 amūrtatve nityatva-darśane apy anyatra anyathā adṛṣṭeḥ / kvacin
02407 nityatva-abhāve apy adṛṣṭasya punar dṛṣṭer iti bhavatu kāryasya
02408 kāraṇena avinābhāvas tadutpatteḥ / svabhāva idānīṃ katham avinābhāvaḥ /
02410 svabhāve apy avinābhāvo bhāva-mātra-anurodhini /
children.translated_text: Even in the case of essential nature, invariable concomitance [exists] for what follows mere existence.

children.text: 02411 yo hi bhāva-mātra-anurodhī svabhāvas tatra avinābhāvo bhāvasya iṣyate /
children.translated_text: For that essential nature which follows mere existence, the invariable concomitance with existence is accepted.

children.text: 02413 tad-abhāve svayaṃ bhāvasya abhāvaḥ syād abhedataḥ //39//
children.translated_text: In the absence of that, existence itself would be absent, due to non-difference. //39//

This is the summary verse. Therefore, since the cause-effect relationship is established even by a single observation and non-observation, the cognition of that [relationship] arises from that, not otherwise—because the positive and negative concomitances depend on the complete observation and non-observation [of all cases]. In some cases, although permanence is observed [together] with incorporeality, since it is not seen otherwise elsewhere; in other cases, although permanence is absent, what was not seen is again seen—thus let there be the invariable concomitance of the effect with the cause due to [the effect's] origination from that. Now, how is essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) invariably concomitant?

children.text:
02414 ya eva bhāvo bhāva-mātra-anurodhī svabhāva ity ucyate / sa eva
02415 svayaṃ vastuto bhāvaḥ / sa ca ātmānaṃ parityajya kathaṃ bhavet /
02416 ya eva tarhi kṛtakaḥ sa eva anityo bheda-abhāvāt / pratijñārthaikadeśo
02417 hetuḥ syāt / na eṣa doṣaḥ / yasmāt /
02418 sarve bhāvāḥ svabhāvena sva-svabhāva-vyavasthiteḥ /
children.translated_text: All entities, by their essential natures, are established in their own respective natures,

children.text: 02419 svabhāva-parabhāvābhyāṃ yasmād vyāvṛtti-bhāginaḥ //40//
children.translated_text: because they participate in exclusion through both essential nature and other-nature. //40//

That very existence which follows mere existence is called 'essential nature.' That is itself, in reality, the entity. And how could it exist while abandoning itself? Then, whatever is produced (<s>kṛtaka</s>) is indeed impermanent, due to the absence of difference. [If one objects that] the <s>hetu</s> would be a part of the <s>pratijñā</s> (thesis)—this is not a fault, because:

children.text: 02420 tasmād yato yato arthānāṃ vyāvṛttis tan-nibandhanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, from whatever [properties] things are excluded, the class-distinctions

children.text: 02421 jāti-bhedāḥ prakalpyante tad-viśeṣa-avagāhinaḥ //41//
children.translated_text: are postulated as based on those [properties], apprehending those specific differences. //41//

children.text: 02422 tasmād yo yena dharmeṇa viśeṣaḥ sampratīyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the specific difference that is cognized through whatever property—

children.text: 02423 na sa śakyas tato anyena tena bhinnā vyavasthitiḥ //42//
children.translated_text: that cannot [be cognized] through another; hence the establishment of distinction. //42//

children.text:
02424 sarva eva hi bhāvāḥ svarūpa-sthitayaḥ / te na ātmānaṃ pareṇa
02425 miśrayanti / tasya aparatva-prasaṅgāt / yad apy eṣām abhinnam
02426 ātmabhūtaṃ rūpaṃ na tat teṣām / tadānīṃ teṣām abhāvāt /
02501 tad eva hi syād abhinnasya bhāvāt / tad-vyatiriktasya bhinnasya
02502 ca abhāvāt / tasya eva ca punar bheda-virodhāt / tac ca ātmani vyavasthitam
02503 amiśram eva / artha-antaram apy aneka-sambandhe api
02504 na tat teṣāṃ sāmānyam atad-rūpatvāt / dvitva-ādi-saṃyoga-kārya-
02505 dravyeṣv api prasaṅgāt / na hi sambandhinā apy anyena anye samānā
02506 nāma / tadvanto nāma syuḥ / bhūta-vat / kaṇṭhe-guṇena /
02507 na abhinna-pratyaya-viṣayāḥ / bhūta-vat / tadātmānam eva hi buddhiḥ
02508 saṃsṛjantī sāmānya-viṣayā pratibhāsate / na eka-sambandhināv iti
02509 bhūta-vat / tad-darśinyāḥ sā bhrāntir iti cet / tad-darśinī iti kutaḥ /
02510 nirbīja-bhrānty-ayogād iti cet / ta eva tad-eka-kāryā bījam / saṃkhyā-
02511 saṃyoga-kārya-dravya-ādimatsu bhūta-ādiṣv abhāvāc ca / tan na tathā
02512 sāmānya-buddhau niveṣa-abhāvāt sāmānyam anyat / sati vā tasya api
02513 svātmani vyavasthānād amiśraṇam anyena / tasmād ime bhāvāḥ
02514 sajātīya-abhimatād anyasmāc ca vyatiriktāḥ svabhāvena eka-rūpatvāt /
02515 yato yato bhinnās tad-bheda-pratyāyanāya kṛta-saṃniveśaiḥ
02516 śabdais tatas tato bhedam upādāya svabhāva-abhede apy aneka-
02517 dharmāṇaḥ pratīyante / te api śabdāḥ sarva-bheda-anākṣepe apy eka-
02518 bheda-codanāt tat-svalakṣaṇa-niṣṭhā eva bhavanti / tad ekasmād
02519 api tasya bhedo asti iti / tasmād ekasya bhāvasya yāvanti pararūpāṇi
02520 tāvat yas tad-apekṣayā vyāvṛttayaḥ / tad-asambhavi-kārya-kāraṇasya
02521 tad-bhedāt / yāvat yaś ca vyāvṛttayas tāvat yaḥ śrutayo
02522 atat-kārya-kāraṇa-parihāreṇa vyavahāra-arthāḥ / yathā prayatnānantarīyakaḥ
02523 śabdaḥ śrāvaṇa ity atat-kārya-kāraṇa-parihāra-arthaḥ /
02524 tasmāt svabhāva-abhede api yena yena dharmeṇa nāmnā yo viśeṣo
02525 bhedaḥ pratīyate na sa śakyo anyena pratyāyayitum iti na eka-arthāḥ
02526 sarva-śabdāḥ / tan na pratijñārthaikadeśo hetur iti / kathaṃ
02527 punar etad gamyate vyavacchedaḥ śabda-liṅgābhyāṃ pratipādyate
02528 vidhinā na vastu-rūpam eva iti / pramāṇa-antarasya śabda- antarasya
02601 ca pravṛtteḥ / tathā hi /
02602 ekasya artha-svabhāvasya pratyakṣasya sataḥ svayam /
children.translated_text: Of a single entity whose nature is directly perceived, existing in itself—

children.text: 02603 ko anyo na dṛṣṭo bhāgaḥ syād yaḥ pramāṇaiḥ parīkṣyate //43//
children.translated_text: what other unseen part could there be that is examined by [further] <s>pramāṇas</s>? //43//

For all entities indeed abide in their own form. They do not mix their self with another, because of the unwanted consequence that that [other] would become non-other. Even if there is an undifferentiated form that is their own nature—that is not [truly] theirs, because at that point they would be absent. For only that [undifferentiated form] would exist, since the undifferentiated exists; and what is different from that, being differentiated, would be absent. And that [differentiated thing], due to the contradiction of difference [with the undifferentiated], would again [be absent]. And that [undifferentiated form], established in itself, is indeed unmixed. Even another entity, though having multiple relations, is not their universal, because it does not have their form; due to the unwanted consequence [applying] even to substances that are the effects of conjunction such as duality and so forth. For things are not called 'the same' as something else even though related to it. They would be called 'possessors of that'—like [possessors of] elements, by a quality of the throat. They are not the objects of an undifferentiated cognition—like elements. For cognition, mixing that very self [with another], appears as having a universal as its object. Not [cognizing] that the two are related to one [universal]—like elements. If [one says] that it is an error of the cognition that sees that—then whence [is it established that it is] 'one that sees that'? If [one says] because there cannot be error without a seed—those very [things], being the single cause of that [cognition], are the seed. And because of the absence [of such a universal] in elements and so forth which possess numerical properties, conjunction-effects, and substances. Therefore, the universal is not something other, because it has no place in the cognition of universals. Or, even if it exists, because it too is established in its own self, there is no mixing with another. Therefore, these entities are excluded by their essential nature from both what is considered homogeneous and from what is other, because they have a single form. From whatever [properties] they are different, in order to convey that difference, words arranged for that [purpose] present them as having many properties even though there is no difference of essential nature, by adopting those [distinctions] from there. Those words too, even though they do not cast off all differences, being prompted by a single difference, are established precisely in the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) of that. Therefore, even from a single [entity], there is differentiation of that. Therefore, however many other-forms a single entity has, that many are its exclusions in reference to those. Because the cause and effect that do not occur in that [entity] differ from it. And however many exclusions there are, that many verbal expressions [exist], serving the purpose of conventional practice by excluding the causes and effects that do not belong to that. Just as 'sound that follows immediately after effort' [or] 'auditory' is for the purpose of excluding causes and effects that do not belong to that. Therefore, even though there is no difference of essential nature, the specific difference that is cognized through whatever property or name cannot be conveyed by another—thus all words are not synonymous. Therefore, the <s>hetu</s> is not a part of the <s>pratijñā</s>. But how is it understood that exclusion is conveyed by words and logical marks positively and not merely as the form of the object? Because of the operation of another <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) and another word. For thus:

children.text:
02604 eko hy artha-ātmā / sa pratyakṣaḥ asiddhe dharmiṇi sādhana-asambhavāt /
02605 yathā anityatve sādhye śabdaḥ / tasya pratyakṣeṇa eva siddheḥ
02606 sarva-ākāra-siddhiḥ / tad-anyasya asiddhasya abhāvāt / bhāve vā
02607 atat-svabhāvatvam / na hi yo yad ekayogakṣemo na bhavati sa
02608 tat-svabhāvo yuktaḥ / tan-mātra-nibandhanatvāt / bheda-vyavahārasya /
02609 anyathā abhāva-prasaṅgād ity uktam / tasmāt pratyakṣe dharmiṇi
02610 tat-svabhāva-sākalya-paricchedāt tatra anavakāśā pramāṇa-antara-
children.translated_text: since the totality of its nature is delimited, there is no scope there for the operation of another

children.text: 02611 vṛttiḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: 02612 no ced bhrānti-nimittena saṃyojyeta guṇa-antaram /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, due to a cause of error, another property would be conjoined—

children.text: 02613 śuktau vā rajata-ākāro rūpa-sādharmya-darśanāt //44//
children.translated_text: like the appearance of silver in a shell, due to perceiving a similarity of form. //44//

For the nature of the object is one. It is directly perceived, since proof is impossible when the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) is unestablished. For example, sound, when impermanence is to be proved. Since all aspects are established through direct perception alone, there is the establishment of all forms. Because what is other than that, being unestablished, does not exist. Or if it exists, it does not have that nature. For what does not share the same fortune with something is not reasonably of that nature, because [conventional practice of] distinction is based on that alone. Otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence of non-existence—as has been stated. Therefore, for a <s>dharmin</s> that is directly perceived,

children.text:
02614 yadi dṛṣṭa-sarva-tattvasya api bhāvasya tathā niścaya-pratirodhinā
02615 bhrānti-nimittena guṇa-antaraṃ na saṃyojyate / yathā śuktau rajata-
02616 ākāraḥ / na hi śuktau dve rūpe samānaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ ca tathā
02617 pratipatti-prasaṅgāt / apratipattau vā vivekena dvitva-vikalpa-ayogāt /
02618 atiprasaṅgāc ca / tasmāt paśyan śukti-rūpaṃ viśiṣṭam eva
02619 paśyati / niścaya-pratyaya-vaikalyāt tv aniścinvan tat-sāmānyaṃ
02620 paśyāmi iti manyate / tato asya rajata-samāropaḥ / tathā / sadṛśā-para-apara-
02621 utpattyā alakṣita-nānātvasya tad-bhāva-samāropāt sthito-bhrāntiḥ /
02622 yāvanto asya parabhāvās tāvanta eva yathāsvaṃ nimitta-
02623 bhāvinaḥ samāropā iti tad-vyavacchedakāni bhavanti pramāṇāni
02624 saphalāni syuḥ / teṣāṃ tu vyavaccheda-phalānāṃ na apratīta-vastv-aṃśa-
02701 pratyāyane pravṛttis tasya dṛṣṭatvāt / anaṃśasya ca eka-deśena
02702 darśana-ayogāt /
children.translated_text: are fruitful, due to the impossibility of seeing what has no parts by a part [alone].

children.text: 02703 tasmād dṛṣṭasya bhāvasya dṛṣṭa eva akhilo guṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, of an entity that has been seen, every property has been seen;

children.text: 02704 bhrānter niścīyate na iti sādhanaṃ sampravartate //45//
children.translated_text: but [since] due to error it is not ascertained, proof is set in motion. //45//

Even for an entity whose entire reality has been seen, if another property is not conjoined through a cause of error that opposes certainty—as [in the case of] the appearance of silver in a shell. For in the shell there are not two forms, one common and one distinguished, because of the unwanted consequence of such cognition. Or in the case of non-cognition, because the duality-alternative is impossible due to discrimination. And because of over-extension. Therefore, one who sees the form of the shell sees only the distinguished [form]. But due to the deficiency of the cognition of certainty, while not ascertaining [the specific form], one thinks 'I see that generality.' From that comes the superimposition of silver. Likewise, due to the superimposition of that nature upon something whose manifold nature is unnoticed because of the arising of similar and dissimilar [instances], there is persistent error. However many other-natures it has, that many superimpositions arise from their respective causes—therefore the <s>pramāṇas</s> that exclude them

children.text: 02705 iti saṃgrahaślokaḥ / tasmān na adṛṣṭa-grahaṇāya dṛṣṭe pramāṇa-antara-vṛttiḥ /
02707 vastu-grahe anumānāc ca dharmasya ekasya niścaye /
children.translated_text: And in the ascertainment of a single property through inference in grasping an object,

children.text: 02708 sarva-dharma-graho apohe na ayam doṣaḥ prasajyate //46//
children.translated_text: the grasping of all properties [occurs] through <s>apoha</s> (exclusion)—this fault does not arise. //46//
This is the summary verse. Therefore, the operation of another <s>pramāṇa</s> regarding what has been seen is not for the apprehension of the unseen.

children.text:
02709 na kevalaṃ pratyakṣa-dṛṣṭe pramāṇa-antara-avṛttiḥ kvacit / yadā anumānam
02710 api vastu vidhinā pratyāyayati na vyavaccheda-kṛt tadā eka-
02711 dharma-niścaye tad-avyatirekāt sarva-dharma-niścaya iti pramāṇa-
02712 antara-avṛttiḥ na hi tasmin niścite tadātmā aniścito yuktaḥ /
02713 yadā punar anumānena samāropa-vyavacchedaḥ kriyate tadā na eka-
02714 samāropa-vyavacchedād anya-vyavacchedaḥ kṛto bhavati iti tad-artham
02715 anyat pravartate / nanu na avaśyaṃ viparyāsa-pūrvaka eva apratīta-
02716 niścayo bhavati / yathā akasmād dhūmād agni-pratipattiḥ / na hi
02717 tatra anagni-samāropaḥ sambhāvyate / tan na sarvatra vyavacchedaḥ
02718 kriyate / uktam atra / dharmi-pratipattāv abhedāt sarva-pratipattiḥ /
02719 bhede vā asambaddhasya tatra apratipattir iti / tasmāt
02720 tatra api tad-darśinas tat-svabhāva-aniścayaḥ kutaḥ viparyāsāt / sa
02721 ca taṃ pradeśaṃ tad-viviktena rūpeṇa niścinvann agni-sattā-bhāvanā-
02722 vimuktayā buddhyā katham aviparyasto nāma / tad-ākāra-
02801 samāropa-saṃśaya-rahitaś ca tat-pratipattau na liṅgam anusaret /
children.translated_text: and doubt of that form would not resort to the logical mark for the cognition of that.

children.text: 02802 na ca tasya anvaya-vyatirekayor ādriyeta /
children.translated_text: Nor would he attend to the positive and negative concomitances of that.

children.text: 02803 tasmād apoha-viṣayam iti liṅgaṃ prakīrtitam /
children.translated_text: Therefore the logical mark is declared to have <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) as its domain.

children.text: 02804 anyathā dharmiṇaḥ siddhāv asiddhaṃ kim ataḥ param //47//
children.translated_text: Otherwise, when the <s>dharmin</s> is already established, what further remains unestablished? //47//

Not only does another <s>pramāṇa</s> not operate regarding what is directly perceived. When inference too conveys an object positively and not through exclusion, then in the ascertainment of one property, because of non-difference from that, there would be ascertainment of all properties—thus another <s>pramāṇa</s> would not operate. For when that is ascertained, it is not reasonable that what is of its nature remains unascertained. But when exclusion of superimposition is made through inference, then from the exclusion of one superimposition, the exclusion of another is not achieved—therefore another [<s>pramāṇa</s>] operates for that purpose. [Objection:] But the ascertainment of what is not cognized does not necessarily presuppose error—as in the case of the cognition of fire from unexpected smoke. For there, the superimposition of non-fire is not conceivable. So exclusion is not made everywhere. It has been stated [in reply]: When the <s>dharmin</s> is cognized, due to non-difference, there is cognition of everything. Or, if there is difference, what is unconnected is not cognized there. Therefore, even there, for one who sees that, whence is there non-ascertainment of that nature? From error. And that [person], ascertaining that location with a form distinguished from it, with a cognition free from the cultivation of the existence of fire—how is he called 'non-erroneous'? And one free from the superimposition

children.text: 02805 iti saṃgrahaślokaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the summary verse.

children.text: 02806 kvacid dṛṣṭe api yaj jñānaṃ sāmānya-arthaṃ vikalpakam /
children.translated_text: Even regarding what has been perceived, that cognition which is conceptual, having a universal as its object,

children.text: 02807 asamāropita-anya-aṃśe tan-mātra-apoha-gocaram //48//
children.translated_text: when no other aspect has been superimposed, has as its domain the exclusion of that alone. //48//

children.text:
02808 yad rūpa-ādi-darśana-anantaram aliṅgaṃ niścaya-jñānaṃ bhavati /
02809 tat katham asati samārope bhavad vyavaccheda-viṣayaṃ bhavati /
02810 samāropa-viṣaye tasya abhāvāt / yatra hy asya samāropo yathā
02811 sthiraḥ sātmaka iti vā na tatra bhede niścayo bhavati /
02812 niścaya-āropa-manasor bādhyabādhakabhāvataḥ /
02813 na hi sarvato bhinno dṛṣṭo api bhāvas tathā eva pratyabhijñāyate /
02814 kvacid bhede vyavadhāna-sambhavāt / yathā śukteḥ śuktitve /
02815 yatra tu pratipattur bhrānti-nimittaṃ na asti tatra eva asya tad-darśana-
02816 aviśeṣe api smārto niścayo bhavati / samāropa-niścayayor bādhyabādhakabhāvāt
02817 niścayasya
02818 samāropa-viveke asya pravṛttir iti gamyate //49//
children.translated_text: That non-inferential ascertaining cognition that arises immediately after the perception of color and the like—how does it, without superimposition, have exclusion as its object? Because of its absence with respect to the object of superimposition. For where there is superimposition upon it—such as 'it is permanent' or 'it possesses a self'—there, no ascertainment of difference arises, due to the mutually contradictory nature of ascertainment and superimposition in the mind. For an entity perceived as entirely different is not recognized as such [i.e., as the same]. Because of the possibility of obscuration regarding some particular difference—as in [recognizing] the shell-nature of a shell. But where there is no cause of error for the cognizer, there alone, even without any difference in the perception of that [object], a memorial ascertainment arises, because of the mutually contradictory nature of superimposition and ascertainment. It is understood that the activity of ascertainment is directed toward the discrimination from superimposition. //49//

children.text:
02819 tad-viveka eva ca anyāpohaḥ / tasmāt tad api tan-mātra-apoha-gocaram /
02820 na vastu-svabhāva-niścaya-ātmakam / tathā hi kasyacin niścaye
02821 apy anyasya apratipatti-darśanāt / tat-svabhāva-niścaye ca tasya ayogāt /
02901 yāvanto aṃśa-samāropās tan-nirāse viniścayāḥ /
children.translated_text: As many as are the superimpositions of [different] aspects, so many are the ascertainments in their removal;

children.text: 02902 tāvantā eva śabdāś ca tena te bhinna-gocarāḥ //50//
children.translated_text: and just as many are the words—therefore they have different domains. //50//

And that very discrimination is <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other). Therefore, that [ascertainment] too has as its domain merely the exclusion of that [superimposed property], not the ascertainment of the real nature of the entity. For even when something is ascertained, non-apprehension of another is observed; and in the ascertainment of its [true] nature, that [non-apprehension] would be impossible.

children.text: 02903 anyathā ekena śabdena vyāpta ekatra vastuni /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, if a single entity were pervaded by a single word,

children.text: 02904 buddhyā vā na anya-viṣaya iti paryāyatā bhavet //51//
children.translated_text: or [if] the cognition had no other object, there would be synonymy. //51//

children.text:
02905 ity antaraślokaḥ /
02906 yasya api nānā-upādher dhīr grāhika-arthasya bhedinaḥ /
02907 yo api manyate bhinnā eva upādhayaḥ parasparam āśrayāc ca /
02908 tan-nibandhanāḥ śrutayas tad-ādhāreṣu vartante / tatra eva vā
02909 tad ayam aprasaṅga iti / tasya api /
02910 nānā-upādhy-upakāra-aṅga-śakty-abhinna-ātmano grahe //52//
children.translated_text: This is an intervening verse. Even for one who holds that the cognition apprehends an object differentiated by multiple <s>upādhis</s> (qualifying conditions), who also thinks that the <s>upādhis</s> are indeed distinct from each other and, due to mutual dependence, the verbal testimonies based on them apply to their substrates—or [who thinks] that precisely therein this objection does not arise—even for him:

children.text:
02911 sarvātmanā upakārasya ko bhedakaḥ syād aniścitaḥ /
02912 yady apy upādhayo bhinnā eva śabda-jñāna-antarāṇāṃ nimittam
02913 arthe / sa tu tais tadvān eka eva upalīyate / tasya nānā-upādhīnām
02914 upakāra-āśraya-śakti-svabhāvasya svātmany abhedāt sarvātmanā
02915 grahaṇe ka eva upādhi-bhedo aniścitaḥ syāt / sarva-upādhy-upakārakatvena
02916 grahaṇāt / na hy upakārakatvaṃ anyad eva tasya svarūpeṇa
02917 gṛhyamāṇasya agṛhītaṃ nāma / ato yad eva asya svabhāvena
02918 grahaṇaṃ tad eva upakāratvena api iti /
children.translated_text: is also its grasping as beneficial.

children.text: 02919 tayor ātmani sambandhād eka-jñāne dvaya-grahaḥ //53//
children.translated_text: Because of the connection of both in [that one] nature, both are grasped in a single cognition. //53//

When what is undifferentiated in its nature—[being] the capacity, the component, the benefit, and the various <s>upādhis</s>—is grasped in its entirety, what distinguishing factor [of <s>upādhis</s>] would remain unascertained? Even though the <s>upādhis</s> are indeed distinct, they are the cause of different words and cognitions regarding the object. But that [object] is apprehended as one, possessing those [<s>upādhis</s>]. Since the nature of the capacity that serves as the basis of benefit for the various <s>upādhis</s> is undifferentiated in its own self, when grasped in its entirety, what distinction of <s>upādhis</s> would remain unascertained—since it is grasped as beneficial to all <s>upādhis</s>? For the beneficialness is not something ungrasped, separate from it, when it is grasped in its own form. Therefore, its very grasping by [its own] nature

children.text:
02920 ātmabhūtasya upādhi-tadvator upakāryopakārakabhāvasya grahaṇāt
02921 eka-jñāne dvayor api grahaṇam iti eka-upādhi-viśiṣṭe api tasmin
02922 gṛhyamāṇe sarva-upādhīnāṃ grahaṇam / tad-grahaṇa- nāntarīyakatvād
02923 upādhimad-grahaṇasya / anyathā tathā api na gṛhyeta /
02924 na hy anya eva anya-upakārako yo na gṛhītaḥ syāt / na ca apy upakārake
02925 tathā gṛhīte upakārya-agrahaṇaṃ tasya apy agrahaṇa-prasaṅgāt /
02926 svasvāmitva-vat / tasmād artha-antara-upādhi-vāde api samānaḥ prasaṅgaḥ /
02927 atha api syād bhinnā eva śaktayaḥ śaktimato yābhir upādhīn
02928 upakaroti / tato na ayaṃ prasaṅga iti /
03001 dharma-upakāra-śaktīnāṃ bhede tās tasya kiṃ yadi /
children.translated_text: if the capacities for benefiting the properties are different, what [relation do] they [have] to it?

children.text: 03002 na upakāras tatas tāsāṃ tathā syād anavasthitiḥ //54//
children.translated_text: If there is no benefit from them, then for those [capacities] there would be an infinite regress. //54//

Because the relationship of benefited and benefactor, which is essential to the <s>upādhi</s> and the <s>upādhi</s>-possessor, is grasped, both are grasped in a single cognition. Thus, even when that [object] qualified by a single <s>upādhi</s> is grasped, all <s>upādhis</s> are grasped—because the grasping of the <s>upādhi</s>-possessor necessarily entails the grasping of those [<s>upādhis</s>]. Otherwise, it would not be grasped even so. For it is not the case that a benefactor is something other [than the benefited], such that it would not be grasped. Nor, when the benefactor is thus grasped, is there non-grasping of the benefited—for otherwise there would be the absurd consequence of its [i.e., the benefited's] non-grasping as well, like the relationship of owner and owned. Therefore, even on the view that <s>upādhis</s> are separate entities, the same consequence follows. Even if one might say that the capacities by which [the object] benefits the <s>upādhis</s> are indeed distinct from the capacity-possessor, and therefore this consequence does not arise—

children.text:
03003 yadi pratyupādhy upakārakatvāni tasya na svātmabhūtāny eva
03004 na api tata upakāram anubhavanti / kiṃ tasya iti tā ucyante / upakāre
03005 vā svātmabhūtābhir ayam ekaḥ śaktibhiḥ śaktīr upakurvan
03006 eka upādhinā api gṛhyamāṇaḥ sarvātmanā gṛhyata eva / tathā
03007 hi / eka-upādhi-grahaṇe tad-upakāriṇyāḥ śakter grahaṇam / tad-grahaṇe
03008 tad-upakārī bhāvaḥ svātmabhūta-sakala-śakty-upakāro gṛhītaḥ
03009 sarvāḥ śaktīr grāhayati tāś ca sva-upādhīn iti tad-avasthaḥ
03010 prasaṅgaḥ / atha tā api śakty-upakāriṇyaḥ śaktayo bhinnā eva
03011 bhāvāt / evam upādhīnāṃ tac-śaktīnāṃ ca aparā parāsv eva śaktiṣv
03012 aparyavasānena ghaṭanāt sa ekas tābhiḥ kadācid apy agṛhītas
03013 tad-upakāra-ātmā tadvattvena na gṛhyate / yadi punaḥ kevalān
03014 eva upādhīn śabda-jñānāny upalīyeran / tadā tasya asamāveṣān na
03015 bhavati tat-pratipatti-mukhena sarva-pratipattiḥ / tadā api tasya
03016 śabdair anākṣepān na syāt tatra pravṛttir iti vyarthaḥ śabda-prayogaḥ
03017 syāt / arthakriyā-āśrayo hi sarvo vidhi-pratiṣedhābhyāṃ vyavahāraḥ
03018 upādhayaś ca tatra asamarthāḥ samarthaś ca na eva ucyata
03019 iti kiṃ śabda-prayogaiḥ / tataś ca upādhayo na upādhayaḥ syuḥ /
03020 kvacit pravṛttau hi kasyacit pradhānasya aṅga-bhāvāt tad-apekṣayā
03021 tathā ucyate / tasya śabdair anākṣepān na te kasyacid aṅga-
03022 bhūtā iti kim upādhayaḥ / lakṣita-lakṣaṇād adoṣa iti cet samānaḥ
03023 prasaṅgaḥ / sa tāvat tair upādhibhir nāntarīyakatayā upalakṣyamāṇa
03024 ekena apy upalakṣaṇe sarvātmanā upalakṣita iti tad-avasthaḥ
03025 prasaṅgaḥ / ko hy atra viśeṣaḥ śabdā vā enam upalakṣayeyus tal-lakṣitā
03101 vā upādhayaḥ / sa tāvat tadānīṃ niścīyate sarva-upakārakaḥ
03102 iti na kiṃcid etat / tasmād /
03103 eka-upakārake grāhye na upakāras tato apare /
children.translated_text: When a single benefactor is to be grasped, there is no further benefit from others;

children.text: 03104 dṛṣṭe tasminn adṛṣṭā ye tad-grahe sakala-grahaḥ //55//
children.translated_text: those not seen when that [one] is seen—in grasping it, all are grasped. //55//

If the capacities for benefiting each <s>upādhi</s> are not essential to it, nor do they derive benefit from it—then in what sense are they called 'its'? Or, if this one [entity], with capacities essential to itself, benefits the capacities through [those] capacities, then even when grasped by a single <s>upādhi</s>, it is grasped in its entirety. For when a single <s>upādhi</s> is grasped, the capacity that benefits it is grasped; when that is grasped, the entity that benefits it—[which] benefits all capacities that are essential to itself—is grasped, causing all capacities to be grasped, and those [capacities cause] their own <s>upādhis</s> [to be grasped]—thus the same consequence [remains]. Or, if the capacities that benefit the capacities are themselves also distinct from the entity—then, since there is no termination in the <s>upādhis</s> and their capacities [requiring] yet further capacities for each other, that one [entity] is never grasped through those [capacities] as having the nature of benefiting them, and hence is not grasped as possessing them. If, however, words and cognitions were to apprehend only the <s>upādhis</s> alone, then since that [entity] is not included [in them], there would be no apprehension of everything through the apprehension of that. Even then, since that [entity] is not indicated by words, there would be no activity [directed] toward it—so the use of words would be pointless. For all conventional usage, whether prescriptive or prohibitive, is based on efficacious action, and the <s>upādhis</s> are incapable of that, while the capable [entity] is never spoken of—so what is the point of using words? And thus the <s>upādhis</s> would not be <s>upādhis</s> [at all]. For it is because something principal requires another as an ancillary component in some activity that [the latter] is called such in relation to [the former]. Since that [entity] is not indicated by words, they [the <s>upādhis</s>] are not ancillary to anything—so how are they <s>upādhis</s>? If [one says] there is no fault because of the indicated-indicator [relation]—the same consequence [applies]. For that [entity], being necessarily indicated by those <s>upādhis</s>, when indicated by even one indicator, is indicated in its entirety—thus the same consequence. For what difference is there [whether] words indicate it or <s>upādhis</s> indicated by them [indicate it]? That [entity] is then ascertained as benefiting all [<s>upādhis</s>]—so this [objection] amounts to nothing. Therefore:

children.text:
03105 iti saṃgrahaślokaḥ /
03106 yadi bhrānti-nivṛtty-arthaṃ gṛhīte apy anyad iṣyate /
03107 syād etat nirbhāgasya vastuno grahaṇe ko anyas tadā na gṛhīto
03108 nāma / sa tu bhrāntyā na avadhāryata iti pramāṇa-antaraṃ pravartate /
03109 yady evam /
children.translated_text: If so—

children.text: 03110 tad vyavaccheda-viṣayaṃ siddhaṃ tadvat tato aparam //56//
children.translated_text: that [other <s>pramāṇa</s>] has exclusion as its object—established; likewise another [<s>pramāṇa</s>] from that. //56//

This is a summarizing verse. If, even when [the object] is grasped, something else is desired for the purpose of removing error—this might work. But when an entity without parts is grasped, what else would then remain ungrasped? That [aspect], however, is not ascertained due to error—so another <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) operates.

children.text:
03111 asamāropa-viṣaye vṛtter /
03112 tat tarhi bhrānti-nivṛtty-arthaṃ pravṛttaṃ pramāṇam / anya-samāropa-
03113 vyavaccheda-phalam iti siddham anyāpoha-viṣayam / tadvat
03114 anyad api / asamāropa-viṣaye vṛtteḥ / yatra asya samāropo na tatra
03115 niścaya iti samāropa-abhāve vartamāno anyāpoha-viṣayaḥ siddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: is no ascertainment—hence [a <s>pramāṇa</s>] operating in the absence of superimposition is established as having <s>anyāpoha</s> as its object.

children.text: 03116 api ca niścayaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, by ascertainments—

children.text: 03117 yan na niścīyate rūpaṃ tat teṣāṃ viṣayaḥ katham //57//
children.translated_text: that form which is not ascertained—how can that be their object? //57//

Because it operates in the domain of non-superimposition. That <s>pramāṇa</s> then, having arisen for the purpose of removing error, has as its result the exclusion of the superimposition of something else—thus it is established as having <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other) as its object. Likewise another [<s>pramāṇa</s>] too. Because it operates in the domain of non-superimposition. Where there is superimposition upon it, there

children.text:
03118 iyam eva khalu niścayānāṃ svārtha-pratipattir yat tan-niścayanam /
03119 tac ced ākāra-antara-vad aniścitaṃ kathaṃ tair gṛhītaṃ /
03120 katham idānīm aniścīyamānaṃ pratyakṣeṇa api gṛhītaṃ nāma /
03121 na pratyakṣaṃ kasyacin niścāyakam / tad ayam api gṛhṇāti tan
03122 na niścayena / kiṃ tarhi / tat-pratibhāsena / tan na niścaya-aniścaya-
03123 vaśāt pratyakṣasya grahaṇa-agrahaṇe / na evaṃ niścayānāṃ kiṃcin
03124 niścinvato apy anyatra aniścayena pravṛtti-bhedād grahaṇa -agrahaṇam /
03125 tasmāt tad eva asya grahaṇaṃ yo niścayaḥ / anyathā eka-ākāre
03126 api tan na syāt / kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ sarvato bhinne vastu-rūpe
03127 anubhava-utpattāv api tathā eva na smārto niścayo bhavati / sahakāri-
03128 vaikalyāt tataś ca /
children.translated_text: from that—

children.text: 03201 pratyakṣeṇa gṛhīte api viśeṣe aṃśa-vivarjite /
children.translated_text: even when a particular devoid of [differentiated] aspects is grasped by perception,

children.text: 03202 yad viśeṣa-avasāye asti pratyakṣaḥ sa pratīyate //58//
children.translated_text: only that which is perceptible through the determination of a [specific] particular is cognized. //58//

This indeed is the apprehension of their own object by ascertainments—namely, the ascertaining of that. If that [form] is unascertained, like some other aspect, how is it grasped by them? How then is what is unascertained grasped even by perception? Perception is not the ascertainer of anything. It too grasps that—but not through ascertainment. Rather, through the appearance of that [in consciousness]. Therefore, the grasping and non-grasping by perception is not due to ascertainment or non-ascertainment. Not so for ascertainments: since even while ascertaining something, there is non-ascertainment elsewhere, and from [that] difference of activity comes grasping and non-grasping. Therefore, only that ascertainment is its grasping. Otherwise, even in a single aspect, that [grasping] would not occur. But what is the reason that, even when an experience arises of the real form [of things] which is entirely unique, a memorial ascertainment does not arise in exactly that way? Because of the deficiency of co-operative conditions. And therefore—

children.text:
03203 yady apy aṃśa-rahitaḥ sarvato bhinna-svabhāvo bhāvo anubhūtas
03204 tathā api na sarva-bhedeṣu tāvatā niścayo bhavati / kāraṇa-antara-

children.translated_text: both words and ascertainments follow convention (<s>saṃketa</s>). //59//

Even though an entity whose nature is entirely unique has been experienced, ascertainment does not arise with respect to all differences merely from that—because it depends on other conditions. For experience generates ascertaining cognitions in accordance with the practice of non-conceptual [habituation]—just as, even without any difference in the perception of form, there arise the concepts of 'corpse,' 'woman,' 'food.' Therein, sharpness of intellect, the habituation of impressions, context, and so forth are the co-operative conditions for the arising of the ascertainment of difference from experience. And due to the differences in proximity, degree, and so on among those very [conditions], there is sequence. Just as, even when there is no difference between being a father and being a teacher, upon seeing the father approaching, [the thought arises:] 'my father is coming,' not 'the teacher.' And that ascertainment, being such, arises [only] when there is no cause of error. Therefore, the ascertainment of all aspects does not [arise merely] because they are not unreal.

And thus there would be the absence of exclusion. Therefore, the exclusion itself is the excluded. But the difference in verbal apprehension is due to the difference in convention. There is no difference in what is denoted. But surely, if there is no difference in what is denoted, even the difference in convention would be improper, since one designation [would suffice] for both. And thus the use of a separative case-ending would be improper, since it

For words do not have any activity dependent on the nature of their object—since [if so,] there would be the absurd consequence of no activity from volition. They illuminate that meaning through restriction, being employed as one wishes to use them, whether for the separated or the unseparated. Therefore, even when 'cow' and 'cowness' designate a single object, when a difference of convention is made for the purpose of conveying some particular [aspect], the separative case-ending, [seemingly] showing a distinct object, appears as if [indicating] a different entity—even though there is no different entity—due to the habituation of seeing such usage. But from that much alone, there is no difference everywhere—because, even elsewhere, there is no restriction for what operates under human volition. Just as one thing is proclaimed in some [context] with the singular number, even without any difference, it is [expressed] with the plural for the purpose of proclaiming importance and the like. But if there is no purpose, there would be no difference in convention. That too indeed exists. For—

But when, without expectation of further exclusion, he wishes to know that [same exclusion], then, without abandoning the further exclusion, for the purpose of not manifesting [it] in that very exclusion from horse, they employ [the expression] "this is a non-horse." For precisely this reason, since in the former case other distinctions are already negated by the function of the word, there is neither co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) nor the qualifier-qualified relation—as in "its cow-ness is white." Because the cognition, which is the basis of that alone, does not appear as one with the distinguishing feature of that alone, and because there is no expectation [of further specification]. Therefore, there is no difference whatsoever in the denoted object of words expressing property and property-bearer, in terms of being the object of a cognition of certainty. One [word], conveying that very [thing] with other distinctions already negated, conveys [it]; the other [conveys it] through negation—this is the [only] difference. "Wishing to make known that meaning, whether by a <s>taddhita</s> (secondary derivative suffix) or a <s>kṛt</s> (primary derivative suffix), or by another [expression]—if one speaks, there is no further difference." //63// And showing just this much difference, one might show it by a <s>taddhita</s> as "cooking-ness" (<s>pācakatva</s>), or by a <s>kṛt</s> as "cooking" (<s>pāka</s>), or by another [word] with a convention made by oneself for making known what is of that nature. But merely by such expression, the thing does not become something different, because the word's convention is made for making known what is of precisely that nature. [Objection:] But "cooking-ness" expresses a relation, not just cooking itself. [Reply:] Surely no "cooker" different from cooking itself is denoted, of the kind being described. And what is denoted by it has been stated—that very thing is [denoted] also by "cooking-ness"—enough with groundless false conceptualizations!

children.translated_text: For those whose words are governed by reality and do not depend on the speaker's intention—

children.text: 03519 ṣaṣṭhī-vacana-bheda-ādi-codyaṃ tān prati yuktimat //65//
children.translated_text: the objection regarding genitive case, number differences, and the like is reasonable against them. //65//

What they say—"Even in the exclusion of the other as the meaning of words, since what is qualified by that is denoted, all the absurd consequences raised against the 'possessor-of-that' position are equally [applicable]"—that too is refuted by this. For there, a sound operating in something else by taking up a separate entity is afflicted with faults such as lack of independence. But exclusion from another is not a separate entity—since two [things are denoted] by a single expression of what is excluded, as stated. How then, since what is excluded, being one, does not follow another, is the exclusion from another a universal? Because it so appears in that cognition. For there is no universal whatsoever [as a real entity]. Cognition, depending on words, arises through the power of beginningless latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), conjoining even properties that are not [actually] conjoined. By the force of its appearance, the universal and co-reference are established, even though the object is unreal—because there is no conjunction or difference among real objects. All of those [objects], differing from others through being causes and effects of that [cognition], and the sound that is their support, function through the removal of the undesired—thus it is called the domain of exclusion of the other. There, without regard to external reality, by the force of the appearance in cognition, one [thing] excluded from many is made the object of words, by conceptual constructions (<s>vikalpa</s>) born from the awakening of latent impressions deposited by experience of those [things], which ascertain the nature of those objects. And in precisely that [domain], this convention of property and property-bearer, which cannot be described as either identical or different from each other, is extended. For the property is not different from the property-bearer, since no separate entity is denoted; nor is it the same—because even property-denoting [words], like substance-denoting ones, would absurdly imply negation of further exclusion. And since [even so] they convey what is intended, there is no [need for] making a different convention. This is the inexpressibility of property and property-bearer in the meaning of words. But in [external] reality, in the unique particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), the general characteristic is inexpressible because of its non-existence. [Objection:] But if property and property-bearer are not different—or if they are different—the genitive and other case-endings that are observed, and the difference of number [singular/plural] observed due to the multiplicity of properties would not apply to the property-bearer. [Reply:] It has been stated here that words lack independence [in their operation]. Moreover—

For even the [convention] that the genitive [is used] for exclusion, [and] the <s>jas</s> and other [suffixes] for plurality—this too has not arisen by itself through the mere proximity of real objects, independent of the speaker's intention. Rather, they employ [words] in that way there, and from that arises such understanding. Likewise elsewhere too, employed by them in whatever manner, they become causes of understanding in just that way. The investigation of the operation of words—which, in their denotata, have functions dependent on persons, which display what is not a [real] entity, and which are causes of conceptual awakening according to habituation—and the establishment of reality solely by their force, is merely a proclamation of stupidity. Words are conventionally established regarding property, property-bearer, and the like—but that [this] is due to a real difference in exclusion—whence is this? Because such usage would be impossible. For we shall explain that when property and property-bearer are different, or when they are of the nature of reality, universals, their connection, co-reference, and the qualifier-qualified relation are not tenable, nor can words function according to reality. children.translated_text: When even a single woman is [called] "wives" (<s>dārāḥ</s>) and even a single grain-substance is [called] "sand" (<s>sikatā</s>)—what plurality is there by which this occurs? If [it is said] "a difference in capacity"—then the singular number would now be abolished everywhere, since there is no single capacity [anywhere]. And effort [to explain it] would be futile. If [it is said] "the singular is [used] elsewhere because of no difference in the real object"—let it be so here too! This convention, devoid of real basis, being made [thus] declares the independence of intention in the use of words. And in "the six cities" (<s>ṣaṇṇagarī</s>)—how is the singular [used] for many? For the cities themselves are not some single thing. Whence their aggregate? Since no [single] entity is constituted from heterogeneous things like palaces, persons, and the like—whence is their aggregate a substance? And they are not in contact—there is no contact, since a palace, being itself of the nature of contact, has no contact with another. From that very [reason], there is no number [applicable to it]. If [it is said] "a city is an existence qualified by contact-with-persons of that [kind]"—what is the qualifier of this unsurpassable [existence]? And since existence is one, even when cities are many, there would be no plural "cities." If [it is said] "the mutual togetherness of two [things]"—what kind of being-together is there for what is not benefited by what benefits? And since persons, contact, and existence are many, how is "city" in the singular? If [it is said] "those of that nature have somewhere an undivided capacity regarding some object, and that is the ground"—no, because capacity does not differ from the nature of the real object; or if it does differ, [then] what is not assisted cannot be made dependent; or if it is assisted, since the capacity of the capacity-assister would also be different, there would be infinite regress and incomprehension; or if it is not different [from the original capacity], the same absurd consequence would apply to the first [case] too—so all this is pointless. In "the nature of space is space-ness"—the genitive, which depends on exclusion, would not apply. For there is no universal there, nor are qualities such as pervasiveness and the like spoken of in that way—because a separate entity cannot be the nature of that [space], and because they would absurdly lack any nature of their own. And if that [nature] too had the nature of a separate entity, there would be over-extension. And thus there would be incomprehension. Likewise, the group of six categories (<s>padārthas</s>) and the like should also be addressed. For no universal, number, or contact is possible there. How then, in the absence of any distinguishing [real] property, is it "the nature of space" and not simply "space"? When, without considering the form that is common to other objects, one wishes to know the form that is the basis of the operation of the word "space," it is said thus. [Objection:] But the expression of a form excluded from everything is not possible. [Reply:] Indeed, that very form is not delivered to the cognition—for there would be the absurd consequence of [it being] beyond the senses. Rather, one who [thinks] "I shall make known what is of that nature" delivers through the word to the listener a reflection in conceptual thought (<s>vikalpa-pratibimba</s>), whose intrinsic nature is not conjoined [with the real thing]. As he said: "In regard to an unseen object, [there is] merely a conceptual image of the object." Thus the unique particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is neither cognized nor communicated by what communicates and what is communicated—for even in hearing about heaven and the like, there would absurdly be no difference of appearance from those who [actually] experience it. Therefore, even one who does not cognize the intrinsic nature of the entity, being of precisely such a nature, is satisfied through ascertaining that [nature] in the conceptual reflection. Precisely because of the understanding of the meaning of words being of such a nature, it is said thus: "A word states its own form." But [this is] not because it generates a cognition in which the own form [of the object] appears. How then, in entities whose forms are exclusively excluded [from each other], [can there be] something called a "universal"? Because they are not conjoined, and because nothing else exists. It has been stated what kind of universal [exists] for unconjoined [entities]—the non-conjunction of each [with the others], the sameness of those that differ from it. Moreover— By that cognition which, appearing as a single object, covers over the other forms with its own form—

children.text: 03812 eka-artha-pratibhāsinyā bhāvān āśritya bhedinaḥ //68 //
children.translated_text: resting upon entities that are [in reality] different, [that cognition] appearing as a single object— //68//

children.translated_text: By that [cognition], entities whose manifold meanings are concealed, being [in reality] different themselves through convention,

children.text: 03814 abhedina iva ābhānti bhāvā rūpeṇa kenacit //69//
children.translated_text: appear as if undifferentiated, through some [common] form. //69//

children.text: 03815 tasyā abhiprāya-vaśāt sāmānyaṃ sat prakīrtitam /
children.translated_text: By the force of its intention, the universal is proclaimed as existent;

children.text: 03816 tad asat paramārthena yathā saṃkalpitaṃ tayā //70//
children.translated_text: but it is non-existent in ultimate reality, just as it is imagined by that [cognition]. //70//

children.translated_text:
Indeed, conceptual cognition, arising in dependence upon objects that are mutually exclusive, following the nature of its own latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), conceals the differentiated form of these [objects], superimposes its own undifferentiated appearance, and presents them as conjoined. And the nature of that [cognition]—which treats distinct entities as having a single provable-and-prover relationship, and [the nature] of the latent impression of that conceptual construction—is that from which this [cognition] appears as it does, being born from that. And that is <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional reality)—for by it one's own form is concealed by another's form. And those [objects], whose distinctions are concealed by it, although they are themselves differentiated, appear as if undifferentiated in some respect. Therefore, what is called <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) is [nothing but] the apprehension of a specific aspect of entities that exist [only] as they appear in cognition—as if manifesting externally—by those who conform to their appearance in cognition. How then is <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other) a universal? It is precisely that <s>anyāpoha</s>. The cognition that grasps precisely that [exclusion] appears, due to the natural error of conceptual constructions, as if it were grasping real objects. For that [cognition], arising only in entities that are distinct from what is other than them, is understood to have distinction as its domain. [Objection:] But the external [objects] are the distinct ones, and conceptual construction does not operate upon them—so how does it arise in them? It is the analysts who discriminate thus, not the ordinary practitioners. The latter, considering their own mental object to be capable of effective action, identify the perceived and the conceptualized objects and proceed [on that basis]. It is said thus in accordance with their intention—because, having been produced by those [real objects], they convey by words [things] as distinct from those that do not produce that [cognition]. But those who inquire into reality do not accept non-difference from the differences of appearance and so forth.
If [one says] the intention of the cognizer is being followed, then even <s>anyāpoha</s> should not be a universal—for cognition is not like that. Indeed, it is not merely this that is not cognized—cognition does not arise even with the aspects of being separate from, or non-separate from, or one with, or permanent in, or pervading the individuals, and so forth. Rather, a cognition of undifferentiated aspect simply arises. What is the basis of that [cognition]? <s>Anyāpoha</s> is stated [as the answer], because of its existence in real things, because of non-contradiction, and because conventional practice, which depends on words, is observed to be thus. But there is no real entity called 'universal' corresponding to how this cognition appears. Because:

The individuals do not follow another, and what follows [them all] does not appear. //
For these individuals do not enter into one another. In the absence of difference, there would be the unwanted consequence of the absence of the universal itself. And nothing else, distinct from them, appears as such in cognition—and how could what does not appear cause another to grasp it by its own nature, or designate it? And [the claim that] what is one and connected with them is itself the universal—this has been rejected because of over-extension.
[Objection:] One universal is the cause of undifferentiated designation and cognition, not everything. [Reply:] How can there be the occurrence of cognition regarding one [thing] from another? [If one says] from its connection with that—then there would be the same unwanted consequence regarding number, effects, substances, and so forth. [If one says] not so, because they are not of the nature of universals—but that is precisely what is being investigated: what is this nature of a universal? [If one says] that where there is a connection, there is the occurrence of cognition, and from that [comes] the universal—this is [merely] stated here. Since the cause [of such cognition] is possible from multiple connections such as effects, substances, and so forth, the occurrence of cognition [arises] from those, and hence [they too would have] the nature of universals. Otherwise, [such cognition] should not arise elsewhere either, because there is no distinguishing [feature]. And thus there would be a confusion of the forms of substance-universals and quality-universals. [Objection:] Then the appearance of cognition itself, being of the nature of knowledge, exists as the universal. [Reply:] No, because:

How could what is non-different from cognition become a different object? //71//
How can the form of cognition be the universal of objects? Because of its non-existence in them. [If one says] because there is the determination of being of that nature, and conventional practice [proceeds] through such error—then what is the basis for the arising of such cognition there? And if it has no basis, it would arise everywhere. Or, how could what is non-different from one cognition be the form of another cognition, [namely] one arising in [connection with] another individual? And thus, not pervading another cognition or another individual, how could it be a universal?
Therefore, this conceptual construction is erroneous—the grasping of identity in objects.
