children.translated_text: the distinction of <s>dharma</s> (property) and <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) are not contradicted as they are cognized. Even when there is the possibility of multiple object-distinctions,

children.text: 04414 dharma-pratibhāsa-bhedais tat-svabhāva-pratipattaye kriyata iti /
children.translated_text: in the investigation of the establishment and negation of a single distinction of that, that very real thing, having been prompted by the word '<s>dharma</s>' with the exclusion of other distinctions, because cognition reflects it in that way,

children.text: 04415 tat-svabhāva-grahaṇāt yā dhīs tad-arthā iva apy anarthikā //
children.translated_text: as if it were a separate property is displayed by establishing its other nature as the <s>dharmin</s> without qualification. And to that extent, because of the difference of <s>dharma</s> and <s>dharmin</s> in that aspect, cognition appears as if possessing difference—not because of a real difference, due to the faults stated above. Through the prompting of such manifold differences,

For if [the universal] were to assist, since there is nothing further to be conferred on what requires no additional qualification, it would produce all its effects at once due to not depending on anything else. Or it would not have the nature of producing that. But the instances (<s>vyaktis</s>), due to the influence of time, place, and conditioning, have differentiated originations and would produce effects as [differentiated] particulars—thus there is no contradiction. Likewise, certain objects too, though having a difference of essential nature, perform the function of a single recognition and so forth; since they differ from those that do not perform that [function], they are said to be 'non-different.' Or many [things] produced by one [cause] are [said to be non-different] due to differing from those not produced by that. But should one understand by this definition of difference that the universal is the same as the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular), or is it something altogether different? What of it? If it is the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, how is it the object of conceptual thought? And if it is something else, how does it perform a causal function? And since impermanence and so forth are cognized in the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, [the universal] does not have that character; and those [impermanence etc.] have the nature of being non-real entities. This is not a fault. The conventional usages of universal, co-reference, property and property-bearer [apply to] the object as it appears in cognition. That conceptual cognition which arises depending on the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) deposited by the experience of grasping the nature of the real thing—though not having that [real thing] as its object, it is as if having it as its object, because its nature originates from the <s>vāsanā</s> deposited by that experience, because its form is one in which that nature is determined through superimposition, because it arises from entities that produce undifferentiated effects and thus grasps as if grasping an undifferentiated object, having a form that in ultimate reality is the same as the distinction from what is other than that—in that [cognition], the object-form that appears as if external, as if one, as if capable of causal function though not [actually] performing it, [appears so] because of the determination and engagement of those who engage in conventional practice, because engagement would be impossible otherwise—because it appears as performing causal function, [it appears] as if different from those that do not perform it—but that is not the reality, because examination is irrelevant—this we shall demonstrate. Those objects, being located in cognition, are grasped as identical with that [cognition] because they appear as excluded from something; not the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, because it does not appear there. And those very [objects], excluded from something, again appear as possessing exclusion from something else and as undifferentiated—thus, even though they do not exist in themselves, because cognition presents them in that way, the conventional usage of universal, co-reference, and so forth is applied to what is a false object. And all this distortion is produced by the <s>vāsanās</s> deposited by the perception of <s>svalakṣaṇas</s> alone—therefore, for conceptual cognitions whose origination is bound to those [<s>svalakṣaṇas</s>], even though they do not reflect that [reality], there is non-deception regarding the real thing—like the error of [seeing] a gem in the light of a gem—but not for others, even though both arise from the difference of that [reality], just as the grasping of some generality while abandoning the pursuit of unperceived particulars leads to the superimposition of other particulars—like the cognition of a gem in the light of a lamp. Therefore, there is no causal efficacy in the objects that are the domain of conceptual cognition. Nor is there an absence of impermanence and so forth in the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>. For impermanence is nothing other than a momentary real thing. Because that [thing], having the property of being present for [only] a moment, is grasped as being of such a nature—thus it is 'this is impermanent' or 'impermanence belongs to this.' Conceptual cognitions, entering into precisely that property, display the exclusions from various single and multiple properties. And they are not without a basis, because they are based on the perception of that difference. Nor do they have the nature of non-real entities, because it is precisely that nature which is thus cognized. But the grasping of a real thing as excluded from the manifold and the singular would be error, because that [thing], producing the effects of one and many, is of such a nature for the sake of manifesting such a nature in investigations of such a nature—not because of a real difference. Because a single thing cannot reasonably be many, and many things cannot reasonably be one, and what is distinct [from both] is negated. Because of the difference in the nature of those [cognitions], if word-meanings are accepted as corresponding to reality, co-reference would be impossible. If [one says] that because of the <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition) of that, a single [thing] is expressed by two [words], there is no fault—[we reply:] since what does not assist [in producing the effect] cannot reasonably be dependent [on another], there is no <s>upādhi</s>. And if there is dependence, since the producer and the produced do not co-exist, both cannot be expressed. If one of them is mentally supplied by the intellect, the word would not have a real object. And if [the word] has as its object what appears in cognition, let everything be just so. Likewise, since [the thing] with a different <s>upādhi</s> does not appear when grasping one from here [alone]. If [one says that] because the conditioned and the conditioning <s>upādhi</s> co-exist, there is no fault—no, because what is already produced has no dependence [on another], it has no <s>upādhi</s>. And an unproduced [entity] has no established nature. Since dependence is in every way non-existent, having made it an imposition of conceptual construction, why does not cognition in conventional usage conform entirely to that very [construction] alone? Because when made the object through a single word-<s>pramāṇa</s>, the force of reality would entail everything, and the purposelessness of other [words] would follow. Because what appears in cognition has no real basis, faults that do not arise from the power of the real thing are not applicable. Therefore, that [cognition], undifferentiated [in one respect], even when making a single form its object, since the other forms are unascertained, being grasped by a cognition that desires another form—even when different word-meanings are brought together, it appears in cognition as undifferentiated—thus universal, qualifier-qualified relation, co-reference, and

children.text: 04416 vikalpikā atat-kārya-artha-bheda-niṣṭhā prajāyate //76//
children.translated_text: the differentiation of statements and the differentiation of what is to be proved and the means of proof are made through the differences of property-appearances that have their basis in that nature, for the cognition of that nature. //

children.text: 04417 tasyāṃ yad rūpam ābhāti bāhyam ekam iva anyataḥ /
children.translated_text: From the grasping of that nature, the cognition that arises, though as if having that as its object, is without [real] object; //

children.text: 04418 vyāvṛttam iva nistattvaṃ parīkṣā-anaṅga-bhāvataḥ //77//
children.translated_text: being conceptual, it is established in the distinction of objects that are the effects of what is not that—the form that appears in it as if external, as if one, as if excluded from something else, is without reality, because examination is irrelevant. //77//

children.text: 04419 arthā jñāna-niviṣṭās te yato vyāvṛtti-rūpiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those objects, situated in cognition, have the form of exclusion;

children.text: 04420 tena abhinnā iva ābhānti vyāvṛttāḥ punar anyataḥ //78//
children.translated_text: therefore they appear as if undifferentiated, [yet] excluded from something else. //78//

children.text: 04421 ta eva teṣāṃ sāmānya-samāna-ādhāra-gocaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those very [objects], through cognitions and designations whose domain is universal, co-reference, and so forth—

children.text: 04422 jñāna-abhidhānair mithyā-artho vyavahāraḥ pratanyate //79//
children.translated_text: the conventional usage, having a false object, is extended. //79//

children.text: 04423 sa ca sarvaḥ padārthānām anyonya-abhāva-saṃśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: And all that [conventional usage] is based on the mutual absence of entities;

children.text: 04424 tena anyāpoha-viṣayo vastu-lābhasya ca āśrayaḥ //80//
children.translated_text: therefore it has the exclusion of others (<s>anyāpoha</s>) as its domain, and is the basis for obtaining real things. //80//

children.text: 04425 yatra asti vastu-sambandho yathokta-anumitau yathā /
children.translated_text: Where there is a connection with reality, as in inference as described—

children.text: 04426 na anyatra bhrānti-sāmye api dīpa-tejo maṇau yathā //81//
children.translated_text: but not elsewhere, even though the error is similar—like the light of a lamp [mistaken for] a gem. //81//

children.text: 04427 tatra eka-kāryo aneko api tad-akārya-anyatā-āśrayaiḥ /
children.translated_text: There, even though many [things] produce a single effect, through [properties] that serve as the basis for being other than what does not produce that effect,

children.text: 04501 ekatvena abhidhā-jñānair vyavahāraṃ pratāryate //82//
children.translated_text: conventional practice is carried out through designations and cognitions [that present them] as one. //82//

children.text: 04502 tathā aneka-kṛd eko api tad-bhāva-paridīpane /
children.translated_text: Likewise, even one [thing] that produces many [effects], for the illumination of that nature,

children.text: 04503 atat-kārya-artha-bhedena nānā-dharma-pratīyate //83//
children.translated_text: is cognized as having many properties through the distinction of objects that are the effects of what is not that. //83//

children.text: 04504 yathā-pratīti-kathitaḥ śabda-artho asāv asann api /
children.translated_text: The meaning of words, described as it is cognized, even though non-existent,

children.text: 04505 sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ ca vastuny asya na sambhavaḥ //84//
children.translated_text: and co-reference—their occurrence in a real thing is impossible. //84//

children.text: 04506 dharma-dharmi-vyavasthānaṃ bhedo abhedaś ca yādṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The establishment of <s>dharma</s> and <s>dharmin</s>, difference and non-difference, of whatever kind—

children.text: 04507 asamīkṣita-tattva-artho yathā loke pratīyate //85//
children.translated_text: is cognized in the world as one whose true meaning is unexamined. //85//

children.text: 04508 taṃ tathā eva samāśritya sādhya-sādhana-saṃsthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Relying on that in just that way, the arrangement of what is to be proved and the means of proof

children.text: 04509 paramārtha-avatārāya vidvadbhir avakalpyate //86//
children.translated_text: is devised by the learned for the sake of arriving at ultimate reality. //86//

children.text: 04510 saṃsṛjyante na bhidyate svato arthāḥ pāramārthikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Real things are not mixed nor divided of themselves;

children.text: 04511 rūpam ekam anekaṃ ca teṣu buddher upaplavaḥ //87//
children.translated_text: the [perception of] one form and many forms in them is the distortion of cognition. //87//

children.text: 04512 bhedas tato ayaṃ bauddhe arthe sāmānyaṃ bheda ity api /
children.translated_text: Therefore this difference exists in the object as cognized; 'universal' and 'difference' too [are such];

children.text: 04513 tasya eva ca anyavyāvṛttyā dharma-bhedaḥ prakalpyate //88//
children.translated_text: and property-difference is postulated for that very [entity] through its exclusion from others. //88//

children.text: 04514 sādhya-sādhana-saṃkalpe vastu-darśana-hānitaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the conception of what is to be proved and the means of proof, due to the loss of perception of the real thing,

children.text: 04515 bhedaḥ sāmānya-saṃsṛṣṭo grāhyo na atra svalakṣaṇam //89//
children.translated_text: difference mixed with universality should be grasped—not the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) here. //89//

children.text: 04516 samāna-bhinna-ādy-ākārair na tad grāhyaṃ kathaṃcana /
children.translated_text: That [<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>] cannot be grasped in any way by forms such as 'the same,' 'different,' and so forth,

children.text: 04517 bhedānāṃ bahu-bhedānāṃ tatra ekasminn ayogataḥ //90//
children.translated_text: because the many differences of [many] differences are impossible in that single [entity]. //90//

children.text: 04518 tad-rūpaṃ sarvato bhinnaṃ tathā tat-pratipādikā /
children.translated_text: Its form is completely different from everything; likewise, the verbal expression that conveys it—

children.text: 04519 na śrutiḥ kalpanā vā asti sāmānyena eva vṛttitaḥ //91//
children.translated_text: neither scripture nor conceptual construction [can grasp it], because they operate only through universals. //91//

children.text:
04520 iti saṃgrahaślokāḥ / kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ svalakṣaṇe śabdā na
04521 prayujyante / yasmāt /
04522 śabdāḥ saṃketitaṃ prāhur vyavahārāya sa smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Words express what has been conventionally agreed upon; that [agreement] is recalled for the purpose of conventional practice;

children.text: 04523 tadā svalakṣaṇaṃ na asti saṃketas tena tatra na //92 //
children.translated_text: at that time the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> does not exist; therefore there is no convention regarding it. //92//
These are the summary verses. But what is the reason that words are not applied to <s>svalakṣaṇas</s> (particulars)? Because:

children.text:
04524 na hi śabdā asaṃketitam arthaṃ prakāśayanti / saṃketaś ca
04525 vyavahāra-arthaṃ kriyate api nāma itaḥ śabdāt kṛta-saṃketād
04526 uttara-kālaṃ imam arthaṃ pratipadyeta iti / na ca prākkṛta-sambandhasya
04527 ekatra svalakṣaṇe śabdasya paścād prayogo yuktaḥ /
04528 tasya deśa-kāla-vyakti-bheda-anāskandhanāt / tasmān na svalakṣaṇe
04529 samayaḥ / sāmānyaṃ tarhi vyatiriktam avyatiriktaṃ vā vyāpi
04530 śabdair abhidhīyate / tan na vyavahāra-kāla-abhāva-doṣaḥ / na etad
04531 asti / yasmāt
04532 api pravarteta pumān vijñāya-arthakriyā-kṣamān//
children.translated_text: For words do not illuminate an object that has not been conventionally agreed upon. And convention is made for the purpose of conventional practice: 'May someone, at a future time, understand this object from this word for which a convention has been made.' And the subsequent application of a word whose connection was previously made with a single <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> is not reasonable, because that [<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>] does not persist across differences of place, time, and instance. Therefore there is no convention regarding the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>. Then is it a universal—whether distinct or non-distinct—that is pervasive and is denoted by words? That does not have the fault of absence at the time of conventional usage. This is not so, because:

children.text: 04601 tat sādhanāya ity artheṣu saṃyojyante abhidhāyakāḥ //93//
children.translated_text: A person would engage [in action] only upon knowing [things] as capable of causal function; //

children.translated_text: Surely it is not a misfortune of the world that a person would suffer from neither establishing conventions nor employing words. Rather, every undertaking of his is to be considered as purpose-oriented, since a fruitless undertaking is to be disregarded. Therefore, this person, in employing words for some purpose, is right to seek some result. And all that [result] is characterized by the acquisition and avoidance of the desirable and undesirable. Hence, this person, knowing the means and non-means to the desirable and undesirable, would employ words or heed instruction with the thought: 'I shall engage in or desist from [action], or cause [others] to engage or desist.' Otherwise, [words would be] to be disregarded. Therein, <s>jāti</s> (universal) is incapable of efficacious action. For a <s>jāti</s> nowhere serves for drawing or milking. And there is no use of words in worldly transactions without such a context. If [one says] that since the particular (<s>vyakti</s>) cannot be directly enjoined, the enjoining of the <s>jāti</s> is for the purpose of indicating the indicated—even when a connection exists that is not enjoined by a word, how would [one] act? For no one, when told 'cut the stick,' cuts the stick-bearer. Nor is activity toward the particular [possible merely] from impossibility [of acting on the universal]—for thus [the speaker] would be an incoherent babbler. Nor is activity toward something other [than what is mentioned possible], like the injunction to milk a bull. Nor is indication of one thing by the enjoining of another [thing valid]. For even when a connection exists, there is no apprehension of the stick-bearer from the word 'stick.' If [one says] this is because the connection there is indeterminate—the same [applies] to the <s>jāti</s> too, since when the particulars pass away, the <s>jāti</s> alone remains. Words like 'brother' and the like might imply the related [party] because they are relational words. But expressions like 'cowness' and the like are not relational designators—because there would be the absurd consequence that <s>jātis</s> devoid of particulars would always follow from those expressions. If [one says] it is accepted because the fitness for connection with that is always cognized—then there would always be non-activity from the word 'cow,' since no particular [state]—whether associated or unassociated—is implied. If [one says] there is no fault since the <s>jāti</s> related to the particular is enjoined—then the particular, which always subsists as its qualifier, is already implied, and so the possessor of that [<s>jāti</s>] would be the thing denoted. And there is no mutual connection between <s>jāti</s> and <s>vyakti</s>, since, not being related as generated and generator, they do not benefit each other. Therefore, indication [of particulars through universals] is also improper. Therefore, words are not to be assigned to <s>jāti</s>, because of the absence of [practical] result. If so, then: the possessor of that [<s>jāti</s>] is sufficient for efficacious actions—therefore the word is applied to that. And that [word]—why is it not applied directly? If words are assigned to the particular and that is fruitful—why then is that word not applied directly to the particulars themselves? What need is there for another intermediary? If [one says] because of infinity—this is the same [problem]. //94//

children.translated_text: If [one says] because of the sameness of the fault [that applies to] the possessor of that [<s>jāti</s>]—let there be a <s>jāti</s>, but [let there be] no further [entity]. //95//

One might say: because of the infinity of particulars, a connection with the word cannot be made. This being so, this infinity applies equally to the possessor of the <s>jāti</s>. For even through the <s>jāti</s>, it is the particular that must be spoken of—hence, since what lacks an established connection is not denoted, a connection must necessarily be made with that [particular]. And that [connection] cannot be made [with infinite particulars]. If [one says] because it is made with what is connected to that [<s>jāti</s>], [the connection] with that [particular] too is already made—it has been stated [in response]: even when a connection is made in one case, there is no apprehension in another; nor does a connection exist [there]. Moreover: when those that perform a certain efficacious action are equal to [i.e., undifferentiated from] those that do not perform it, why is [the word] not applied [to them]? One might say: even when the object of a word is that which is excluded from others, since the possessor of the exclusion is what is denoted, there is no difference from the position of the possessor of that [<s>jāti</s>]. For what difference is there here—whether exclusion [stands for] <s>jāti</s>, or the possessor of exclusion [stands for] the possessor of <s>jāti</s>? Let there be the fault of [the position of] the possessor of that [<s>jāti</s>]—but let there not be another <s>jāti</s>. For even one who accepts the <s>jāti</s> must necessarily accept the difference of entities. Because in its absence, there would be the absurd consequence of the absence of that [<s>jāti</s>] too. And that difference from one [entity]—which is the non-difference from others—let there be apprehension of things qualified by that. Since it is impossible to entirely avoid the fault in any case, and since there is no purpose in accepting another entity, since the purpose of that [other entity] is accomplished by another [means], and since that acceptance [of difference] is inevitable in any case.

children.translated_text: of words—so what need have you for another universal? //97//

For this person, in employing a word with regard to objects, also employs it [with the intent] that [the hearer] would act by avoiding the undesirable. When permission to act is granted elsewhere too, the use of that name would be pointless; and since either the permission to act or desist would be disregarded [if a single injunction were sufficient], there would be no speech at all if the exclusion from others is not expressed. Therefore, exclusion must necessarily be conveyed by a word. And that [exclusion] is undifferentiated in what is other than that [object]—so it is also a property of the <s>jāti</s>. Therefore, abandoning the definite acceptance, definite injunction, and establishment of the <s>jāti</s> as the meaning [of words], and imagining another entity, is merely an insistence on [what is] purposeless—because his [the opponent's] hypothesis is unfounded. For it is not the case that exclusion is not made—but those who describe the domain of [practical] activity have called it <s>jāti</s>.

Surely it was said that [the universal] shows the domain of activity—this has been stated. But what was stated is improper. For it has been explained that it [the <s>jāti</s>] is not fit for [practical] activity. The activity through it as an intermediary has also been refuted. And there is an intermediary in the case of enjoining the possessor of the <s>jāti</s>. If the domain of activity [belongs to] both <s>jāti</s> and the possessor of <s>jāti</s>, why are exclusion and the possessor of exclusion not accepted? If [one says] because exclusion, being unreal, cannot be a means—the same [applies] to the <s>jāti</s>. If [one says] there is no fault because of the possessor of <s>jāti</s> being a means—the same applies to the possessor of exclusion. And according to the proponents of exclusion, verbal cognition apprehends what is unreal. That [verbal cognition], due to the influence of error, causes activity even toward what is non-efficacious, by determining it to be efficacious. But correspondence with reality occurs when there is a restriction to the arising of the real [entity]. Otherwise it simply does not exist. If [one says] the arising of reality is non-erroneous—no, because [verbal cognition] determines as that what does not appear as that. And because of deviation, as seen in the case of the error of [taking] the luster of a gem for the gem [itself]. If [one says] the correspondence of error with reality [is the point]—no, because of the very deviation described. For the defining mark of error is a false appearance. But the correspondence [of cognition with reality] is due to the necessary connection [of the verbal cognition with reality], not dependent on the appearance. But when the mind is directed to the real as it actually is, there is no activity because the apprehended universal is incapable of efficacious action. And if activity were [directed] elsewhere, there would be over-extension. And in the grasping of the possessor of <s>jāti</s>, the pointlessness of the universal and other [defects] have been stated. If [one says] even in the grasping of <s>jāti</s>, a cognition that appears as connected [with the particular] causes activity due to the connection—then neither the <s>jāti</s> nor the possessor of <s>jāti</s> [is grasped], since the nature of even one [entity] is not grasped—so the opponent's own position would be adopted. If so, then since there is no entity that persists [across instances], in things that differ in their fundamental nature, the recognition 'this is that same [thing]' would not occur. This is not a fault, because:

children.text: 05117 parasya api na sā buddhiḥ sāmānyād eva kevalāt //99//

Conjoining [them], one would make a recognition even upon seeing another. //
This has been stated: even though they are different, entities produce the same practical effect, like the sense faculties and so forth. For one who sees that single practical effect such as cognition in those [entities], the entities, which are differentiated from others by the very nature of things—through the awakening of the latent impressions of one's own experience, conjoined with the sound that has the exclusion of those [others] as its domain—they produce an erroneous cognition conjoined with [the thought] "this is that very [same thing]," [a cognition] conjoined with difference. Otherwise, there would be no cognition possessing the conjunction of difference—as in the case of stick-bearers. For there, even when one stick is connected [with a person], there is not in another case [the thought] "this is that very [same one]"; rather, [only] "that is here." But recognition is not like that; rather, [it is] "this is that very [same thing]." Therefore, even for one who sees one [thing] in many, the conjunction of difference is not reasonable, as [it would be with real identity]. But through the force of error, there is no contradiction in such cognition. [Objection:] Error is not reasonable in the absence of a cause. [Reply:] Those very entities, producing the same single effect, are the cause, through the avenue of experience, by being the cause of the latent impression of conceptual construction whose fruit is error, by nature. For even in the case of mirages and so forth, [which cause] the error of water and so on, those two entities that produce the experience which is the cause of the cognition that apprehends a single undifferentiated aspect are the cause, even though they are different. For there is no other universal whatsoever that would be so cognized. Or if [the universal] exists, the cognition grasping a real object would not be erroneous. [Objection:] The error is due to the superimposition of an unreal aspect. [Reply:] Then that [cognition] is not a grasper of the universal. For whatever aspect this [cognition] superimposes, that alone is its object—because what has not been made an object cannot be superimposed, just like another aspect. And that [aspect] does not exist there—hence it is not a universal. [Objection:] When there is the grasping of a universal, the superimposition of that [universal onto individuals] does not [happen] otherwise, because of over-extension. [Reply:] When there is the grasping of things producing the same single effect, why is that not accepted? Even one who accepts universals must accept the capacity of individuals to produce a single effect. Therefore, those very [individuals], being differentiated from others, produce such cognition—so what need is there for a universal? [Objection:] Why does [cognition] not apprehend [things] just as they are, without the conjunction of difference? [Reply:] This is the incapacity of conceptual constructions, arising from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). Errors do not arise only in dependence on external [objects]; they also arise from internal disturbance, like the error of seeing hairs [floating in space] and so forth. [Objection:] If there is disturbance arising from <s>avidyā</s>, there would be the same consequence for visual cognition and so forth. [Reply:] No, because that [<s>avidyā</s>] has the character of conceptual construction. For <s>avidyā</s> is precisely conceptual construction. It distorts by its very nature. Sense cognitions are not conceptual in this way. Nor is this fault [present] in them—we shall explain [that it is] because non-dual [cognitions] appear as dual. Even when all [cognitions] are distorted, the distinction between <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) and its semblance [is maintained] until the turning away of the basis, due to conformity with what is considered fit for practical effect. Even though false, [it is valid] due to being conducive to tranquility, like the designation 'mother' and so forth. In the case of the mirage, although there is no difference in the error between the cognition of water and the other [cognition], due to the production of [cognitions] by different entities, the distinction [is drawn] from the conformity with the fitness and unfitness for the desired practical effect—the other [cognitions] are from what is unfit. [Objection:] How can [cognition] arise from what is unfit? [Reply:] Because there is no restriction of connection with objects for conceptual constructions. For conceptual constructions do not arise only in accordance with objects. When the mirage is not seen, the error of water [does not arise]—hence it is said to arise from that; but it is not [produced] in accordance with its own nature, by the giving back of a resemblance of nature by the object that does not distinguish non-water. Rather, that [erroneous cognition] is produced, due to the lack of skill in specific characteristics, by the awakening of one's own latent impressions, dependent upon [external] conditions. Therefore, from the birth [of cognition] from different entities, due to the error of conceptual construction, the recognition "this is that very [same thing]" [arises]—not from the seeing of a separate universal, nor from a non-separate [universal] that does not follow [the individuals] like the individuals themselves. children.translated_text: For there is no so-called benefactor for one that bears its own nature without additional qualification, as before—because of over-extension. And even if it generates something else, what use is that [benefactor] to it? If it [the universal] depends on that [benefactor], what is this substrate-superstratum relation for something that does not benefit? Or there would be over-extension. And even if there is benefit, since the necessary connection with that is in precisely that [domain]—what else benefits it by producing that? If the substrate, which depends on that [universal], has no benefit in its utilization—what is this so-called dependence? An entity whose properties have the nature of originating from that, and which depends [on conditions] due to the necessary connection of its intrinsic nature—[to say that] it, whose nature admits no additional qualification, also depends on others—this is contradictory. Therefore, whatever necessary connection of anything anywhere—all of that is subsumed under the relation of being produced. Because it does not benefit in the production of another's existence. And because what is ineffective does not benefit. Therefore, when the universal, benefited by the particular, [is said to be] the cause of generating cognition—in that generation, the particular is charged with being the effect of that [universal]. Even if the universal alone had capacity, since the capacity of particulars is not established anywhere in this [matter], they would be ungraspable. [Objection:] The particulars are capable because they appear in cognition. [Reply:] How do those whose beneficial role is not established appear?—that is precisely what is considered when a universal is accepted. Because what does not benefit cannot be an object, due to over-extension. There is no appearance in cognition of what is not an object. If [it is said that] because of the inability of non-existents to benefit, past and future things and so forth would not be objects—let them indeed be [cognitions] having those [things] as objects, [yet] without [real] objects. Even without [real] objects, the appearance that imitates them is intrinsic to cognition itself, arising from the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) deposited by the experience of that form. And capacity [is established] from conformity to the existence and non-existence [of the object], not from appearance—because the universal exists apart from the particulars even without appearing. And because errors like hair [seen by a diseased eye] and the like, though appearing, are non-existent. [Objection:] If cognition has undifferentiated appearance, [the objects] are not different—such is the view. [Reply:] We do not say that many things cannot produce a single effect. What then? [We say that] cognition, having those forms imposed upon different objects, would not have undifferentiated appearance. For in cognitions grasping the universal, there is no appearance of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular), since those [cognitions] exist even in its absence, and [the particular] appears in its own cognition through a different form—because one [thing] cannot reasonably have multiple forms, and because of over-extension. Therefore, this [cognition], arising from different objects, does not appear as undifferentiated while grasping them. Even though its appearance is not of that [reality], it causes the world to engage [in action] through the error of determination. But that form appearing in it does not exist in [real] objects—because what is undifferentiated [cannot exist] among what is different from others. And it is formless. [The cognition] grasping precisely that [formless universal] is thereby distorted—this has been stated before. Moreover—even for advocates of real universals, the particulars are indeed different. How then is the cognition of undifferentiated form regarding them?—the objection is the same. [Reply:] It is not the same, because there the undifferentiated universal exists. [Counter:] But even there, its appearance is not discerned despite its existence. For that [cognition] is observed as having the appearance of color, shape, and the like. And the universal is not of such a kind. And there is no other undifferentiated form apart from it. Even for advocates of the <s>ākṛti</s>-universal (form-universal), since it does not differ from the particular, its non-occurrence in another object [means that] due to difference, undifferentiated appearance is not tenable. Or alternatively—let

children.translated_text: [is made] for the purpose of knowing that. //110//

It has been explained that there is no conjunction of intrinsic natures among entities. There, a cognition with conjoined forms is nothing but error. But the different entities, being causes of conceptual thought in sequence, generate [cognition] by their intrinsic nature—and so [their identity] is called their undifferentiated difference, [meaning] the discrimination from the intrinsic nature of what does not produce some single [cognition] or the like. That [cognition] too, though differentiated with each substance, being by nature the cause of a single recognition that overwhelms [awareness of] difference, appears as undifferentiated. Because the particulars, being causes of a cognition and the like that appears as undifferentiated—[a cognition] that is the cause of a recognition of such a nature—generate a single cognition whose ultimate reality is the difference of intrinsic natures, [yet whose] conjoined form is [produced] by intrinsic nature—this has been stated repeatedly. Therefore, the non-difference of entities is precisely [their] production of a single effect. And that [production of a single effect] is the separation from the effect of what is not that—

children.text:
05719 eva yuktaḥ / yo ayam anyonyaṃ viveko bhāvānāṃ tat-pratītaya
05720 eva saṃketo api kriyamāṇaḥ śobheta atat-kāri-vivekena pravṛtty-arthatayā /
05721 yadi hi na tat-pratīty-arthaḥ saṃketas tasya vyavahāra-
05722 kāle apy asaṃsparśān na anya-parihāreṇa pravarteta / na hi sa
05723 teṣāṃ tebhyo vivekaḥ śabdena codita iti / sā ca śrutiḥ /
05801 akārya-kṛti-tat-kāri-tulya-rūpa-avabhāsinīm /
children.translated_text: generating a cognition that appears with a form similar to what produces that effect [and] not producing other effects,

children.text: 05802 dhiyaṃ vastu-pṛthagbhāva-mātra-bījām anarthikām //111//
children.translated_text: whose seed is merely the difference of real things, [a cognition that is] purposeless [in itself]— //111//

This alone is proper. This mutual discrimination of entities—even the convention made for the cognition of those [entities] would be fitting, with the purpose of operation through the discrimination from what does not produce that [effect]. For if the convention were not for the purpose of that cognition, then even at the time of practical usage, due to [the word's] having no connection [with reality], it would not operate through the exclusion of others. For it is not the case that [the word] is prompted by [indicating] the discrimination of those [things] from those [others]—rather, that utterance,

children.text: 05803 janayanty apy atat-kāri-parihāra-aṅga-bhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: even while generating [such cognition], through serving as an element of the exclusion of what does not produce that [effect],

children.text: 05804 vastu-bheda-āśrayāc ca arthe na visaṃvādikā matā //112//
children.translated_text: and because it depends on the difference of real things regarding the object—[the word] is considered non-deceptive. //112//

children.text:
05805 tato anyāpoha-viṣayā tat-kartṛ-āśrita-bhāvataḥ /
05806 eka-svabhāva-rahiteṣv artheṣu tam adhyāropya-utpadyamānāṃ mithyā-
05807 pratibhāsitvād akārya-kāriṇam api tat-kārya-kāriṇam iva adhyavasyantīṃ
05808 vastu-pṛthagbhāva-mātra-bījāṃ samāna-adhyavasāyāṃ
05809 mithyā-buddhiṃ śrutir janayanty api tad-anya-parihāra-aṅga-abhāvāt
05810 paramārthatas tad-vyatirekiṣu padārtheṣu na visaṃvādikā ity ucyate /
05811 tathā hi sa teṣu vyatireko bhūtaḥ / sarvathā avyatikramaṇīyatvāt /
05812 na eko vyatirikto avyatirikto vā sarvathā ayogāt / tasya
05813 samāveśane vastuni dūra-utsṛṣṭam eva vastu syāc śabda-jñānābhyām /
05814 tad-viṣaya-abhimatasya tasya abhāvāt / anyasya ca vastu-
05815 dharmasya kasyacid asaṃsparśāt / tata eva ca sā śrutir anyāpoha-
05816 viṣayayā ity ucyate / anyavyāvṛtteṣv artheṣu vyāvṛtti-bhedam
05817 upādāya aviśeṣeṇa niveśanāt / vyavahāre apy anya-parihāreṇa
05818 pravartanāt /
children.translated_text: [it functions thus].

children.text: 05819 avṛkṣa-vyatirekeṇa vṛkṣa-artha-grahaṇe dvayam //113//
children.translated_text: In grasping the meaning of 'tree' through exclusion from non-tree, both [tree and non-tree] //113//

Therefore [it is said to be] having the exclusion of the other as its domain, because of depending on its author— Generating a false cognition in objects devoid of a single intrinsic nature—[a cognition] that, being a false appearance, determines even what does not produce that effect as if it produced it, whose seed is merely the difference of real things, whose determination is uniform—even while generating [such cognition through] utterance, because of the absence of [the word] being an element of the exclusion of what is other than that, [the word] is said to be non-deceptive regarding objects that ultimately differ from that. For that difference among them is real—because it cannot be transgressed in any way. Nothing is exclusively different or exclusively non-different—because both [alternatives] are impossible in every respect. If that [real particular] were subsumed [under the universal], the real thing would be cast far away by words and cognitions—because that [real particular] which is taken to be their object does not exist [as such], and because no other real property has any connection [with it]. And for that very reason, that utterance is said to have the exclusion of the other as its domain—because it is indiscriminately applied by taking up the difference of exclusion in objects that are excluded from others. Even in practical usage, because it operates through the exclusion of others,

children.text: 05820 anyonya-āśrayam ity eka-graha-abhāve dvaya-agrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: are mutually dependent—thus in the absence of grasping one, neither is grasped;

children.text: 05821 saṃketa-asambhavas tasmād iti kecit pracakṣate //114//
children.translated_text: therefore convention is impossible—so some declare. //114//

children.text:
05822 yady avṛkṣebhyo bhedo vṛkṣas tasya avṛkṣa-grahaṇam antareṇa
05823 tathā grahītum aśakyatvāt avijñāta-vṛkṣeṇa avṛkṣasya api tad-vyavaccheda-
05824 rūpasya aparijñānāt buddhāv anārūḍhe arthe na saṃketaḥ
05825 śakyata ity eke /
05901 teṣām avṛkṣāḥ saṃkete vyavacchinnā na vā /
05902 ya evam ekaṃ vastu-sāmānyam abhyupagamya itaretara-āśrayam
05903 anya-vyavacchedena saṃkete codayanti / teṣāṃ tatra api saṃketa-
05904 karaṇe avṛkṣā vyavacchinnā na vā
children.translated_text: are non-trees excluded or not?

children.text: 05905 yadi /
children.translated_text: If

children.text: 05906 vyavacchinnāḥ kathaṃ jñātāḥ prāg vṛkṣa-grahaṇād ṛte //115//
children.translated_text: they are excluded, how are they known prior to and without the grasping of 'tree'? //115//

If 'tree' is the difference from non-trees, since it cannot be grasped as such without grasping non-tree, and since one who has not known 'tree' also cannot know non-tree (which has the form of exclusion from that [tree]), since the object has not entered the cognition, convention cannot be made—so say some. For them: are non-trees excluded at the time of convention, or not?— Those who, having accepted one real universal, raise the objection of mutual dependence regarding convention through exclusion of the other—for them too, at the time of making that convention,

children.text:
05907 na hi tadā pratipattā vṛkṣaṃ vetti na avṛkṣaṃ taj-jñānāya eva
05908 tad-arthitayā upagamāt / so ajānānaḥ katham avṛkṣa-vyavacchedaṃ
05909 pratipadyeta saṃkete / apratipattau ca aparihṛta-tad-anya-
05910 niveśinaḥ śabdād
children.translated_text: from such a word,

children.text: 05911 anirākaraṇe teṣāṃ saṃkete vyavahāriṇām /
children.translated_text: when they, the users of convention, have not been excluded,

children.text: 05912 na syāt tat-parihāreṇa pravṛttir vṛkṣa-bheda-vat //116//
children.translated_text: there would be no operation through their exclusion—just like the difference of tree [species]. //116//

For at that time the cognizer does not know 'tree,' nor non-tree, since he approaches [the convention] precisely for the purpose of knowing that. How then, not knowing [tree], can he understand the exclusion of non-tree in the convention? And without understanding—from a word that is applied without having excluded what is other than that—

children.text:
05913 na hi saṃkete para-avyavacchedena niveśitāc śabdād vyavahāre
05914 tat-parihāreṇa pravṛttir yuktā / śiṃśapā-ādi-bheda-vat / atha api syāt /
05915 avidhāya niṣidhya-anyat pradarśya ekaṃ puraḥ sthitam /
children.translated_text: Without positively enjoining [anything], having prohibited the other, showing one [thing] standing before [the learner],

children.text: 05916 vṛkṣo ayam iti saṃketaḥ kriyate tat prapadyate //117//
children.translated_text: the convention 'this is a tree' is made; one accepts that. //117//

For operation through the exclusion of the other from a word that has been applied in convention without excluding the other is not reasonable—just like the difference of <s>śiṃśapā</s> (Dalbergia) and the like. But perhaps—

children.text:
05917 vyavahāre api tena ayam adoṣa iti cet /
05918 na vai vastu-sat sāmānya-vādinā kasyacid vyavacchedena kiṃcid
05919 vidhīyate / kiṃ tarhi / ekam agrato vyavasthitaṃ vastu sandarśya
05920 vṛkṣo ayam iti saṃketaḥ kriyate / saṃketa-kāle tathā-dṛṣṭam
05921 eva ayam arthaṃ tat-sambandhinaṃ vā vyavahāre api pratipadyata
06001 iti na samānaḥ prasaṅgaḥ / na samānaḥ / yasmāt tatra api /
06002 taruḥ /
children.translated_text: a tree—

children.text: 06003 ayam apy ayam eva iti prasaṅgo na nivartate //118//
children.translated_text: the absurd consequence that 'this too is this very one' cannot be averted. //118//

[Objection:] In practical usage too, by that [same process], there is no fault. [Reply:] Indeed, by one who holds that universals are real, nothing is positively enjoined through the exclusion of something [else]. What then? Showing one real thing standing before [the learner], the convention 'this is a tree' is made. What was thus seen at the time of convention—that very object, or one related to it, is understood even in practical usage—thus the absurd consequence is not the same. [Reply:] It is not the same, because even there—

children.text:
06004 ekaṃ pradarśya ayaṃ vṛkṣa ity api bruvāṇo ayam apy ayam eva ity
06005 ubhayīṃ gatiṃ na ativartate / tayoś ca sa eva doṣaḥ / na doṣaḥ
06006 dṛṣṭa-viparītasya sujñānatvāt / ekaṃ hi kiṃcit paśyato anyatra
06007 tad-ākāra-vivekinīṃ buddhim anubhavatas tato anyad iti yathā-anubhavaṃ
06008 tad-vivecano vaidharmya-niścaya utpadyate / sa hy
06009 ayam eva vṛkṣa iti pradarśya vyutpāditaḥ / yatra eva taṃ na
06010 paśyati tam eva avṛkṣaṃ svayam eva pratipadyate / na idaṃ vyavaccheda-
06011 vādinaḥ sambhavati / ekatra dṛṣṭasya rūpasya kvacid
06012 ananvayād darśanena pratipattau vyakty-antare api na syāt tathā
06013 pratītiḥ / evaṃ tarhi tatra api tulyam etat / yasmāt /
06014 eka-pratyavamarśa-ākhye jñāna ekatra hi sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who is established in the cognition called 'recognition' regarding one [thing],

children.text: 06015 prapattā tad-atad-hetūn arthān vibhajate svayam //119//
children.translated_text: having comprehended, distinguishes on his own the objects that are causes and non-causes of that. //119//

For having shown one [tree] and said 'this is a tree,' when also [indicating] 'this too is this very [thing],' one does not transcend both modes. And in both of those, the same fault [applies]. [Reply:] There is no fault, because what is contrary to what has been observed is easily known. For one who sees some one thing, and who experiences a cognition that distinguishes that form elsewhere—'it is other than that'—a determination of dissimilarity arises as a discrimination of that, in accordance with experience. For he has been instructed by showing 'this is indeed a tree.' Wherever he does not see that [tree], he understands on his own that it is a non-tree. This is not possible for one who advocates exclusion. Since the form seen in one [instance], not being positively present anywhere else, the cognition through seeing [would not occur]—nor in another instance would there be such cognition. [Reply:] Then the same [applies] there too. Because:

children.text:
06016 niveditam etat prāg yathā ete bhāvāḥ prakṛti-bhedino api jñāna-ādikam
06017 ekaṃ kāryaṃ kecit kurvanti na anya iti / tān ayaṃ tatra svayam
06018 eva tad-hetūn atad-hetūṃś ca vibhajya pratyeti / tasya /
06019 tad-buddhi-vartino bhāvān bhāto hetutayā dhiyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The entities present in that cognition, appearing as the cause of the cognition,

children.text: 06020 ahetu-rūpa-vikalān eka-rūpān iva svayam //120//
children.translated_text: devoid of the form of non-causes, as if of one form, on their own— //120//

This was explained before: how these entities, though differing in nature, some produce a single effect such as cognition, while others do not. This [person] distinguishes on his own the causes and non-causes of that there, and cognizes [them]. Of that [person]:

children.text: 06021 bhedena pratipadyeta ity uktir bhede niyujyate /
children.translated_text: 'One would cognize through difference'—this statement is applied to difference;

children.text: 06022 taṃ tasyāḥ pratiyatī dhīr bhrāntyā ekaṃ vastv iva īkṣyate //121//
children.translated_text: cognition cognizes that of that [statement]; through error, it is seen as if [it were] one object. //121//

children.text:
06023 teṣāṃ prakṛtyā eva pratyaya-vaśāt tathābhūta-vikalpa-kāraṇānām
06024 anvayāt tad-draṣṭur buddhau viparivartamānān taj-jñāna-
06025 hetutayā tad-anyavyāvṛttyā ca atathābhūtān api tathā-adhyavasitān
06026 avibhakta-bāhya-adhyātmika-bhedān pratipattā pratipattim anusṛtya
06027 ete vṛkṣā iti sva-para-vikalpeṣv eka-pratibhāsān ādarśya vikalpa-
06028 vijñāne vyavasthitas tad-vijñāna-hetūn bhedena pratipadyeta
06101 ity uktim atad-hetubhyo bhede niyuṅkte / taṃ tasyāḥ pratipadyamānā
06102 buddhir vikalpikā bhrānti-vaśād eva eka-vastu-grahiṇī iva
06103 pratibhāti / na punar ekaṃ vastu tatra dṛśyam asti yasya darśana-
06104 adarśanābhyāṃ bhinna-darśane apy eṣa vṛkṣa-avṛkṣa-vibhāgaṃ
06105 kurvīta / tasya śākhā-ādi-pratibhāsa-vibhāgena daṇḍa-vad daṇḍiny
06106 agrahaṇāt / agṛhītasya ca apara-pravibhāgena anupalakṣaṇāt / ākṛter
06107 apy ekatra dṛṣṭāyā anyatra draṣṭum aśakyatvāt / tad-atadvator
06108 vṛkṣa-avṛkṣatve vyaktir eka eva vṛkṣaḥ syāt / bhavatu nāma ghaṭa-ādi-
06109 śabdeṣv artha-antara-vyavacchedaḥ / atha jñeya-ādi-padeṣu katham /
06110 na hy ajñeyaṃ kiṃcid asti yato bhedaḥ syāt / tato bhedena
06111 viṣayīkaraṇa eva tasya jñeyatvāt / na eṣa doṣaḥ / yasmāt /
06112 kvacin niveśanāya arthe vinivartya kutaścana /
children.translated_text: A word is employed for the purpose of settling [the mind] on a certain object by turning [it] away from something—

children.text: 06113 buddheḥ prayujyate śabdas tad-arthasya avadhāraṇāt //122//
children.translated_text: because the meaning of that [word] is the ascertainment [of that object]. //122//

Because of the natural following of those [entities], which through the force of conditions are the causes of such conceptual construction, for the one who sees that, as they revolve in his cognition—as the cause of that cognition and through exclusion from what is other than that, even though not actually being of that nature, they are determined to be so, with the distinction of external and internal undivided—the cognizer, following his cognition, shows 'these are trees' in his own and others' conceptual constructions as appearing as one, and being established in conceptual cognition, applies the statement 'one would cognize the causes of that cognition through difference' to [their] difference from the non-causes of that. The conceptual cognition that cognizes that [difference] of that [statement] appears, through the force of error alone, as if grasping a single object. But there is no single object visible there whose observation and non-observation would enable this person to make the distinction between tree and non-tree. Because, through the division of appearances such as branches and so forth, like a stick in the stick-bearer, [the universal] is not grasped. And because what is not grasped cannot be characterized by further subdivision. And because a form (<s>ākṛti</s>) seen in one [instance] cannot be seen in another. In [the view of] those for whom tree-hood and non-tree-hood belong to presence and absence of that [universal], only one individual would be a tree. [Objection:] Let there be exclusion of other objects in words like 'pot' and so forth. But in words like 'knowable' and so forth, how [does exclusion work]? For there is nothing unknowable from which there could be difference. Since precisely from difference [from that], it becomes knowable by being made the object. [Reply:] This is not a fault. Because:

children.text: 06114 vyartho anyathā prayogaḥ syāt taj jñeya-ādi-padeṣv api /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, the application [of a word] would be purposeless; and in words like 'knowable' and so forth too,

children.text: 06115 vyavahāra-upanīteṣu vyavacchedyo asti kaścana //123//
children.translated_text: when brought into conventional usage, there is something to be excluded. //123//

children.text:
06116 śabdaṃ hi prayuñjānaḥ sarvo anvaya-vyatirekau na ativartate /
06117 tasya pravṛtti-nivṛtty-arthatvāt / yadi hy ayaṃ na kasyacit kutaścin
06118 nivartayet pravartayed vā buddhiṃ yathābhūta-anujñānāt
06119 sarva-vyavahāreṣu na kiṃcid vyāharet / vyāhārasya avadhāraṇa-
06120 nāntarīyakatvāt / yathā ghaṭena udakam ānayeti / yadi ghaṭena añjalinā
06121 vā udaka-ānayanaṃ yathākathaṃcid abhimataṃ syāt udakam
06122 ānayety eva vaktavyaṃ syāt / na ghaṭena iti / tathā paṃśunā
06123 vā anena vā yena kenacid ānītena artha ānayety eva syād anākṣipta-
06124 karaṇa-karmakam / evam ānayanam anyad vā yat kiṃcid
06125 anuṣṭhānaṃ vā abhimataṃ tadā ānayety api na
06126 brūyāt / vyarthatvād vacanasya / tathā vyavahāra-upanītānāṃ jñeya-ādi-
06201 padānām api kenacid vyavacchedyena bhavitavyam / ananya-āśaṅkāyāṃ
06202 prayoga-ayogāt tatra hi yad eva mūḍha-mater āśaṅkā-sthānaṃ
06203 tad eva nivartyam / anāśaṅkamāno vā kiṃ parasmād
06204 upadeśam apekṣate / aśrotṛ-saṃskāraṃ ca bruvāṇaḥ kathaṃ
06205 na unmattaḥ / tat-saṃskārāya eva śabdānāṃ kṛta-saṃketatvāt / avyavahāra-
06206 upanītaś ca na eva kaścit jñeya-ādi-śabdo asti / vākya-gatasya
06207 padasya artha-cintanāt / kva punar ete śabdāḥ prayujyanta iti
06208 prayoga-viṣaya-cintāyām anyāpoha ucyate / anirdiṣṭa-prayogaṃ tu
06209 jñeya-śabdasya ko artha iti praśne na kaścid arthaḥ / tataḥ kvacid
06210 apratipatteḥ / tathā ghaṭa-ādi-śabdānām api / yā api kvacit prakaraṇe
06211 kevala-śabda-śravaṇāt pratipattir dṛṣṭa-prayoga-anusāreṇa sākāṅkṣatvāt
06212 sā aparisamāpta-tad-viplava eva ghaṭa-ādi-śabdeṣu /
06213 tādṛśo jñeya-ādi-śabdeṣv api yathā-darśanam asty eva / tasmāt
06214 sarva eva śabda-prayogaḥ kutaścid buddhiṃ nivartya kvacin niveśana-
06215 arthaḥ / tat-sāphalyāt /
06216 niveśanaṃ ca yo yasmād bhidyate vinivartya tam /
children.translated_text: And the settling [on something]—by turning away that from which [the object] differs—

children.text: 06217 tad-bhede bhidyamānānāṃ samāna-ākāra-bhāsini //124//
children.translated_text: when what is being distinguished is distinguished, [the word settles the mind] on what appears as having a similar form. //124//

For everyone who employs a word does not transcend positive and negative concomitance, because [words] have the purpose of engagement and disengagement. For if this [word] would not turn away or engage someone's cognition from or toward something, then since [everything would be] a mere acknowledgment of how things are, one would say nothing in any conventional transaction—because verbal expression necessarily involves ascertainment. For example, 'Bring water with a pot.' If bringing water with a pot or with cupped hands, or in any manner whatsoever, were intended, then one should say only 'bring water,' not 'with a pot.' Likewise, if it were [equally acceptable to bring it] with dust or with this or with whatever, since any [method of] bringing would serve the purpose, 'bring' alone should be said, without specifying the instrument and object. Similarly, if bringing or any other action or performance whatsoever were intended, then one should not even say 'bring'—because the statement would be purposeless. Likewise, even words like 'knowable' and so forth, when brought into conventional usage, must have something to be excluded. Because application [of a word] is impossible when there is no suspicion of something else. For precisely that which is a source of doubt for the confused mind is what needs to be negated. And one who has no doubt—what need does he have for instruction from another? And one who speaks without creating an impression in the listener—how is he not a madman? Because conventions are made for words precisely for the purpose of creating impressions. And there is no word such as 'knowable' and so forth that is not brought into conventional usage, because the meaning of a word in a sentence is considered [only in context]. But where are these words employed?—in the investigation of the domain of application, exclusion of others is stated. But when the application is not specified, what is the meaning of the word 'knowable'?—to this question, there is no meaning, because there is no cognition of anything from that [alone]. The same [applies] to words like 'pot' and so forth. Even the cognition that arises somewhere from merely hearing a word in isolation—since it follows previously observed usage and is expectant [of further context]—that is in words like 'pot' and so forth precisely an incomplete distortion. In words like 'knowable' and so forth too, such [cognition] exists in accordance with what has been observed. Therefore every application of a word is for the purpose of settling [the mind] on something by turning it away from something else—because of [the word's] fruitfulness in that [function].

children.text: 06218 sa ca ayam anyavyāvṛttyā gamyate tasya vastunaḥ /
children.translated_text: And this [difference] is understood through exclusion from others; it is called

children.text: 06219 kaścid bhāga iti prokto rūpaṃ na asya api kiṃcana //125//
children.translated_text: 'some part' of that real thing—but even this has no [independent] form. //125//

children.text: 06220 tad-gatāv eva śabdebhyo gamyate anya-nivartanam /
children.translated_text: From words, what is understood in that very direction is the negation of others;

children.text: 06221 na tatra gamyate kaścid viśiṣṭaḥ kenacit paraḥ //126//
children.translated_text: no specific [entity] distinguished by anything else is understood there. //126//

children.text: 06222 na ca api śabdo dvaya-kṛd anyonya-abhāva ity asan /
children.translated_text: And the word does not have a dual function; mutual absence, being non-existent,

children.text: 06223 arūpo rūpavattvena darśanaṃ buddhi-viplavaḥ //127//
children.translated_text: is formless—seeing it as if possessing form is a distortion of cognition. //127//

children.text:
06224 niveśyamāno apy eṣa śabdo yasmād bhidyate taṃ vinivartya
06225 bhidyamānānāṃ bhede samāna-rūpa-pratibhāsiny ākṣipta-tad-anyavyāvṛttir
06226 niveśyata iti / sa eva ayam artha-antara-vyāvṛttyā
06227 tasya vastunaḥ kaścid bhāgo gamyate śabdo artha-antara-nivṛtti-
06301 viśiṣṭān eva bhāvān āha ity ādinā nirdiṣṭaḥ / sa hi taṃ bhedaṃ
06302 kathayann artha-antara-vyavacchedam ākṣipan eva vartate /
06303 eka-gata-bheda-codanāyās tad-anyavyāvṛtty-ākṣepa-nāntarīyakatvāt /
06304 sa eva bhedas tad-vyāvṛttyā gato bhāgas tad-gates tad-upādhitvāt
06305 tad-viśiṣṭo gata ity ucyate / na punar artha-antara-nivṛttir viśeṣaṇa-
06306 bhūtā keṣāṃcid arthānāṃ yayā viśiṣṭāḥ śabdaiś codyante / daṇḍi-vat /
06307 dvayor hi bhidyamānayor bhedasya ubhaya-gatatvād
06308 eka-bheda-abhidhāne api nāntarīyakas tad-anya-ākṣepo bhavati iti tayor
06309 na viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ / eka-bheda-abhidhāne apy anyavyāvṛtti-
06310 gater anvaya-vyatireka-codanayā vyavahāra-aṅgatāṃ śabdānāṃ
06311 darśayaṃs tad-vyāvṛttyā gamyate tad-viśiṣṭo vā ity āha / ata
06312 eva ca śabdasya na dvau vyāpārau tad-anyavyāvartanaṃ svārtha-
06313 abhidhānaṃ ca / svārtha-abhidhānād eva tad-anyavyāvṛtti-gateḥ /
06314 svārthasya bheda-rūpatvāt / na hy anvayo avyatireko ananvayo
06315 vā vyatirekaḥ / eka-anvayasya parihārya-abhāve niṣphala-codanatvāt
06316 tathā eka-parihārasya kvacit sthity-abhāve / sa ca ayaṃ bhedo arūpaḥ /
06317 rūpavattvena tv asya darśanaṃ kevalaṃ buddhi-viplava
children.translated_text: but seeing it as if possessing form is merely a distortion
of cognition.

children.text: 06401 tena eva aparamārtho asāv anyathā na hi vastunaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore it is not ultimately real; for otherwise, the exclusion of a real thing

children.text: 06402 vyāvṛttir vastu bhavati bhedo asya asmād iti īraṇāt //128//
children.translated_text: would not be a real thing—because of the statement 'this is its difference from that.' //128//

Even this word, when being applied [to settle on an object], having turned away from that which [the object] differs from, is applied [to settle on an object] in whose difference from what is being distinguished the exclusion from that which is other than it is entailed, appearing as having a similar form. This very [process] is described as 'some part of that real thing is understood through exclusion from other things'—'the word expresses entities qualified precisely by the exclusion of other things' and so forth. For one who states that difference implicitly entails the exclusion of other things, because the prompting of a difference belonging to one [entity] necessarily entails the exclusion from what is other than it. That very difference, understood through the exclusion from it, is called a 'part understood [in that direction],' because that [exclusion] is the <s>upādhi</s> (limiting condition) of the understanding in that direction—qualified by it, it is said to be 'understood.' But the negation of other objects is not a qualifier of certain objects by which they, being qualified, are indicated by words—like 'staff-bearer.' For of two things being distinguished, since difference belongs to both, even in the expression of one difference, the implication of what is other than it necessarily follows—thus they do not have the qualifier-qualified relationship. Showing that words serve conventional practice through the understanding of exclusion from others even in the expression of one difference, through the prompting of positive and negative concomitance, he says 'it is understood through the exclusion from that' or 'qualified by that.' For this very reason, the word does not have two functions—the negation of what is other than it and the expression of its own meaning—because the understanding of the exclusion from that other follows from the very expression of its own meaning, since its own meaning has the form of difference. For positive concomitance is not [separate from] negative concomitance, nor is non-positive-concomitance [the same as] negative concomitance. Because the prompting of a single positive concomitance, in the absence of something to be excluded, would be fruitless; likewise a single exclusion, [which must] have stability somewhere. And this difference is formless;

children.text:
06403 rūpaṃ hi paramārthaḥ / bhedaś ced rūpaṃ syāt / tad-rūpaṃ vā
06404 syād atad-rūpaṃ vā / tādrūpye tad eva iti na anyas tato bhidyeta /
06405 na hi tasya rūpam anyasya syāt / na tad eva bhedasya rūpaṃ /
06406 rūpaṃ ca anyad eva syāt / tataś ca bhāvas tasmād vyāvarteta /
06407 tato asmāt tasya bheda iti na syāt / yat khalu yad-bhedād vyāvartate
06408 tad eva tad bhavati iti so asya bheda iti ca na syāt / na
06409 hy anyonyasya bhedo bhavati / sambandha-abhāvāt / sati vā sa
06410 kāryakāraṇabhāva iti rūpaṃ taj-janitaṃ bheda ity aviśeṣāt /
06411 sarva-kāryāṇi sva-kāraṇānāṃ vyāvṛttayaḥ syuḥ / rūpa-antaratve
06412 ca bhedasya tato apy asya bheda iti bheda-upādhitvāt dravya-antara-van
06413 na bhedaḥ syāt / na hi bheda-upādhir eva bhedo ayam ata
06414 iti viśeṣa-nirdeśāt / tataś ca upādhy-abhāve bhedasya eva abhāvaḥ syāt /
06415 tasmān na vyatiriktaḥ / tad-anya-gaty-abhāvāc ca vastuno na paramārthaḥ /
06416 kathaṃ tarhy abhinnasya vastunaḥ śabdena codane
06417 tasya eva anyato api bhedād anaṃśaya-eka-bheda-codane sarva-bheda-
06418 gates tatra śabda-pramāṇa-antarāṇi vyarthāni na syuḥ / yasmāt /
06419 eka-artha-śleṣa-viccheda eko vyāpriyate dhvaniḥ /
children.translated_text: One sound operates by [performing] the joining and separating of a single meaning;

children.text: 06420 liṅgaṃ vā tatra vicchinnaṃ vācyaṃ vastu na kiṃcana //129//
children.translated_text: the logical mark too [operates thus]; what is separated there is something to be expressed—no real thing. //129//

For form is the ultimate reality. If difference were a form, it would either be of that form or not of that form. If it were of that form, then it would be that very [thing] and nothing other would be differentiated from it. For the form of one cannot be that of another. Nor is the form of difference identical [to the thing]. And the form would be something else entirely. And then the entity would be excluded from that [difference]. Then 'its difference from this' would not be [the case]. For what is excluded by the difference from something is that very thing—thus 'that is its difference' would not hold. For one thing does not have the difference of another, because of the absence of a relation. Or if there is [a relation], it is a cause-effect relationship—so 'form' and 'the difference produced by it' would be indistinguishable. All effects would be the exclusions of their own causes. And if difference has a different form, then there would be its difference from that too—and since difference is the <s>upādhi</s> [of further difference], like another substance, it would not be a difference. For [someone may say:] 'This is not merely a limiting condition of difference—this is a difference from that'—because of the specific indication. And then, in the absence of a limiting condition, difference itself would be absent. Therefore [difference] is not distinct [from the thing]. And because there is no other possibility for a real thing, [difference] is not ultimately real. But how then, when the undifferentiated real thing is prompted by a word, since from the difference of that very [thing] from others, when one difference is prompted in what has no parts, the understanding of all differences [would follow], and words and other <s>pramāṇas</s> there would not be purposeless? Because:

children.text: 06421 yasya abhidhānato vastu-sāmarthyād akhile gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: That from whose expression, through the power of the real thing, there would be the understanding of everything—

children.text: 06422 bhaven nānā-phalaḥ śabda eka-ādhāro bhavaty ataḥ //130//
children.translated_text: the word, having a single basis, would therefore have manifold results. //130//

children.text:
06423 uktaṃ prāg yathā saṃsṛṣṭa-bāhya-adhyātmika-bhedā buddhiḥ svam
06424 eva ābhāsaṃ vyavahāra-viṣayam arthakriyā-yogyam adhyavasāya
06425 śabda-artham upanayati iti / tatra eva ca te śabdās tais tair bhrānti-
06426 kāraṇaiḥ saṃsṛṣṭa-rūpa iva ābhāti yathā-saṃketaṃ vicchedāya vyāpriyante/
06427 na ca eka-sādhyaṃ vyavacchedam anyaḥ karoti / saṃketa-
06501 pratiniyamāt na ca vicchinnaṃ kiṃcid vastv ākṣipyate
06502 yasya abhidhānād vastu-balena akhile gatiḥ syāt / śabdānāṃ buddhi-
06503 viplava-viṣayatvāt / tatra ca avastuni vastu-sāmarthya-abhāvāt / tathābhūta-
06504 artha-darśana-dvāreṇa ayaṃ nānā-eka-dharma-bheda-abheda-pratibhāsa-
06505 viplava-anusārī vyavahāra iti tasya tat-pratibandhe sati
06506 tad-avyabhicāraḥ / tato vitathād apy ante tathābhūta eva vastuni
06507 jñāna-saṃvādāt / na punar bhinna-ākāra-grāhiṇāṃ jñāna-śabdānāṃ
06508 eka-vastu-viṣayatvāt nānā-phalaḥ śabda eka-ādhāro vyāghātāt / yathā varṇite
06509 tu buddhi-pratibhāsa-āśraye na doṣa iti /
children.translated_text: when [the word] is based on what appears in cognition, there is no fault.

children.text: 06510 vicchedaṃ sūcayan ekam apratikṣipya vartate /
children.translated_text: When indicating separation while not excluding one [property],

children.text: 06511 yadā anyaṃ tena sa vyāpta ekatvena ca bhāsate //131//
children.translated_text: it operates on another—by that it is pervaded and appears as one. //131//

It was stated before that cognition, with the distinction of external and internal mixed together, determines its own appearance—which is the object of conventional practice and capable of causal function—as the meaning of the word and presents it. And it is precisely there that those words operate for the purpose of separation, in accordance with convention, in [that appearance] which appears as if having mixed forms through various causes of error. And one [word] does not effect the separation that is to be accomplished by another, because of the restriction of convention. And no separated real thing is implied from whose expression, through the power of reality, the understanding of everything would follow—because words have as their domain the distortion of cognition. And in that [distortion], which is not a real thing, there is no power of reality. This conventional practice, which follows the distortion of the appearance of difference and non-difference of manifold and single properties through the window of perceiving objects of such a nature—when it is bound to that [reality], it does not deviate from it. Therefore, from what is ultimately false too, in the end there is concordance of cognition with the real thing that is precisely of that nature. But [this is] not because cognitions and words that grasp different forms have a single real object as their domain—in that case, the word, having a single basis, would have manifold results, which would be contradictory. But as described,

children.text: 06512 sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ syāt tadā buddhy-anurodhataḥ /
children.translated_text: There would be co-reference, then, in conformity with cognition;

children.text: 06513 vastu-dharmasya saṃsparśo viccheda-karaṇe dhvaneḥ //132//
children.translated_text: there is no contact with a real property for the sound that effects separation. //132//

children.text: 06514 syāt satyaṃ sa hi tatra iti na eka-vastv-abhidhāyini /
children.translated_text: It may be true [that] 'it is there'—but not in a cognition that designates a single entity,

children.text: 06515 buddhāv abhāsamānasya dṛśyasya abhāva-niścayāt //133//
children.translated_text: because of the ascertainment of the absence of what is perceptible [yet] does not appear in cognition. //133//

children.text: 06516 ity antaraślokāḥ /
children.translated_text: These are intervening verses.

children.text: 06517 tena anyāpoha-viṣayāḥ proktāḥ sāmānya-gocarāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, words and cognitions that have universals as their domain are said to have <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other) as their object,

children.text: 06518 śabdāś ca buddhayaś ca eva vastuny eṣām asambhavāt //134//
children.translated_text: because their occurrence in a real thing is impossible. //134//

children.text:
06519 yadi hi vidhi-rūpeṇa vastv eva śabdair vikalpair vā api viṣayīkriyeta
06520 so ayaṃ sarva-artha-sarva-ākāra-pratīti-prasaṅgo asāmānādhikaraṇya-
06521 ādayaś ca iti manyamānaḥ praṇetā nyāya-śāstrasya anyāpoha-
06522 viṣayāv etau prāha / tathā hi /
06523 ekatvād vastu-rūpasya bhinna-rūpā matiḥ kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the nature of a real thing is one, whence would cognition of differentiated form [arise]?

children.text: 06524 anvaya-vyatirekau vā na ekasya eka-artha-gocarau //135//
children.translated_text: Or, positive and negative concomitance of one [entity] would not have different objects. //135//

For if a real thing itself were made the object by words or concepts in a positive manner, there would be the absurd consequence of the cognition of all objects in all aspects, as well as [impossibility of] co-reference and the like—thinking thus, the author of the <s>Nyāya</s> treatise declared these two [words and cognitions] to have <s>anyāpoha</s> as their object. For:

children.text:
06525 tad ekam anaṃśaṃ vastu kathaṃ bhinna-ākārābhir buddhibhir
06526 viṣayīkriyate / ākāra-bheda-āśrayatvād bhedasya / tasya ca abhedāt /
06527 tadātmano api sāmānyasya tad-ekayogakṣematvāt / tad ayam
06528 anyonya-artha-parihāreṇa eka-viṣayayor vṛtty-abhāvāt sāmānādhikaraṇya-
06601 ādir na ca vastv-ātmana ekasya tatra eva vṛttir
06602 avṛttiś ca yuktā vyāghātāt / na ca anyatra avartamānaṃ sāmānyaṃ
06603 syāt / sāmānyasya vṛttir na viśeṣasya iti cet / na / bheda-abhāvāt / tad
06604 hi eka-rūpaṃ sāmānyaṃ vā bhavet viśeṣo vā / na hy asati rūpa-bhede
06605 ayaṃ pravibhāgo yuktaḥ sati vā avyatireko na syād ity uktam /
06606 tad ayam avibhāgo anviyād vā na vā / na punar ananvayo anvayī
06607 ca / yo api bhinnam eva sāmānyam āha / tasya api /
06608 abheda-vyavahārāś ca bhede syur anibandhanāḥ /
06609 yathāsvaṃ śabdā bhinnam artham abhidadhānāḥ katham eka-artha-
06610 buddhy-āśrayāḥ syuḥ / artha-antara-abhidhāyinaś ca anākṣepakāḥ
06611 nirākāṅkṣatvāt kathaṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva-āśrayāḥ /
children.translated_text: And [how could] those that denote another object, being non-suggestive due to [their] self-sufficiency, be the basis for the qualifier-qualified relationship?

children.text: 06612 sarvatra bhāvād vyāvṛtter na ete doṣāḥ prasaṅginaḥ //136//
children.translated_text: Since exclusion exists everywhere, these faults do not follow. //136//

That single, partless real thing—how is it made the object of cognitions with differentiated aspects? Because difference depends on a basis of difference of aspects—and that [real thing] is undifferentiated. Even a universal that is identical with it shares its single fortune. Thus, since there is no occurrence of two [cognitions] in a single object when each excludes the other's object, co-reference and the like [are impossible]. Nor is it reasonable that a single entity should both occur and not occur there, because of contradiction. Nor could a universal that does not occur elsewhere [be a universal]. If [one says] the universal occurs [there] but not the particular—no, because there is no difference. For that entity, being of one form, would be either a universal or a particular. For without a difference of form, this division is not reasonable; and if there is [a difference], there would be no non-distinction, as stated. So this undivided [thing] either persists [across instances] or does not—but it cannot both not persist and persist. Even for one who says the universal is entirely different [from the particular]: conventions of non-difference would be groundless in [the case of] difference. Words denoting distinct objects each in its own right—how could they be the basis for a cognition of a single object?

children.text:
06613 yathā hy ekas tasmād bhinnas tathā anyo api iti bhedasya asāmānya-
06614 doṣo api na asti / pariśiṣṭa-abhāvas tu prāg eva uktaḥ / api ca /
06615 eka-kāryeṣu bhedeṣu tat-kārya-paricodane /
children.translated_text: Among [things that are] different [yet] produce a single effect, in enjoining [them by] that effect,

children.text: 06616 gaurava-aśakti-vaiphalyād bheda-ākhyāyāḥ samā śrutiḥ //137//
children.translated_text: because of cumbersomeness, incapability, and futility of the designation of difference, the verbal expression is the same [for all]. //137//

For just as one [thing] is different from that [other], so too is another—hence there is no fault of non-universality of difference. The absence of the remainder has already been stated earlier. Moreover:

children.text: 06617 kṛtā vṛddhair atat-kārya-vyāvṛtti-vinibandhanā /
children.translated_text: It was made by the elders, based on the exclusion from [those that do] not [produce] that effect—

children.text: 06618 na bhāve sarva-bhāvānāṃ svabhāvasya vyavasthiteḥ //138//
children.translated_text: not on the [positive] existence [of anything], since the own nature of all entities is fixed [and unique]. //138//

children.text: 06619 yad rūpaṃ śābaleyasya bāhuleyasya na asti tat /
children.translated_text: The form that belongs to <s>Śābaleya</s> does not belong to <s>Bāhuleya</s>;

children.text: 06620 atat-kārya-parāvṛttir dvayor api ca vidyate //139//
children.translated_text: yet the exclusion from what does not produce that effect exists for both. //139//

children.text: 06621 artha-abhedena ca vinā śabda-abhedo na yujyate /
children.translated_text: And without identity of meaning, identity of words is not reasonable;

children.text: 06622 tasmāt tat-kāryatā api iṣṭā atat-kāryād eva bhinnatā //140//
children.translated_text: therefore, the production of that effect is accepted [as the basis]—differentiation is only from what does not produce that effect. //140//

children.text: 06623 cakṣur-ādau yathā rūpa-vijñāna-eka-phale kvacit//
children.translated_text: Just as in [the case of] the eye and the like, where the result is a single cognition of visible form, in some [case],

children.text: 06624 aviśeṣeṇa tat-kārya-codanā-sambhave sati //141//
children.translated_text: when it is possible to enjoin without distinction by that effect— //141//

children.text: 06625 sakṛt sarva-pratīty-arthaṃ kaścit sāṃketikīṃ śrutim /
children.translated_text: someone would establish a conventional expression for the purpose of a single apprehension of all [of them],

children.text: 06626 kuryād ṛte api tad-rūpa-sāmānyād vyatirekiṇaḥ //142//
children.translated_text: even without a distinct universal of that form. //142//
