10507 vā abhyupagamya pravṛtti-nivṛttī vilomayan yathā abhyupagamaṃ
10508 pratipādyate nirupākhya-vad anya-vad vā iti / sa eva tāvad
10509 upalabdhy-abhāvaḥ kathaṃ siddha iti cet / etad uttaratra vakṣyāmaḥ /
10510 anyatra apy anumāne sādhya-dharmeṇa vyāptaṃ sādhanam
10511 icchan kim iti dṛṣṭāntena pratyāyyo vyāpya-nirdeśād eva
10512 vyāpnuvataḥ siddheḥ / niścita-arthasya api smṛty-artho dṛṣṭānta iti
10513 cet / tad itaratra api samānaṃ / so ayam anyatra anupalambha-mātrād
10514 asad-vyavahāraṃ pratipadyamāno api iha vyāmūḍha iti
10515 smāryate / atha yad idaṃ na santi pradhāna-ādayo anupalabdher
10516 iti / tatra katham asad-vyavahāra-vidhiḥ sad-vyavahāra-niṣedho
10517 vā / kathaṃ ca na syāt / tad-artha-pratiṣedhe dharmi-vācino aprayogād
10518 abhidhānasya nirviṣayasya ca pratiṣedhasya ayogāt / na eṣa
10519 doṣaḥ / yasmāt /
10520 anādi-vāsanā-udbhūta-vikalpa-pariniṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Established in conceptual construction arising from beginningless latent impressions,

children.text: 10521 śabda-arthas trividho dharmo bhāva-abhāva-ubhaya-āśrayaḥ //205 //
children.translated_text: the meaning of words—the threefold property—has existence, non-existence, and both as its basis. //205//

For an entity that does not co-exist with another—because of the contradiction of their arising, since the material causes of the two are the basis of mutual deficiency—even when one of those two contradictories is present, the cognition of the absence of the other arises, as was stated before. This is not established separately from non-apprehension—because from that very [non-apprehension comes] the cognition of contradiction, and from contradiction the proof of absence. Let [it be granted that] from such non-apprehension there is the cognition of absence. But how then is it an inference? And how could it not be? [Objection:] Because it does not require an example. For in this [case] there is no example. [Reply:] Is not a space-flower and so forth, which is without characterization, an example? [Objection:] That is non-existent—how is it to be known, so that it could serve [as an example]? [Reply:] From non-apprehension alone, if [one says so]. [Objection:] Then how is the establishment of non-existence without an example [achieved]? Or if there is an example, there would be the unwanted consequence of infinite regress. And thus, non-cognition [would result]. [Reply:] Therefore, just as the establishment of absence of what is without characterization [proceeds without an example], so too elsewhere, because of the non-requirement of an example, it is not non-inference. Even while hearing, the dear-to-the-gods [i.e., the fool] is not skilled in ascertainment. For the occasion of the conventional practices of the word 'non-existent' is the non-apprehension of what is apprehendable. That [non-apprehension], from its own proximity, establishes these [conventions] that are its own occasions—hence, every [situation] here where there is the fitting proximity of the aggregate of its own occasions is an example. Non-existence here is, again, precisely non-apprehension. For this very reason, because this [non-apprehension] has the character of inference of an effect from a cause, we shall explain that it is included in the <s>svabhāva-hetu</s> (essential nature reason). In the negation of the conventional practices of the word 'existent' too, sprouts and so forth whose deficiency of occasion is not [present] through the cessation of the <s>pramāṇa</s> are the example—not merely what is without characterization. Even regarding what is without characterization, it is precisely this operation that is negated. Non-existence characterized by non-apprehension is already established. This confused [person], having accepted the occasion or the absence of that, reverses the operation and non-operation, and is instructed according to his acceptance—whether like what is without characterization or like other [things]. [Objection:] How then is that very absence of apprehension itself established? [Reply:] We shall explain this later. [Objection:] In other inferences too, when one wishes the proof to be pervaded by the property to be proved, why should it be made known by an example, since from the mere indication of the pervaded, the pervader is established? [Objection:] The example is for the purpose of recollection, even for one whose object is ascertained. [Reply:] That is the same elsewhere too. This [person], though elsewhere he accepts the conventional practice of 'non-existent' from mere non-apprehension, is here recalled as confused. Now, regarding the [claim] 'primordial matter and so forth do not exist, because of non-apprehension'—how is the convention of 'non-existent' established there, or how is the convention of 'existent' negated? And how could it not be? [Objection:] Because in the negation of the meaning of that [word], the word denoting the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) is not employed, and because the negation of a designation that has no object is not reasonable. [Reply:] This is not a fault. Because—

children.text: 10522 tasmin bhāva-anupādāne sādhye asya anupalambhanam /
children.translated_text: When the non-adoption of existence is what is to be proved regarding that [word-meaning], its non-apprehension

children.text: 10523 tathā hetur na tasya eva abhāvaḥ śabda-prayogataḥ //206//
children.translated_text: is likewise the reason; [it is] not the absence of that very [thing] based on the use of the word. //206//

children.text:
10524 niveditam etat yathā na ete śabdāḥ svalakṣaṇa-viṣayā anādi-
10525 vāsanā-prabhava-vikalpa-pratibhāsinam arthaṃ viṣayatvena ātmasāt
10526 kurvanti vaktuḥ śrotus ca tad-vikalpa-bhājo yathāpratibhāsi-
10527 vastu-pratipādana-samīha-aprayogāt tad-ākāra-vikalpa-jananāc ca /
10601 na ca upādāna-kārya-pratyaya-apratibhāsi rūpaṃ śakyaṃ tad-viṣayatvena
10602 adhyavasātum / sa tu vikalpaḥ sad-asad-ubhaya-pratyaya-āhita-
10603 vāsanā-prabhava iti tat-pratibhāsy-ākāra-adhyavasāya-vaśena
10604 ca bhāva-abhāva-ubhaya-dharma ity ucyate / tad atra dharmiṇi vyavasthitāḥ
10605 sadasattvaṃ cintayanti kim ayaṃ pradhāna-śabda-pratibhāsy
10606 artho bhāva-upādāno na vā iti / tasya bhāva-anupādānatve
10607 sādhye sa eva pratyātma-vedyatvād apratikṣepa-arho artho dharmī /
10608 na ca sa eva arthaḥ svalakṣaṇam iti śakyaṃ vaktum / asamprāpta-niruddhayor
10609 apy arthayos tasya anapāyāt / vastu-viparīta-ākāra-niveśiṣv
10610 api tīrtha-anantarīya-pratyayeṣu bhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Because it exists even in the cognitions immediately following the holy ones' [teachings], which involve aspects contrary to reality.

children.text: 10611 paramārtha-eka-tānatve śabdānām anibandhanā /
children.translated_text: If words had a single ultimate referent, there would be no unfounded

children.text: 10612 na syāt pravṛttir artheṣu darśana-antara-bhediṣu //207//
children.translated_text: operation [of words] regarding objects that differ [according to] different philosophical views. //207//

This has been explained—how these words do not have <s>svalakṣaṇas</s> (particulars) as their objects, [but rather] they appropriate as their object the meaning that appears in the conceptual construction born from beginningless latent impressions—because neither for the speaker nor for the hearer, who partakes of that conceptual construction, is there an effort to convey the real thing as it appears [in direct experience], and because [words] produce conceptual construction of that form. And a form that does not appear in the cognitions of apprehension, effect, and condition cannot be determined as the object of that [word]. But that conceptual construction arises from latent impressions deposited by the cognitions of existent, non-existent, and both—and through the determination of the aspect that appears in that [conceptual construction], it is called the property of existence, non-existence, and both. Therefore, those who are established in that <s>dharmin</s> (subject) consider its existence and non-existence: 'Is this meaning, which appears in the word <s>pradhāna</s>, one that adopts existence or not?' When its non-adoption of existence is to be proved, that very object—worthy of non-rejection because it is known to each [person] individually—is the <s>dharmin</s>. And it cannot be said that that object is a <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>—because it does not depart [from cognition] even regarding past and unborn objects.

children.text: 10613 atīta-ajātayor vā api na ca syād anṛta-arthatā /
children.translated_text: Nor would there be the falsity of meaning even regarding past and unborn [things].

children.text: 10614 vācaḥ kasyāścid ity eṣā bauddha-artha-viṣayā matā //208//
children.translated_text: of some speech—this is considered to have the Buddhist meaning as its domain. //208//

children.text:
10615 iti saṃgrahaślokau / tasya ca yathā samīhita-rūpa-anupādānatve
10616 sādhye tathā anupalambho asya dharmo asti iti na sādhana-dharma-asiddhiḥ /
10617 na punar atra ayam eva śabda-vikalpa-pratibhāsy artho apahnūyate /
10618 tasya buddhāv upasthāpanāya śabda-prayogāt / tad-abhāve
10619 tad-ayogāt / api ca /
10620 śabda-artha-apahnave sādhye dharma-ādhāra-nirākṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: When the denial of the word-meaning is the property to be proved, since the substrate of the property would be eliminated,

children.text: 10621 na sādhyaḥ samudāyaḥ syāt siddho dharmaś ca kevalaḥ //209//
children.translated_text: the aggregate would not be the <s>sādhya</s> (property to be proved), and the property alone would be already established. //209//

These are the summary verses. And just as, when the non-adoption of the desired form is the property to be proved, the non-perception of this is its property—hence there is no non-establishment of the property of the probans. But here it is not the case that the very object appearing in verbal conceptualization is being denied—because words are employed in order to present that [object] in cognition. Because in its absence, that [presentation] would be impossible. Moreover:

children.text:
10623 yadi hi śabda-artha eva apohyeta pradhāna-śabda-vācyasya dharmiṇa
10624 eva nirākaraṇān nirādhāraḥ sādhya-dharmaḥ syāt / tad ayam
10625 ādhāra-vyavaccheda-anapekṣo na vivāda-āśraya iti na upanyasanīya
10626 eva syāt / kiṃ ca /
10627 sad-asat-pakṣa-bhedena śabda-artha-anapavādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: By those who do not deny the word-meaning, through the division of the positions 'existent' and 'non-existent,'

children.text: 10628 vastv eva cintyate hy atra pratibaddhaḥ phala-udayaḥ //210//
children.translated_text: it is a real thing itself that is investigated here—for the arising of the result is restricted [to that]. //210//

For if the word-meaning itself were to be denied, then since the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) denoted by the primary word would itself be eliminated, the property to be proved would be without a substrate. Thus this [property], not depending on the delimitation of a substrate, would not be the basis of dispute, and hence would not need to be presented at all. Moreover:

children.text: 10629 arthakriyāsamarthasya vicāraiḥ kiṃ tad-arthinām /
children.translated_text: For one capable of efficacious action, what [use is] investigation to those who desire that [result]?

children.text: 10630 ṣaṇḍhasya rūpa-vairūpye kāminyāḥ kiṃ parīkṣayā //211//
children.translated_text: What [use is] the examination of beauty and ugliness of a eunuch to a woman desiring [a lover]? //211//

children.text:
10701 na hi śabda-artho asan san vā kaṃcit puruṣa-artham uparuṇaddhi
10702 samādadhāti vā / yathā abhiniveśam atattvāt / yathā atattvaṃ ca asamīhitatvāt /
10703 tad ayaṃ pravartamānaḥ sarvadā sad-asac-cintāyām
10704 avadhīrita-vikalpa-pratibhāso vastv eva adhiṣṭhānīkaroti yatra ayaṃ
10705 puruṣa-arthaḥ pratibaddho yathā agnau śīta-pratīkāra-ādiḥ / na hy
10706 atra śabda-arthaḥ samarthas tad-anubhava-āptāv api tad-abhāvāt /
10707 tad ayam arthakriyā-arthī tad-asamarthaṃ prati dattā-anuyogo bhavituṃ
10708 na yuktaḥ / na hi vṛṣasyantī ṣaṇḍhasya rūpa-vairūpya-parīkṣāyām
10709 avadhatte / yat punar etad uktaṃ kalpitasya anupalabdhir
10710 dharma iti tasya ko arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: is a property'—what is its meaning?

children.text: 10711 śabda-arthaḥ kalpanā-jñāna-viṣayatvena kalpitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word-meaning is 'imagined' by virtue of being the object of conceptual cognition;

children.text: 10712 dharmo vastv-āśraya-asiddhir asya ukto nyāyavādinā //212//
children.translated_text: its property, says the logician, is the non-establishment of a real substrate. //212//

For the word-meaning, whether existent or non-existent, neither obstructs nor establishes any human purpose—because one's attachment [to it] is not in accordance with reality, and because its non-accordance with reality is because it is not desired [as the real goal]. So this person, always acting, in the investigation of existence and non-existence, disregarding the appearance of conceptual construction, takes as his basis the real thing itself, where this human purpose is restricted—as in [the case of] fire for the remedy of cold and the like. For the word-meaning is not capable [of fulfilling that purpose]—even upon obtaining the experience of that [word-meaning], that [capability] is absent. Therefore, it is not reasonable for this person, who desires efficacious action, to be engaged in inquiry regarding what is incapable of that. For a woman in heat does not attend to the examination of the beauty or ugliness of a eunuch. Now, what was stated—'the non-perception of what is imagined

children.text:
10713 kalpanā-viṣayatvāc śabda-artha eva kalpitaḥ / tasya vastv -āśraya-anupalambho
10714 dharma ity abhiprāyaḥ / yad uktam na pramāṇa-
10715 traya-nivṛttāv api bhāva-abhāva-siddhir iti / tan mā bhūd anya-pramāṇa-
10716 anivṛttau nivṛttiḥ / tayor asakala-viṣayatvād āgamaḥ punar
10717 na kiṃcin na vyāpnoti / tan-nivṛttiḥ kathaṃ na gamikā iti / uktam
10718 atra na āgameṣu sarva-arthā upanibadhyante aprakaraṇa-āpannatvād
10719 iti / api ca /
10720 nāntarīyakatā abhāvāc śabdānāṃ vastubhiḥ saha /
children.translated_text: Because of the absence of a necessary connection of words with real things,

children.text: 10721 na artha-siddhis tatas te hi vaktṛ-abhiprāya-sūcakāḥ //213//
children.translated_text: the establishment of objects [does not follow] from them—for they are indicators of the speaker's intention. //213//

The word-meaning is 'imagined' precisely because of being the object of conceptualization. Its property is the non-perception of a real substrate—this is the intended meaning. As for what was stated—that even upon the cessation of the three <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition), existence and non-existence are not established—let there not be cessation when other <s>pramāṇas</s> have not ceased. Since those two [perception and inference] do not cover all domains, but scripture (<s>āgama</s>) indeed pervades everything—how is its cessation not indicative [of absence]? The response has been stated: not all objects are recorded in scriptures, because they do not pertain to the relevant topic. Moreover:

children.text:
10722 na hi śabdā yathābhāvaṃ vartante yatas tebhyo artha-prakṛtir
10723 niścīyeta / te hi vaktur vivakṣā-vṛttaya iti tan-nāntarīyakās
10724 tām eva gamayeyuḥ / na ca puruṣa-icchāḥ sarvā yathārtha-bhāvinyaḥ /
10725 na ca tad-apratibaddha-svabhāvo bhāvo anyaṃ gamayati /
10801 yat tarhi idam āpta-vāda-avisaṃvāda-sāmānyād anumānatā ity āgamasya
10802 prāmāṇyam anumānatvam uktam tat kathaṃ / na ayaṃ puruṣo anāśritya āgama-
10803 āsituṃ samarthaḥ / atyakṣa-phalānāṃ keṣāṃcit
10804 pravṛtti-nivṛttyor mahā-anuśaṃsā-pāpa-śravaṇāt tad-bhāve virodha-
10805 adarśanāc ca / tat sati pravartitavye varam evaṃ pravṛtta
10806 iti parīkṣayā prāmāṇyam āha / tac ca /
10807 sambaddha-anuguṇa-upāyaṃ puruṣa-artha-abhidhāyakam /
children.translated_text: a statement that describes a human purpose, with connected and appropriate means,

children.text: 10808 parīkṣā-adhikṛtaṃ vākyam ato anadhikṛtaṃ param //214//
children.translated_text: is subject to examination; the rest is not subject [to examination]. //214//

For words do not operate in accordance with reality, such that from them the true nature of objects could be ascertained. For they operate according to the speaker's desire to express, and being necessarily connected with that [desire], they would indicate only that. And not all human wishes are in accordance with the real state of affairs. Nor does an entity whose nature is not restricted to that [desire] indicate another [entity]. Now, what was stated—that the authority of scripture is its character as inference, because of the general non-deception of the words of a reliable person (<s>āpta</s>)—how [is this]? This person is not capable of taking a position without relying on scripture. Because, for certain [injunctions] whose results are beyond the senses, great rewards and sins are heard of for engagement and disengagement, and because no contradiction is seen when [those injunctions hold] true. Therefore, when one must act, it is better to act in this way—this is the authority established through examination. And that—

children.text:
10809 sambaddho vākyānām eka-artha-upasaṃhāra-upakāraḥ / na daśa-dāḍima-ādi-
10810 vākyānām iva anupasaṃhāra eva / anyathā vaktur vaiguṇyam
10811 udbhāvayet / aśakya-upāya-phalāni ca śāstrāṇi phala-arthī na ādriyeta
10812 vicārayitum apuruṣa-artha-phalāni ca / viṣa-śamanāya takṣaka-
10813 phaṇa-ratna-alaṃkāra-upadeśa-vat kāka-danta-parīkṣā-vac ca / tad viparyayeṇa
10814 upasaṃhāra-vat śakya-upāyaṃ puruṣa-artha-abhidhāyi ca
10815 śāstraṃ parīkṣyeta anyatra avadhānasya eva ayuktatvāt / tad yadi na
10816 parīkṣāyāṃ visaṃvāda-bhāk pravartamānaḥ śobheta / kaḥ punar
10817 asya avisaṃvādaḥ /
children.translated_text: its non-deception?

children.text: 10818 pratyakṣeṇa anumānena dvividhena apy abādhakam /
children.translated_text: Uncontradicted by perception and by both types of inference—

children.text: 10819 dṛṣṭa-adṛṣṭa-arthayor asya avisaṃvādas tad-arthayoḥ //215//
children.translated_text: regarding its visible and invisible objects—this is its non-deception with respect to those objects. //215//

'Connected' means that the statements contribute to the conclusion of a single purpose—not like the statement 'ten pomegranates' and the like, which have no conclusion. Otherwise, it would reveal the deficiency of the speaker. And one who desires results would not attend to examine scriptures whose means are impossible to implement, or whose results are not of human purpose—like the instruction to adorn oneself with the gem from the hood of a <s>Takṣaka</s> serpent for curing poison, or like the examination of a crow's teeth. Conversely, a scripture that has a conclusion, has implementable means, and describes a human purpose should be examined—because attending to anything else is simply unreasonable. If, then, it does not prove deceptive upon examination, it would be commendable. But what is

children.text:
10820 pratyakṣeṇa abādhanaṃ pratyakṣa-abhimatānām arthānāṃ tathābhāvaḥ
10821 yathā nīla-ādi-sukha-duḥkha-nimitta-upalakṣaṇa-rāga-ādi-buddhīnām /
10822 atathā-abhimatānāṃ ca apratyakṣatā yathā śabda-ādi-rūpa-
10823 saṃniveśināṃ sukha-ādīnāṃ dravya-karma-sāmānya-saṃyoga-ādīnāṃ
10824 ca / tathā anāgama-apekṣa-anumāna-viṣaya-abhimatānāṃ tathābhāvaḥ
10825 yathā catūrṇām āryasatyānām / ananumeyānāṃ tathābhāvo
10901 yathā ātma-ādīnām / āgama-apekṣa-anumāne api yathā rāga-ādi-
10902 rūpaṃ tat-prabhavaṃ ca adharmam abhyupagamya tat-prahāṇāya
10903 snāna-agnihotra-āder anupadeśaḥ / sa iyaṃ śakya-pariccheda-aśeṣa-viṣaya-
10904 viśuddhir avisaṃvādaḥ /
children.translated_text: such as the self and the like. Also, in inference dependent on scripture, [for example,] having accepted the nature of passion and the like and the demerit (<s>adharma</s>) arising from them, the non-teaching of bathing, fire-sacrifice, and the like for their abandonment. This purity in all domains that can be ascertained is non-deception.

children.text: 10905 āpta-vāda-avisaṃvāda-sāmānyād anumānatā /
children.translated_text: Because of the general non-deception of the words of a reliable person (<s>āpta</s>), it has the character of inference—

children.text: 10906 buddher agatyā abhihitā parokṣe apy asya gocare //216//
children.translated_text: this is stated, out of necessity, for the cognition regarding even its imperceptible domain. //216//

Non-contradiction by perception [means] the reality of objects that are accepted as perceptible—such as cognitions of blue and the like, of pleasure and pain, and characterized by passion and the like having [pleasure and pain] as their causes. And the imperceptibility of those accepted as not being so—such as pleasure and the like that have the form of sound and the like, and substances, actions, universals, conjunction, and the like. Likewise, the reality of those accepted as objects of inference not dependent on scripture—such as the Four Noble Truths. And the non-inferrability of those whose reality [is as stated]—

children.text:
10907 tasya ca asya evaṃbhūtasya āpta-bhūtasya avisaṃvāda-sāmānyād adṛṣṭa-
10908 vyabhicārasya pratyakṣa-anumāna-āgamye apy arthe pratipattes
10909 tad-āśrayatvāt tad-anya-pratipatti-vad avisaṃvādo anumīyate /
10910 tataḥ śabda-prabhavā api satī na śābda-vad abhiprāyaṃ nivedayaty
10911 eva ity artha-avisaṃvādād anumānam api / athavā anyathā āpta-vādasya
10912 avisaṃvādād anumānatvam ucyate /
children.translated_text: is stated because of non-deception:

children.text: 10913 heya-upādeya-tattvasya sa upāyasya prasiddhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: from the well-known truthfulness of the means to the reality of what is to be avoided and adopted—

children.text: 10914 pradhāna-artha-avisaṃvādād anumānaṃ paratra vā //217//
children.translated_text: from the non-deception regarding the principal purpose, it is inference regarding the rest as well. //217//

And for this one who is thus characterized as reliable, because of the general non-deception—whose deviation has not been observed—even in the object that cannot be reached by perception and inference, since the apprehension depends on that [reliable person], non-deception is inferred, like apprehension dependent on other [reliable sources]. Therefore, even though arising from words, since it does not merely communicate intention like ordinary verbal [testimony], due to non-deception regarding the object, it is also inference. Or, alternatively, the character of inference of reliable speech

children.text:
10915 heya-upādeya-tad-upāyānāṃ tad-upadiṣṭānām avaiparītyam avisaṃvādaḥ /
10916 yathā catūrṇām āryasatyānāṃ vakṣyamāṇanītyā / tasya asya
10917 puruṣa-artha-upayogino abhiyoga-arthasya avisaṃvādād viṣaya-antare
10918 api tathātva-upagamo na vipralambhāya anuparodhāt niṣprayojana-
10919 vitatha-abhidhāna-vaiphalyāc ca vaktuḥ / tad etad agatyā ubhayathā
10920 apy anumānatvam āgamasya upavarṇitam / varam āgamāt
10921 pravṛttāv evaṃ pravṛttir iti / na khalv evam anumānam anapāyam
10922 anāntarīyakatvād artheṣu śabdānām iti niveditam etat /
10923 puruṣa-atiśaya-apekṣaṃ yathārtham apare viduḥ /
10924 yathārtha-darśana-ādi-guṇa-yuktaḥ puruṣa āptas tat-praṇayanam avisaṃvāda
children.translated_text: a person endowed with the qualities of truthful perception and the like is a reliable person (<s>āpta</s>); his composition is non-deception—

children.text: 11001 ity anye /
children.translated_text: so say others.

children.text: 11002 iṣṭo ayam arthaḥ śakyeta jñātuṃ so atiśayo yadi //218//
children.translated_text: This meaning would be acceptable if that [personal] excellence could be known. //218//

Non-deception is the non-falsity of what is taught by him regarding what is to be avoided, what is to be adopted, and the means to those—as in the case of the Four Noble Truths, in the manner to be described. Because of the non-deception of this person [the <s>Buddha</s>], which is relevant to human purpose and worthy of engagement, the acceptance of truthfulness in other domains too is not for the purpose of deception—because there is no incompatibility [with that truthfulness], and because a false statement without purpose would be futile for the speaker. Thus, this character of inference for scripture has been described in both ways, out of necessity. It is better to act in this way when acting on the basis of scripture—for inference based on [the necessary connection between] words and objects is not without flaw, as has been explained. Others understand [the matter as] depending on a person of excellence, being truthful:

children.text:
11003 sarve eva āgamam anāgamaṃ vā pravṛtti-kāmo anveṣate prekṣā-
11004 pūrva-kārī na vyasanena / api nāma anuṣṭheyam ato jñātvā pravṛtto
11005 arthavān syām iti / sa śakya-darśana-avisaṃvāda-pratyayena anyatra api
11006 pravartate / evaṃprāyatvāl loka-vyavahārasya / puruṣa-parīkṣayā
11007 tu pravṛttāv apravṛttir eva / tasya tathābhūtasya jñātum
11008 aśakyatvāt na aniṣṭeḥ / tādṛśām avitatha-abhidhānāt / tathā hi /
11009 ayam evaṃ na vā ity anya-doṣa-anirdoṣatā api vā /
children.translated_text: 'This person is thus or not'—whether another is flawed or flawless—

children.text: 11010 durlabhatvāt pramāṇānāṃ durbodhā ity apare viduḥ //219//
children.translated_text: is difficult to know, because of the rarity of [appropriate] means of valid cognition—so others hold. //219//

Everyone who desires to act, whether [relying on] scripture or non-scripture, investigates—acting with deliberation, not out of compulsion—[thinking:] 'Perhaps, having learned what is to be practiced from this, I would be successful in my endeavor.' He acts elsewhere too based on the confidence of non-deception in what can be observed. Because worldly conduct is generally of this kind. But in acting based on the examination of the person, there would be non-engagement altogether—because it is impossible to know him as being of such a nature. Not because of unwillingness—because such persons are truthful in their statements. For:

children.text:
11011 caitasyebhyo hi guṇa-doṣebhyaḥ puruṣāḥ samyaṅ-mithyā-pravṛttaḥ
11012 te ca atīndriyāḥ sva-prabhava-kāya-vāg-vyavahāra-anumeyāḥ
11013 syuḥ / vyavahārāś ca prāyaśo buddhi-pūrvam anyathā api kartuṃ
11014 śakyante puruṣa-icchā-vṛttitvāt teṣāṃ ca citra-abhisandhitvāt /
11015 tad ayaṃ liṅga-saṃkarāt katham aniścinvan pratipadyeta / atha
11016 kiṃ na eva sa tādṛśaḥ puruṣo asti yo nirdoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: is there really no such person who is faultless?

children.text: 11017 sarveṣāṃ savipakṣatvān nirhrāsa-atiśaya-śritām /
children.translated_text: Since all [afflictions] have their opposites, and are subject to diminution and increase,

children.text: 11018 sa ātmībhāvāt tad-abhyāsād dhīyeran āśravāḥ kvacit //220 //
children.translated_text: because of their [opposite's] becoming one's own nature, through the practice of that, the <s>āśravas</s> (afflictions) would diminish in some [person]. //220//

For persons act rightly or wrongly due to mental qualities and faults. And those [mental states] are beyond the senses and would have to be inferred from the behavior of body and speech that arises from them. But behaviors can mostly be done otherwise too, deliberately, because they operate according to human volition and because of the varied intentions [of persons]. So how can this person, unable to ascertain [the truth] due to the confusion of marks, [correctly] apprehend [the other's nature]? But then,

children.text:
11019 sa tu prahīṇa-āśravo durjñānaḥ / doṣā hi nirhrāsa-atiśaya-dharmaṇo
11020 vipakṣa-abhibhava-utkarṣa-apakarṣaṃ sādhayanti jvālā-ādi-vat / te hi
11021 vikalpa-prabhavāḥ saty apy upādāne kasyacin mano-guṇasya abhyāsād
11022 apakarṣiṇaḥ / tat-pāṭave niranvaya-vināśa-dharmāṇaḥ
11023 syuḥ / jvālā-ādi-vad eva / tena syād api nirdoṣaḥ / kathaṃ nirdoṣo
11024 nāma / yāvatā doṣa-vipakṣa-sātmatve api doṣa-sātmano vipakṣa-utpatti-vad
11025 yathā-pratyayaṃ doṣa-utpattir api / na ayaṃ doṣaḥ / yasmāt /
11027 nirupadrava-bhūta-artha-svabhāvasya viparyayaiḥ//
children.translated_text: But one whose <s>āśravas</s> have been eliminated is difficult to know. For faults, having the property of diminution and increase, establish the increase and decrease of overpowering the opposite—like flames and the like. For they arise from conceptual construction, and even when the material cause is present, they diminish through the habituation of a certain mental quality. When that [quality] is perfected, they would have the property of destruction without remainder—just like flames and the like. Therefore, there may indeed be one who is faultless. [Objection:] How can there be one who is 'faultless'? Since even when one has made the opposite of faults one's own nature, the arising of faults would follow the arising of their conditions, just as the arising of the opposite [can follow] even when faults have been made one's own nature. This is not a fault, because:

children.text:
11028 na bādhā yatnavattve api buddhes tat-pakṣa-pātataḥ //221 /
11101 na hi svabhāvo ayatnena vinivartayituṃ śakyaḥ / śrotriya-
11102 kāpālika-ghṛṇā-vat / yatnaś ca prāpya-nivartyayoḥ svabhāvayor
11103 guṇa-doṣa-darśanena kriyeta / tac ca vipakṣa-sātmanaḥ puruṣasya
11104 doṣeṣu na sambhavati / tasya nirupadravatvāt / aśeṣa-doṣa-hāneḥ
11105 paryavasthāna-janma-pratibaddha-duḥkha-vivekāt praśama-sukha-
11106 rasasya anudvejanāc ca / abhūta-arthaṃ khalv apy upādāna- bala-bhāvi-
11107 santānasya viparyaya-upādānān na syāt / na tu bhūta-artham vastu-
11108 bala-utpatteḥ / abhūta-arthāś ca doṣā na pratipakṣa-sātmya-bādhinaḥ /
11109 tasmān na punar doṣa-utpattiḥ / yatne api buddher guṇa-pakṣa-
11110 pātena pratipakṣa eva yatna-ādhānāt parīkṣāvato viśeṣeṇa aduṣṭa-
11111 ātmanaḥ / kaḥ punar eṣāṃ doṣāṇāṃ prabhavo yat-pratipakṣa-
11112 abhyāsāt prahīyante /
11113 sarvāsāṃ doṣa-jātīnāṃ jātiḥ satkāyadarśanāt//
children.translated_text: For one whose nature is the unafflicted reality of things, there is no harm from distortions, even when effort is made—because of the mind's partiality toward that side. //221// For essential nature cannot be reversed without effort—like the disgust of a learned <s>Brahmin</s> toward a <s>Kāpālika</s> (skull-bearer). And effort would be made through the perception of the qualities and faults of the natures to be attained and to be removed. But that is not possible regarding faults for a person who has made the opposite [of faults] his own nature—because of his being unafflicted. Because of the abandonment of all faults without remainder, because of the discrimination from suffering connected with [afflicted] birth and its consequences, because of the relishing of the happiness of tranquility, and because of the absence of disturbance. Even for one in a continuum that exists through the force of habituation of an unreal object, there would be [no return to] distortion through the adoption of a distorted [perception]—but not [the same for] what accords with reality, because of origination through the force of the real thing. And faults, being unreal, do not obstruct the habituation of the opposite. Therefore, there is no re-arising of faults—even when effort [is made], because of the mind's partiality toward the side of qualities, effort is directed precisely toward the opposite, especially for one who examines and whose nature is uncorrupted. But what is the origin of these faults, through whose opposite's practice they are eliminated?

children.text: 11114 sā avidyā tatra tat-snehas tasmād dveṣa-ādi-sambhavaḥ //222 //
children.translated_text: Of all classes of faults, the origin is <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (the view of the self-complex); // that is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance); from that [arises] attachment to that; from that, the arising of hatred and the like. //222//

children.text:
11115 na hi na ahaṃ na mama iti paśyataṃ parigraham antareṇa kvacit
11116 snehaḥ / na ca ananurāgiṇaḥ kvacid dveṣaḥ / ātma-ātmīya-anuparodhiny
11117 uparodha-pratighātini ca tad-abhāvāt / tasmāt samāna-jātīya-abhyāsajam
11118 ātma-darśanam ātmīya-grahaṃ prasūte / tau ca tat-snehaṃ
11119 sa ca dveṣa-ādīni iti satkāyadarśanajāḥ sarva-doṣāḥ / tad eva ca ajñānam
11120 ity ucyate /
11121 moho nidānaṃ doṣāṇām ata eva abhidhīyate//
children.translated_text: For those who do not see 'I' or 'mine,' there is no affection anywhere without possessiveness. And for one who has no attachment, there is no hatred anywhere—because of the absence of that [hatred] toward what neither obstructs nor counteracts what belongs to self and what is one's own. Therefore, the perception of self, born of the practice of what is homogeneous [with it], gives rise to the grasping of 'mine.' And those two [give rise to] attachment to that, and that [gives rise to] hatred and the like—thus all faults are born of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. And that very [satkāyadṛṣṭi] is called ignorance.

children.text: 11122 satkāyadṛṣṭir anyatra tat-prahāṇe prahāṇataḥ //223 //
children.translated_text: Delusion is said to be the root cause of faults; // <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> [operates] elsewhere; by its abandonment, [all faults are] abandoned. //223//

children.text:
11123 mohaṃ doṣa-nidānam āhuḥ amūḍhasya doṣa-anutpatteḥ punar
11124 anyatra satkāyadṛṣṭim / tac ca etat pradhāna-nirdeśe sati syād
11125 aneka-janmanāṃ doṣāṇām eka-utpatti-virodhāt / na ca dvayoḥ prādhānye
11201 ekaika-nirdeśaḥ para-bhāga-bhāk / ubhayathā apy ekasya
11202 nirdeśe na virodhaḥ / prādhānyaṃ punas tad-upādānatvena /
11203 tat-prahāṇe doṣāṇāṃ prahāṇāt / tasmāt sambhavati satkāyadarśana-
11204 janmanāṃ doṣāṇāṃ tat-pratipakṣa-nairātmya-darśana-abhyāsāt
11205 prahāṇam / sa tu kṣīṇa-doṣo duranvayo yad-upadeśād ayaṃ pratipadyeta /
11206 mā bhūt puruṣa-āśrayaṃ vacanam āgamaḥ praṇetur
11207 duranvayatvāt /
11208 girāṃ mithyātva-hetūnāṃ doṣāṇāṃ puruṣa-āśrayāt//
children.translated_text: They call delusion (<s>moha</s>) the root of the afflictions (<s>doṣa</s>), since afflictions do not arise for the undeluded; others [identify it as] the view of the self-aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>). And this would apply when the primary [cause] is indicated—because the arising of afflictions of many births from a single source is contradictory. And when both are primary, the indication of each one partakes of the other's portion. There is no contradiction in indicating one in either way. The primacy is through being the material cause of that—because when that is abandoned, the afflictions are abandoned. Therefore it is possible that afflictions born from the view of the self-aggregate are abandoned through the cultivation of the counter-agent—the vision of selflessness (<s>nairātmya-darśana</s>). But that one whose afflictions are extinguished is difficult to follow—from whose instruction this [disciple] might understand. Let not scripture (<s>āgama</s>) be a person-dependent statement, because its author is difficult to follow. Since the afflictions, which are the causes of the falsity of speech, reside in a person—

children.text: 11209 apauruṣeyaṃ satya-artham iti kecit pracakṣate //224 //
children.translated_text: some declare [the Veda to be] authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) and true in meaning. //224//

children.text:
11210 na khalu sarva eva āgamaḥ sambhāvya-vipralambhaḥ / vipralambha-
11211 hetūnāṃ doṣāṇāṃ puruṣa-āśrayād apauruṣeyaṃ satya-artham ity
11212 eke / kāraṇa-abhāvo hi kārya-abhāvaṃ sādhayati iti / ya evaṃvādinas
11213 tān eva prati /
11214 girāṃ satya-artha-hetūnāṃ guṇānāṃ puruṣa-āśrayāt//
children.translated_text: Surely not every scripture is susceptible to deception. Since the afflictions, which are the causes of deception, reside in a person—therefore [the Veda is] authorless and true in meaning, say some. For the absence of a cause establishes the absence of an effect. Against those who speak thus: Since the virtues, which are the causes of the truth of speech, [also] reside in a person—

children.text: 11215 apauruṣeyaṃ mithyā-arthaṃ kiṃ na ity anye pracakṣate //225 //
children.translated_text: why do not others declare [that] the authorless [Veda] is false in meaning? //225//

children.text:
11216 yathā rāga-ādi-parītaḥ puruṣo mṛṣā-vādī dṛṣṭas tathā dayā-dharmatā-
11217 ādi-yuktaḥ satya-vāk / tad yathā vacanasya puruṣa-āśrayān mithyā-arthatā
11218 tathā satya-arthatā api iti / sa nivartamānas tām api nivartayati
11219 ity ānarthakyaṃ syād viparyayo vā / na hi śabdāḥ prakṛtyā arthavantaḥ /
11220 samayāt tato artha-khyāteḥ kāya-saṃjñā-ādi-vat / aprātikūlyaṃ
11221 tu yogyatā samaye tad-icchā-praṇayanāt / nisarga-siddheṣv
11222 icchā-vaśāt pratipādana-ayogāt / te anarthakāḥ puruṣa-saṃskārād
11223 arthavantaḥ syuḥ / tat-saṃskāryatā eva ca eṣāṃ pauruṣeyatā yuktā
11224 na utpattiḥ / tata eva artha-vipralambhāt / utpanno apy anyathā samito
11225 na uparodhī tad-anya-puruṣa-dharma-vat / tad ayaṃ nivartamānaḥ
11226 sva-kṛta-samaya-sambhavām artha-pratibhāṃ nivartayati /
11227 tat kutas tan-nivṛttyā satya-arthatā / atha punar utpattir eva pauruṣeyatā /
11301 na samaya-ākhyānam /
11302 artha-jñāpana-hetur hi saṃketaḥ puruṣa-āśrayaḥ//
children.translated_text: Just as a person afflicted by desire and the like is seen to speak falsely, so one endowed with compassion, righteousness, and the like speaks truthfully. Therefore, just as speech has false meaning because it resides in a person, so it has true meaning as well. One who removes [the person-dependence] would remove that [truth] too—so there would be purposelessness or reversal. For words are not meaningful by their own nature— [they are meaningful] from convention, because the meaning is known from that, like bodily gestures (<s>kāya-saṃjñā</s>) and the like. Non-opposition is the fitness in convention, because the desire [to express] is produced for that [purpose]. Because [fitness] cannot be demonstrated at will for what is naturally established. Those [words], being meaningless, would become meaningful through human conditioning (<s>saṃskāra</s>). And this very conditionability is their proper person-dependence (<s>pauruṣeyatā</s>)—not their origination. Because deception in meaning [arises] from precisely that. Even what has originated, when conventionalized differently, does not obstruct—like the properties of persons other than that [original author]. Thus, this [person], when removed, removes the cognition of meaning that arises from his self-made convention. Therefore, how is there truth of meaning from the removal of that [person]? But again, if person-dependence is precisely origination, not the declaration of convention—

children.text: 11303 girām apauruṣeyatve apy ato mithyātva-sambhavaḥ //226 //
children.translated_text: even given the authorlessness of speech, the possibility of falsity [remains] because the convention, which is the cause of making meaning known, resides in a person. //226//

children.text:
11304 kiṃ hy asya apauruṣeyatayā yato hi samayād artha-pratipattiḥ
11305 sa pauruṣeyo vitatho api syāt / śīla-sādhana-svarga-vacanaṃ tad anyathā
11306 samayena viparyāsayet / tena ayathārtham api prakāśana-sambhavāt
11307 sa eva doṣaḥ /
11308 sambandha-apauruṣeyatve syāt pratītir asaṃvidaḥ//
children.translated_text: For what [use is] its authorlessness—since the convention from which the cognition of meaning [arises] is person-dependent and could even be false? The statement about morality, practice, and heaven could be reversed through a different convention. Therefore, since incorrect illumination is possible even through that, the same fault [applies]. If the connection [between word and meaning] is authorless, there would be cognition without communication—

children.text:
11309 syād etad akārya-sambandhā eva śabdāḥ / na te artheṣu puruṣair
11310 anyathā viparyasyante / tena adoṣa iti / kim idānīṃ saṃketena /
11311 sa hi sambandho yato artha-pratītiḥ / sa ced apauruṣeyo na ayaṃ
11312 samayam apekṣeta / apratīty-āśrayo vā kathaṃ sambandhaḥ /
11313 saṃketāt tad-abhivyaktāv asamartha-anya-kalpanā //227 //
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Let the words have an uncreated connection. They are not reversed to other meanings by persons. Therefore there is no fault. [Reply:] What then [is the role] of convention? For the connection from which the cognition of meaning [arises]—if that is authorless, this [word] would not depend on convention. Or how is a connection [possible] that is not based on cognition? If it is manifested from convention, the postulation of something else that is incapable [is unfounded]. //227//

children.text:
11314 na vai sambandho vidyamāno apy anabhivyaktaḥ pratīti-hetuḥ /
11315 saṃketas tv enam abhivyanakti / sa tarhi siddha-upasthāyī kim
11316 akāraṇaṃ poṣyate / nanv iyān sambandhasya vyāpāro yad artha-
11317 pratīti-jananam / tat samayena eva kṛtam iti / na ayogye samayaḥ
11318 samartha iti yogyatā tat-sambandhaś cet / tat kiṃ vai śabdaḥ
11319 sambandho astu / samarthaṃ hi rūpaṃ śabdasya yogyatā kārya-
11320 kāraṇa-yogyatā-vat / sā ced artha-antaraṃ kiṃ śabdasya iti sambandho
11321 vācyaḥ / yogyatā-upakāra iti cet / na / nityāyāḥ niratiśayatvāt /
11322 tatra apy atiprasaṅgāt upakāra-asiddheḥ / yogyatāyāṃ ca svato yogyatve
11323 artha eva kiṃ na iṣyate / samayas tarhi kathaṃ śabda-artha-
11324 sambandhāḥ / puruṣeṣu vṛtteḥ / na amiśrāṇāṃ siddhānāṃ kaścit
11325 sambandho abheda-prasaṅgāt anapekṣaṇāc ca / artha-viśeṣa-samīha-
11326 apreritā vāg ata idam iti viduṣaḥ sva-nidāna-ābhāsinam arthaṃ
11327 sūcayati iti buddhi-rūpa-vāg vijñaptyor janyajanakabhāvaḥ sambandhaḥ
11401 tataḥ śabdāt pratipattir avinābhāvāt / tad-ākhyānaṃ
11402 samayaḥ / tataḥ pratyāyaka-sambandha-siddheḥ sambandha-ākhyānāt /
11403 na tu sa eva sambandhaḥ / astu vā anya eva nityaḥ sambandhaḥ /
11404 tena
11405 girām eka-artha-niyame na syād artha-antare gatiḥ//
children.translated_text: For a connection, even if existing, does not cause cognition when unmanifested. But convention manifests it. [Reply:] Then, since [convention] already accomplishes [the task] on its own, why is a causeless [connection] to be nourished? [Objection:] But the function of the connection is precisely the generation of the cognition of meaning—and that is accomplished by convention alone. [Reply:] Convention is not effective regarding what is unfit—if [you say] the fitness is that connection, then what [need for] the word? Let the connection itself be [a word]. For the effective form of the word is its fitness—like the fitness of cause and effect. If that [fitness] is something different—why should what belongs to the word be called a 'connection'? [Objection:] It benefits the fitness. [Reply:] No—because what is permanent admits no additional qualification. And because of over-extension there too, the benefit is not established. And if the fitness has fitness inherently, why is it not accepted as being the meaning itself? Then how are convention, word, meaning, and connection [related]? [They operate] through the practice of persons. There is no connection of unmixed established [entities]—because of the absurd consequence of identity and because of non-dependence. Speech, impelled by the desire for a specific meaning, indicates to the knower 'this is that'—manifesting the meaning that reflects its own cause—thus the produced-producer relation between cognition-form speech and notification is the connection. From that word, cognition [arises] because of inseparability. The declaration of that is convention. Therefrom, since the connection with the means of conveying is established through the declaration of the connection, [convention is] not that connection itself. Or let there be a different, permanent connection. Through that—

children.text:
11406 na hi tena sambandhena asambaddhe arthe pratītir yuktā / tasya
11407 vaiphalya-prasaṅgāt / dṛṣṭaś ca icchā-vaśāt kṛta-samayaḥ sarvaḥ
11408 sarvasya dīpakaḥ /
children.translated_text: everyone would be an illuminator of everything.

children.text: 11409 aneka-artha-abhisambandhe viruddha-vyakti-sambhavaḥ //228 //
children.translated_text: When [there is] connection with multiple meanings, the occurrence of contradictory manifestations [would result]. //228//

For cognition would not be reasonable regarding a meaning not connected through that connection—because [the connection] would be rendered fruitless. And it is observed that all [meanings] are established through conventions made at will.

children.text:
11410 atha mā bhūd dṛṣṭa-virodha iti sarve sarvasya vācakāḥ / tathā na
11411 sarvaḥ sarva-sādhano asaṃkarāt kāryakāraṇatāyāḥ / tatra pratiniyata-
11412 sādhane abhimate arthe sarva-sādhya-sādhana-sādhāraṇasya
11413 śabdasya-iṣṭa-vyaktim eva samayakāraḥ karoti iti kuta etat so aniyato
11414 niyamaṃ puruṣāt pratipadyate / tadā /
11415 apauruṣeyatāyāś ca vyarthā syāt parikalpanā//
children.translated_text: Or, lest there be contradiction with what is observed, let every [word] denote everything. Likewise, not everything is the means of producing everything—because of the non-mixture of the cause-effect relation. There, regarding the intended object with a restricted means of production, the convention-maker establishes the desired manifestation of a word that is common to all objects to be proved and their means of proof—whence [is it known that] the unrestricted [word] receives its restriction from a person? Then the imagination of authorlessness would be pointless. //

children.text:
11416 api nāma asaṃkīrṇam arthaṃ jānīyām iti saṃkara-hetuḥ puruṣa-upākīrṇaḥ /
11417 tatra yādṛśāḥ puruṣaiḥ kvacit prayuktāḥ saṃkīryante
11418 tādṛśā eva sarva-sādhāraṇāḥ santaḥ kvacit tair viniyamitās
11419 tattva-aparijñānāt / prakṛtyā eva vaidikā niyatā iti cet / na upadeśam
11420 apekṣeran na anyathā saṃketena prakāśayeyuḥ vyākhyā-vikalpaś
11421 ca na syāt / upadeśasya ca iṣṭa-saṃvādaḥ śakya-vikalpe na asti iti
11422 vyarthā eva apauruṣeyatā /
children.translated_text: authorlessness is entirely pointless.

children.text: 11423 vācyaś ca hetur bhinnānāṃ sambandhasya vyavasthiteḥ //229 //
children.translated_text: And the cause of the established connection of different [words and meanings] must be stated. //229//

[Objection:] 'May I know the unmixed meaning'—[thus the convention-maker], who is the cause of mixture, is contaminated by persons. [Reply:] In that case, those very [words] which, when employed by persons somewhere, become mixed—those same [words], though common to all, when restricted by them [to specific meanings] elsewhere, [are restricted] due to not fully understanding their nature. [Objection:] The Vedic [words] are naturally restricted. [Reply:] Then they would not depend on instruction, they would not illuminate otherwise through convention, and there would be no possibility of varying interpretation. And the desired correspondence of instruction does not exist when varying interpretation is possible—therefore

children.text:
11425 arthā hi bāhyā na rūpaṃ śabdasya na śabdo arthānām / yena abhinna-
11426 ātmatayā vyavasthā-bhede api nāntarīyakatā syāt / kṛtakatva-
11427 anityatva-vat / na apy ete vivakṣā-janmāno dhvanayo ajanmāno
11428 vā vivakṣā-vyaṅgyāḥ na artha-āyattāḥ / tataḥ katham idānīṃ
11501 tat-pratiniyama-saṃsādhyaṃ tad-anvayaṃ sādhayeyuḥ / na hy
11502 apratibaddhas tat-sādhana iti /
11503 asaṃskāryatayā pumbhiḥ sarvathā syān nirarthatā//
children.translated_text: For external objects are not the form of words, nor are words [the form] of objects. By which [means], through having an undifferentiated nature, even when there is a difference of establishment, inseparability would hold—like being-produced and being-impermanent. Nor are these sounds, born of the desire to speak, unborn [yet] manifested by the desire to speak, [nor are they] dependent on objects. Then how could they establish the positive concomitance to be accomplished by their restriction to those [objects]? For what is not necessarily connected is not the means of establishing that. If [they are] not conditionable by persons at all, there would be complete meaninglessness. //

children.text: 11504 saṃskāra-upagame mukhyaṃ gaja-snānam idaṃ bhavet //230//
children.translated_text: If conditioning is accepted, this [authorlessness] would be a principal [case of] bathing an elephant. //230//

children.text:
11505 iti saṃgrahaślokaḥ / api ca / śabda-arthayoḥ sambandho nityo vā
11506 syād anityo vā / yady anityaḥ puruṣa-icchā vṛttir avṛttir vā / apuruṣa-
11507 adhīnatve puruṣāṇāṃ yathā abhiprāyaṃ deśa-ādi-parāvṛttyā tena
11508 pratipādanaṃ na syāt / icchāyām apy anāyattasya kadācid ayogāt /
11509 parvata-ādi-vat / ayam eva nityatve api doṣas tasya sthira-rūpasya
11510 parāvṛtty-ayogād iti samaṃ sarva-avasthāne api iṣṭa-pratiniyama-abhāvāt /
11511 tato viśeṣa-pratipattir na syād iti pūrvavat prasaṅgaḥ /
11512 icchā-vṛttau ca pauruṣeyatvam iti vipralambha-āśaṅkā / api ca /
11513 sambandhinām anityatvān na sambandhe asti nityatā /
11514 parāśrayo hi sambandho apratibandhe tayoḥ sambandhitā ayogāt /
11515 sa ca āśrayo anityaḥ / apāye asya sambandhasya apy apāyaḥ anyathā anāśritaḥ
11516 syāt / tato na nityaḥ / tad-āśraya-arthaś ca vaktavyaḥ /
11517 nityasya anupakāryatvāt / anupakurvāṇaś ca anāśrayaḥ / jāter vācyatvād
11518 adoṣa iti cet / na / tad-vacane prayojana-abhāvād iti nirloṭhitam

11520 vāciṣu sarvadā jāti-codane viśeṣa-antara-vyudāsena pravṛtty-ayogāc
11521 ca / tasmād anvaya-vyatirekiṇo bhāvasya bhāva-abhāvau sambandhaḥ /
11523 arthair ataḥ sa śabdānāṃ saṃskāryaḥ puruṣair dhiyā //231 /
11524 tāv eva bhāva-abhāvāv āśritya-asaṃsṛṣṭāv api saṃsṛṣṭāv iva puruṣasya
11601 vyavahāra-bhāvanātaḥ pratibhāta iti pauruṣeyo bhāvānāṃ
11602 saṃśleṣaḥ / kiṃ ca āśraya-vināśān naṣṭe sambandhe sa śabdaḥ punar
11603 asambandhatvān na apūrveṇa yojyeta / utpanna-utpannāś ca bhāvāḥ
11604 sthita-sambandha-abhāvād asambandhino avācyāḥ syuḥ / tatra
11605 api /
11606 arthair eva saha utpāde /
11607 kalpyamāne
11608 na svabhāva-viparyayaḥ /
11609 śabdeṣu yuktaḥ /
11610 atha mā bhūn naṣṭa-sambandhasya śabdasya artha-antare vaiguṇyaṃ
11611 arthānāṃ ca avācyatā ity utpanno arthaḥ sambandhavān yady utpadyeta
11612 sa sambandha utpanno api na śabde syāt / tasya tena asambandhi-
11613 svabhāvasya svabhāva-viparyayam antareṇa tad-bhāva-ayogāt /
11614 arthena saha utpannasya anyataḥ siddhasya anupakāriṇi śabde
11615 asamāśrayāc ca / tasya api tadutpatti-sahakāritve samarthasya nitya-utpādana-
11616 prasaṅgaḥ / anapekṣatvān nityasya anupakārāt / asāmarthye
11617 api paścād api svabhāva-atyāgād aśaktiḥ /
children.translated_text: even afterward, because [the word] does not abandon its nature, there is incapacity.

children.text: 11618 sambandhe na ayaṃ doṣo vikalpite //232//
children.translated_text: There is no fault in this when the connection is imagined [conventionally]. //232//

This is a summary verse. Moreover—the connection between word and meaning would be either permanent or impermanent. If impermanent—[it operates through] human will, presence or absence [of the connection]. If not person-dependent, the demonstration [of meaning] by persons according to their intention, through reversal from place and the like, through that [connection], would not be [possible]. Because [something] not dependent on will is sometimes impossible—like a mountain and the like. This same fault [applies] even if permanent—because something of fixed nature cannot be reversed—thus equally, even in all circumstances, there is an absence of the desired restriction. Therefore, specific cognition would not [arise]—and the same absurd consequence as before [follows]. And if [the connection] operates through will, [there is] person-dependence—hence the suspicion of deception. Moreover— Because the connected [terms] are impermanent, there is no permanence in the connection. For a connection depends on another [i.e., on its terms]—because without a necessary connection between those two, there can be no state of being connected. And that substrate is impermanent. When it perishes, the connection too perishes—otherwise it would be without a substrate. Therefore it is not permanent. And the purpose of a substrate for it must be stated—because what is permanent cannot be benefited. And what does not benefit has no substrate. [Objection:] There is no fault, because it is expressible through the universal. [Reply:] No—because there is no purpose in expressing it—this has been thoroughly examined. And because universals are impossible everywhere, [this] is inapplicable to the arbitrary, particular-denoting [Vedic words]; and because when universals are always charged, operation through the exclusion of other particularities would be impossible. Therefore, the connection of an entity that has positive and negative concomitance is the presence and absence of the entity. Therefore that [connection] of words is to be conditioned by persons through cognition. //231// Resting upon precisely those presence and absence [of entities], which, though unconjoined, appear as if conjoined through the person's habituated conventional practice—thus the conjunction of entities is person-made. Moreover—when the connection is destroyed through the destruction of the substrate, that word, being again unconnected, would not be joined with a new [meaning]. And entities that arise again and again, in the absence of a permanent connection, would be unconnected and inexpressible. There too—

children.text:
11619 na hi bhāva-śleṣa-apekṣī puruṣa-bhāvanā-pratibhāsī tad-apekṣa-alakṣaṇaḥ
11620 sambandhaḥ / so ayam nityānām apy aparāvartayan svabhāvaṃ
11621 kutaścit svayam utprekṣya ghaṭayed iti te api tathā
11622 syuḥ / na ca cyavana-dharmāṇaḥ / yad uktam āśraya-apāyena āśrita-
11623 sambandha-vināśād anityaḥ sa iti tatra /
children.translated_text: that [connection] is impermanent because of the destruction of the connection that depends on the substrate through the perishing of the substrate—

children.text: 11624 nityatvād āśraya-apāye apy anāśo yadi jāti-vat /
children.translated_text: if, even when the substrate perishes, [the connection] does not perish because of permanence, like the universal—

children.text: 11625 nityeṣv āśraya-sāmarthyaṃ kiṃ yena iṣṭaḥ sa āśrayaḥ //233//
children.translated_text: what capacity of the substrate [is there] for permanent [things], by which that [substrate] is desired as a substrate? //233//

For the connection that is not dependent on the conjunction of entities, that appears through the habituated practice of a person, is not characterized by dependence on that [real conjunction]. This [connection], not reversing the nature of even permanent [entities], could itself, having been conceived from somewhere, conjoin [them]—and thus they too would be [connected]. And they do not have the nature of perishing. As for what was said—'it is impermanent because of the destruction of the dependent connection through the perishing of the substrate'—regarding that:

children.text:
11626 śrūyata etan nityā jātir āśrayitā ca na apy āśrayeṇa saha naśyati iti /
11627 kevalaṃ nityeṣv āśraya-sāmarthyaṃ na paśyāmaḥ yena asāv āśrayaḥ /
11628 kṛtasya karaṇa-abhāvād akārakasya ca anapekṣatvāt / vyaktir
11629 upakāro jāteḥ sambandhasya ca āśrayāt tena āśraya iti cet
children.translated_text: [Objection:] The particular is the benefit of the universal, and because of the connection's substrate—therefore [it is called] a substrate. If so—

children.text: 11701 jñāna-utpādana-hetūnāṃ sambandhāt sahakāriṇām /
children.translated_text: Because of the connection with cooperating conditions that are causes of generating cognition,

children.text: 11702 tad-utpādana-yogyatvena utpattir vyaktir iṣyate //234//
children.translated_text: origination as fitness for generating that [cognition] is accepted as manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>). //234//

It is heard that the universal is permanent and is substratum-dependent, yet does not perish along with the substratum. But we do not see any capacity of the substrate for permanent [things] by which it would be a substrate—because of the absence of a producer for what is [already] produced, and because what does not produce is not depended upon.

children.text: 11703 ghaṭa-ādiṣv api yukti-jñair aviśeṣe avikāriṇām /
children.translated_text: Even in [the case of] pots and the like, by those who know reasoning—when there is no difference for what is unmodifiable,

children.text: 11704 vyañjakaiḥ svaiḥ kutaḥ ko artho vyaktās tais te yato matāḥ //235 //
children.translated_text: what purpose [is there] with their own manifestors, [since] they are considered manifested by them from which [source]? //235//

11805 tat-kāryasya eva jñānasya abhāvāt / na hi tatra śabda-rūpam

11809 artha-pratipādanam api śabdānām animittaṃ kiṃ na iṣyate / tasmāt

11812 siddhy-artha-pratīter na kaścit sampradāyam apekṣeta / sampradāya-

11819 sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: And if <s>sambandha</s> (relation) were a real entity, there would be diversity of cognition due to difference.

children.text: 11820 tābhyām abhede tāv eva na ato anyā vastuno gatiḥ //236//
children.translated_text: If [relation] is non-different from those two [relata], then they alone [exist]; there is no other status of the entity beyond that. //236//

The <s>abhivyakti</s> (manifestation) of pots and so forth is nothing but the arising, from the auxiliary cause, of a subsequent moment capable of generating cognition, which depends on the material cause. Otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence of producing cognition without depending on that auxiliary contribution. And because what produces the capacity is the generator; and because that [capacity] is of the same nature as it; and if it were something different, there would be the unwanted consequence of the entity providing no assistance, and since cognition would arise from mere capacity, there would be the unwanted consequence of perpetual non-apprehension of pots and so forth, and the unwanted consequence of apprehension without depending on light, because what requires no dependence provides no assistance to the self. Therefore, these [objects], depending on something else for generating cognition of their own domain, thereby acquire an excellence of their own nature. Hence they are produced by it. But since they do not establish the form of the knowable, through the power of cognition they are made known—'manifested'—by a word that expresses the excellence of the effect, for the purpose of indicating a distinction. In this way, <s>jāti</s> (universal), <s>sambandha</s> (relation), and the like, since they cannot be assisted in any way whatsoever, cannot be rightly said to be manifested by something that provides no assistance.

children.text:
11821 rūpa-bheda-nibandhanatvād vyavasthā-antarasya tad-rūpaṃ tad eva
11822 syāt / dharma-bhedas tu syāt pūrva-ukta-krameṇa / sa ca aviruddha
11823 eva na vastu-bhedaḥ / na ca bheda-abhedau muktvā vastuno anyā
11824 gatiḥ / tasya rūpa-lakṣaṇatvād / rūpasya ca etad-vikalpa-anativṛtteḥ /
11825 api ca /
11826 bhinnatvād vastu-rūpasya sambandhaḥ kalpanā-kṛtaḥ /
11827 ity uktaṃ prāk / na hi śleṣa-lakṣaṇaḥ sambandho aśliṣṭeṣu padārtheṣu
11828 sambhavati / na ca artha-antaram eṣāṃ sambandhaḥ / yasmāt
11901 sad-dravyaṃ syāt para-adhīnaṃ sambandho anyasya vā katham //237 //
children.translated_text: Since the distinction [of relation] is grounded in difference of form, that form would be identical with those [relata]. There may be a difference of properties in the manner previously stated, but that is not contradictory and does not constitute a difference of entity. And apart from difference and non-difference, there is no other status of an entity, because it is defined by its form, and because form does not go beyond this pair of alternatives. Moreover—

children.text:
11903 na hi siddhaṃ sat param apekṣate / na anapekṣaḥ svatantraḥ sambandhaḥ /
11904 dravyam iti ca svabhāva ucyate / sa kathaṃ parabhāvasya
11905 śleṣaḥ syāt / na hi svabhāva-antara-sattayā anyaḥ śliṣṭo nāma /
11906 mā bhūd aśliṣṭena śliṣṭena tu syād iti cet / na / tasya eva
11907 tābhyāṃ śleṣa-asiddheḥ sa eva asiddho yas tau śleṣayet / tad ayam
11908 atiprasaṅgo yady arthāv artha-antareṇa śliṣyato viśeṣa-abhāvāt / kiṃ

children.translated_text: If the relation were an established substance, it would depend on another; or how could a relation belong to something else? //237//

children.text: 11910 varṇā nirarthakāḥ santaḥ pada-ādi parikalpitam /
children.translated_text: For what is already established does not depend on another. A relation that is independent [of relata] is not [a relation]. And 'substance' means 'own nature.' How could that be a conjunction of what belongs to another? For one is not 'conjoined' with another merely by the existence of a different own nature. [Objection:] Let it not be conjoined with something unconjoined, but let it be so with something conjoined. [Reply:] No, because the conjunction of that very [relation] with those two is itself unestablished. That very [relation] which would conjoin those two is itself unestablished. This leads to infinite regress if two entities are conjoined through a third entity, since there is no distinguishing feature [to stop it]. Furthermore—

children.text: 11911 avastuni kathaṃ vṛttiḥ sambandhasya asya vastunaḥ //238//
children.translated_text: <s>Varṇas</s> (phonemes), being meaningless in themselves, and <s>pada</s> (words) and so forth being conceptually constructed—

Because the nature of a real entity is differentiated, <s>sambandha</s> (relation) is a product of conceptual construction—so it was stated earlier. For a relation characterized as conjunction is not possible among things that are not conjoined. Nor is the relation of these [word and meaning] something different [from them]. Because—

children.text:
11912 vācako hi vacana-aṅgena tadvān syāt / santo apy avācakā varṇāḥ /
11913 tan na teṣu vācyavācakasambandhaḥ / tad-vṛttau svarūpa-hāni-
11914 prasaṅgāt / krama-viśeṣeṇa vācakā varṇā iti cet / na / kramasya anartha-
11915 antaratvena abhedakatvāt / tad-rūpasya krama-antare apy aviśeṣāt
11916 tulyā syāt pratipattiḥ / arthāntaratvam api kramasya niṣetsyāmaḥ /
11917 tad asati varṇānāṃ vācakatve pada-ādi vācakaṃ syāt /
11918 tac ca na kiṃcid vyatireka-avyatireka-virodhāt / tasmād indriya-
11919 vijñāna-viśeṣa-anubandhī sabhāga-vāsanā-upādāna -vikalpa-pratibhāsa-vibhramaḥ
11920 padam / vākyaṃ ca eka-avabhāsi mithyā eva / eka-anekatva-
11921 ayogāt / na hy ekam / anekayā buddhyā krameṇa grahaṇa-ayogāt /
11922 na ca tad ekayā grāhyaṃ varṇa-anukrama-grahaṇāt / eka-varṇa-
11923 grahaṇa-kāle ca aneka-buddhi-vyatikramāt / kṣaṇikatvāt buddhīnām /
11924 kṣaṇasya eka-paramāṇu-vyatikrama-kālatvāt / ādhikye vibhāgavataḥ
11925 paryavasāna-ayogāt / aneka-aṇu-vyatyaya-nimeṣa-tulyakālatvād
11926 antya-varṇa-parisamāpteḥ / yathā-anubhavaṃ smaraṇāt
11927 smṛtir api tat-kāla eva / anubhava-smaraṇa-anukramayor viśeṣa-anupalakṣaṇatvāc
11928 ca / na apy anekaṃ pada-ādi / abheda-pratibhāsanād buddhes
11929 tad-anekatvasya niṣetsyamānatvāc ca / tan na vastu / tasya
11930 etad-vikalpa-anatikramāt / vastu ca sambandhaḥ / sa kathaṃ
12001 tad-āśrayaḥ syāt / āśrayanīya-ayogāt / anāśrito hy evaṃ syāt /
12002 tathā ca asambandhaḥ / tasmān na svābhāvikaḥ śabda-arthayoḥ
12003 sambandhaḥ / tad-abhiprāyasya prayogād utpanno abhivyakto
12004 vā śabdo tad-avyabhicārī iti tattvam asya sambandhaḥ / sā ca utpattir
12005 abhivyaktir vā avyabhicāra-āśrayaḥ pauruṣeyī iti pauruṣeya eva
12006 sambandhas tad-dvāreṇa ca artha-pratyāyane aniyamaḥ śabdānām
12007 ity apauruṣeyatve api sa eva vipralambhaḥ /
children.translated_text: For what is expressive would be so through a component of expression. Phonemes, though existent, are non-expressive. Therefore, there is no signifier-signified relation (<s>vācyavācakasambandha</s>) in them, because if it resided there, there would be the unwanted consequence of the loss of their own form. [Objection:] Phonemes are expressive through a particular sequence. [Reply:] No, because sequence, not being a different entity, is not a differentiator, and since that form is not different in another sequence either, the cognition would be the same. We shall also refute the claim that sequence is a separate entity. Therefore, in the absence of expressiveness in phonemes, <s>pada</s> (words) and so forth would be the expressive [units]. But those too are nothing real, because of the contradiction between being excluded [from reality] and not being excluded. Therefore, the word is a mistaken appearance in a conceptual construction whose material cause is a latent impression of the same class, connected with a particular sensory cognition. And a sentence, appearing as a unity, is entirely false—because it cannot be either one or many. For it is not one, since it cannot be grasped in a single act by the multiple cognitions [of its parts] occurring in sequence. Nor can it be grasped by a single cognition, since the phonemes are grasped in sequence. And at the time of grasping a single phoneme, multiple cognitions are excluded, because cognitions are momentary, and because a moment is the time for the displacement of a single atom. When there are more [atoms], there can be no completion for what has parts, since the time for the displacement of multiple atoms equals the duration of a blink, [which corresponds to] the completion of the final phoneme. Because memory follows experience as it occurred, the memory too [arises] at that very time. And because one cannot discern a difference between the sequences of experience and memory. Nor is the word and so forth a plurality, because cognition appears as non-different, and because we shall refute the plurality of that [cognition]. Therefore it is not a real entity, since it does not go beyond this pair of alternatives. And <s>sambandha</s> (relation) is a real entity. How then could it have its locus in that [unreal word]? Because it is not fit to be a locus. For thus it would be without a locus, and consequently there would be no relation. Therefore, there is no natural relation between word and meaning. The truth about this relation is that a word, produced or manifested by one who intends that [meaning], is invariably associated with that [meaning]—that is the <s>avinābhāva</s> (invariable concomitance) called its relation. And that production or manifestation, which is the basis of invariable concomitance, is of human origin (<s>pauruṣeya</s>)—therefore the relation itself is of human origin, and through that, words have no fixed restriction in conveying meaning.

children.text: 12008 apauruṣeyatā api iṣṭā kartṛṛṇām asmṛteḥ kila /
children.translated_text: Thus, even [if one posits] <s>apauruṣeyatva</s> (authorlessness), that same deception [remains].

children.text: 12009 yā api iyam apauruṣeyatā veda-vākyānāṃ kartur asmaraṇād varṇyate /
children.translated_text: The <s>apauruṣeyatā</s> (authorlessness) [of Vedic sentences] is also maintained on the grounds that their authors are not remembered.

children.text: 12011 santy asya apy anuvaktāra iti dhig vyāpakaṃ tamaḥ //239//
children.translated_text: This very [doctrine] too has those who repeat it—alas for the all-pervading darkness! //239//
how can this real relation have its locus in something unreal? //238//

children.text:
12012 tasya eva tāvad īdṛśaṃ prajñā-skhalitaṃ kathaṃ vṛttam iti savismaya-
12013 anukampaṃ naś cetaḥ / tad apare apy anuvadanti iti nirdaya-
12014 ākrānta-bhuvanaṃ dhig vyāpakaṃ tamaḥ / kaḥ prāṇino hita-īpsā-
12015 vipralabdhasya aparādhaḥ / tathā hi smaranti saugatā mantrāṇāṃ
12016 kartṛṛn aṣṭaka-ādīn / hiraṇyagarbhaṃ ca kāṇādāḥ / teṣāṃ
12017 sa mithyā-vāda iti cet / ka idānīm evaṃ pauruṣeyo anyo api /
12018 kumārasambhava-ādiṣv ātmānam anyaṃ vā praṇetāram upadiśanto
12019 yad evaṃ prativyūhyeran / tatra prativahane abhyupeta-
12020 bādhā iti cet / nanv idam eva abhyupagama-aṅgam iti kasya bādhā /
12021 tat parasya api tulyam eva / tasya iṣṭatvād adoṣa iti cet / kuto asya iyam
12022 iṣṭir apramāṇikā prāg āsīt / akasmād grāhī ca ayaṃ kiṃ punaḥ
12023 kvacit sādhanam apekṣate / yat pauruṣeya-apauruṣeya-cintayā
12024 ātmānam āyāsayati / tata eva iṣṭer anabhyupeta-bādhāyāṃ tad-anyasya
12025 api tulyam ity anupālambhaḥ / anatiśaya-darśī ca ayaṃ
12026 vākyeṣv evaṃprakārāṇām apauruṣeyatva-sādhanānāṃ kārya-dharmāṇāṃ
12101 vā kvacid atiśayam abhyupeta ity apratyaya eva asya vṛttiḥ /
12102 dṛśyante ca vicchinna-kriyā-sampradāyāḥ kṛtakāś ca / tān yatnavanta
12103 upalabhanta iti cet / na / niyama-abhāvāt / anyatra anupalambhasya
12104 upalambhasya vā para-upadeśād apratyayād aniścaya-arthatvāt /
12105 svayaṃ-kṛtānām apy apahnotṛ-darśanāt / niṣṭhā-gamanasya
12106 aśakyatvāt /
children.translated_text: is impossible.

children.text: 12107 yathā ayam anyato aśrutvā na imaṃ varṇa-pada-kramam /
children.translated_text: Just as this [person], not having heard from another, is not able to utter this particular sequence of phonemes and words,

children.text: 12108 vaktuṃ samarthaḥ puruṣas tathā anyo api iti kaścana //240//
children.translated_text: so too another [person is unable]—so [argues] a certain one. //240//

First, that such a lapse of intelligence occurred in him [the original proponent]—our mind [responds] with wonder and pity. That others too repeat it—alas for the all-pervading darkness that mercilessly engulfs the world! What is the fault of a living being deceived in its desire for benefit? For the Buddhists remember the authors of <s>mantras</s>—the <s>Aṣṭakas</s> and others. And the <s>Kāṇādas</s> [remember] <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. [Objection:] Their statement is false. [Reply:] Then who now [proves] that this other [Veda] too is of human origin? If those who indicate themselves or another as the author in the <s>Kumārasambhava</s> and other [works] were to be refuted in the same way— [Objection:] In refuting that, there would be a contradiction with what is accepted. [Reply:] But this very [claim of authorlessness] is a component of what is accepted—so whose [position] is contradicted? That is equally [a problem] for the other side too. [Objection:] Because it is accepted [by us], there is no fault. [Reply:] Where did this groundless acceptance of his come from in the first place? And if he accepts [things] without any reason, why does he ever require a proof for anything? Why does he trouble himself with the investigation of whether [the Veda is] of human or non-human origin? Since that acceptance itself [is groundless], when there is no contradiction with what is accepted, the same applies to the other [side] too—so there is no ground for reproach. And this one, seeing no excellence in statements of such a kind—among the proofs of authorlessness or among properties [that are] effects—has accepted excellence somewhere [arbitrarily], so his conduct is simply untrustworthy. And [texts] are seen whose tradition of practice has been interrupted and which are [clearly] composed. [Objection:] People found them with effort. [Reply:] No, because there is no invariable rule [about this], because non-perception elsewhere or perception [elsewhere] through another's instruction is untrustworthy and inconclusive in meaning, because even of self-composed [works] deniers are seen, and because reaching a final conclusion

children.text:
12109 tasya api tad eva uttaram evam apauruṣeyatve api kim idānīṃ pauruṣeyam
12110 ity ādi / tathā hi /
12111 anyo vā racito granthaḥ sampradāyād ṛte paraiḥ /
children.translated_text: What other text, composed by others without a tradition,

children.text: 12112 dṛṣṭaḥ ko abhihito yena so apy evaṃ na anumīyate //241//
children.translated_text: has been seen, on account of which that [Veda] too would be inferred [to have an author] in the same way? //241//
To that too, the same reply [applies]: even if [the Veda is] authorless, what then—is it [therefore] of human origin? and so forth. Namely—

children.text:
12113 na khalu kiṃcid anyad apauruṣeyatva-āśrayo anyatra idānīntanānām
12114 anupadeśa-pāṭha-aśakteḥ / sā ca anyatra apy ekena racite granthe anyasya
12115 tulyā / tad-anusāriṇā sarvas tathā unneyo na vā kaścit / tasya
12116 tathā aniṣṭatvād ity ādāv apy uktam iṣṭes tad-āśrayatvād ity ādi /
children.translated_text: that is not desired by him—this was stated at the beginning: 'because acceptance is the basis for that,' and so forth.

children.text: 12117 api ca /
children.translated_text: Moreover—

children.text: 12118 yaj-jātīyo yataḥ siddhaḥ sa tasmād agni-kāṣṭha-vat /
children.translated_text: Whatever is of the same kind as what is established from a certain [source], that [is inferred] from it, like fire and firewood.

children.text: 12119 adṛṣṭa-hetur anyo apy aviśiṣṭaḥ sampratīyate //242//
children.translated_text: Even another whose cause is unseen is understood to be no different [in kind]. //242//

Indeed, there is no other basis for [claiming] authorlessness anywhere besides the inability of present-day people to recite without instruction. And that [inability] is equally [present] elsewhere too, when a text has been composed by one person and another [tries to recite it]. Therefore, everyone should be inferred [to have a human author] in the same way, or no one at all. Since

children.text:
12120 na adarśanād hetur ahetuko nāma / adṛṣṭa-hetavo api hi bhāvās
12121 tad-anyaiḥ svabhāva-abhedam anubhavantas tathāvidhāḥ samunnīyante /
12122 hetu-rūpa-nivṛttāv api tad-rūpam anivṛttaṃ kārya-dharma-
12123 vyatikramān na tataḥ syād iti na kaścit tathā vacanīyaḥ /
12124 rūpa-viśeṣo vā tathā darśanīyo ya enaṃ hetum anuvidadhyāt / yena iṣṭa-
12125 aniṣṭayor iṣṭa-viparyayo na syāt / svabhāva-nivṛtteś ca hetor
12126 abhedane bhāvānāṃ bhedaḥ syād ākasmika iti na kvacid vinivarteta /
12127 tasmād yaḥ svabhāvo yaj-janmā dṛṣṭaḥ so anyatra apy avibhajyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever has been observed to have a certain nature and to have arisen from a certain [source], that same [thing], being undifferentiated elsewhere too,

children.text: 12128 svātmanā tat-kārya-dharmatāṃ na ativartate agni-indhana-vat /
children.translated_text: does not go beyond the status of being an effect of that [same cause], by its own nature—like fire and fuel.

children.text: 12201 tatra apradarśya ye bhedaṃ kārya-sāmānya-darśanāt /
children.translated_text: Those who, without demonstrating a difference therein, from the mere observation of a general effect-property

children.text: 12202 hetavaḥ pravitanyante sarve te vyabhicāriṇaḥ //243//
children.translated_text: extend [their] reasons [to all cases]—all of them are deviant [in their reasoning]. //243//

A cause is not 'causeless' merely because it is not seen. For even entities whose causes are unseen, when they are experienced as having no difference in nature from others [of the same kind], are inferred to be of that same kind. Even when the form of the cause has ceased, the form [of the effect] does not cease—no one should say that it would not be so because of deviation from the properties of the effect. Or else a distinguishing feature of form must be shown that would track back to this cause, so that the desired and undesired [cases] would not be reversed. And if the nature of the cause does not cease, the differentiation among entities would be causeless, and so would never be arrested anywhere.

12203 yathā-adyo api pathika-kṛto agnir jvālā-antara-pūrvako na araṇi-nirmathana-
12204 pūrvakaḥ / pathika-agnitvāt / anantara-agni-vad iti / kathaṃ
12205 punaḥ pathika-agner vyabhicāraḥ / jvālā-udbhava-sāmarthyaṃ hy
12206 āśritya dahanasya hetv-antaraṃ pratikṣipyate / yadi hi vinā jvālayā
12207 syād anyatra api syād iti / tatra jvālā-itara-janmanor abādhyabādhakatve
12208 jvālā-aprabhavatvam anyathā api syād iti dharmayor
12209 ekatra arthe sambhavāt sa pathika-agnir anyo vā artha eka-pratiniyato
12210 na syād ity āśaṅkyate vyabhicāraḥ / so apy anyonya-vyatirekī
12211 dharma-dvaya-avatāro vastu-sāmānye aviruddha ity ucyate na avasthā-
12212 bhedini viśeṣe / niṣkalasya ātmanas tad-atattva-virodhāt / na ca

12214 vyatirekeṇa asambhava-abhāvāt / evaṃbhūtaḥ pathika-agnir

12309 tattva-lakṣaṇo asty eva viśeṣaḥ / satyam asti / na kevalaṃ
12310 tayor eva / kiṃ tarhi / ḍiṇḍika-purāṇa-itarayor api / na ca sva-prakriyā-

12318 satya-adhiṣṭhāna-balā viṣa-dahana-ādi-stambhana-darśanāt /
12319 śabarāṇāṃ ca keṣāṃcid adya api mantra-karaṇāt / avaidikānāṃ

12324 tat katham ekatra viruddha-abhidhāyi dvayam satyaṃ
12325 syāt / tatra artha-antara-kalpane tad anyatra api tulyam ity artha-anirṇayāt
12326 kvacid apratipattiḥ / tathā ca sad apy anupayogam apauruṣeyam /
12327 bauddha-ādīnām amantratve tad-anyatra api koṣa-pānaṃ
12328 syāt karaṇīyam / viṣa-karma-adhikṛto bauddhā api dṛśyante / tatra amantratvam

12405 idānīṃ satya-prabhavau mantra-kalpau paraspara-virodhinau / na

12407 lakṣaṇāv api tau staḥ / sa prabhāvo gati-siddhi-viśeṣābhyām api
12408 syāt / yadi pauruṣeyā mantrāḥ kiṃ na sarve puruṣā mantra-kāriṇaḥ /

12422 pratiroddhā / bādhya-adṛṣṭer bādhyabādhakabhāva-asiddheḥ / etena

12501 adhyayanād iti cet / ukta-uttaram etat / adarśanād
