children.translated_text: Therefore there exists someone of extraordinary [power], and the arguments for rejecting this have also been refuted.

children.text: 16413 buddhi-indriya-ukti-puṃstva-ādi sādhanaṃ yat tu varṇyate /
children.translated_text: Intelligence, sense-faculties, speech, masculinity, and the like—whatever is stated as proof [against an extraordinary person],

children.text: 16414 pramāṇa-ābhaṃ yathārthā asti na hi śeṣavato gatiḥ //311//
children.translated_text: it merely resembles a valid means of knowledge; for there is no definitive understanding of what has a remainder. //311//

children.text:
16415 yat tu buddhi-indriya-vacana-yogāt puṃstvād iti puruṣa-atiśaya-pratikṣepa-
16416 sādhanaṃ tat tv agamakam eva / pratikṣepa-sāmānya-
16417 sādhanayor asambhavāt / na hy atīndriyeṣv atad-darśinaḥ pratikṣepaḥ
16418 sambhavati / satām apy eṣām ajñānāt / ata eva virodha-asiddheḥ /
16419 avirodhinā ca saha sambhava-avirodhād ity apy uktam /
16420 na api itara-sāmānya-siddhir viśeṣa-asambhavasya jñātum aśakyatvāt /
16421 īdṛśeṣu ca anupalabdher hetutva-pratikṣepāt / puṃstva-ādi-sāmye
16422 api kasyacid viśeṣasya darśanāt / sambhavad-viśeṣe ca sāmya-asiddhir
16423 ity uktam / tasmāc śeṣavad anumānam etat / vyatirekasya
16424 sandehād asamartham adarśane api vipakṣa-vṛtteḥ / api
16425 ca evaṃvādino jaiminīyāḥ svam eva vādaṃ sva-vācā vidhurayanti /
children.translated_text: and thus the <s>Jaiminīyas</s>, who hold this view, undermine their own position by their own words.

children.text: 16426 tathā hi /
children.translated_text: For example:

children.text: 16501 artho ayaṃ na ayam artho na iti śabdā vadanti na /
children.translated_text: "This is the meaning, this is not the meaning"—words do not declare this.

children.text: 16502 kalpyo ayam arthaḥ puruṣais te ca rāga-ādi-saṃyutāḥ //312//
children.translated_text: The meaning must be constructed by persons, and they are endowed with <s>rāga</s> (passion) and the like. //312//

As for the argument for rejecting the extraordinary nature of a person based on intelligence, sense-faculties, speech, and masculinity—that is indeed inconclusive. Because it is impossible for it to serve as both a general refutation and a specific proof. For one who does not perceive supersensible things cannot refute them. Since even [the opponent] does not know whether they exist. For this very reason, the opposition is unestablished. With what is not contradictory,

children.text: 16503 tatra ekas tattvavin na anya iti bhedaś ca kiṃ-kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Among them, one is a knower of truth and not another—by what is this distinction caused?

children.text: 16504 tadvat puṃstve katham api jñānī kaścit kathaṃ na vaḥ //313//
children.translated_text: Likewise, regarding masculinity, how is it that some knower [exists] and yet none according to you? //313//

children.text:
16506 na khalv ete vaidikāḥ śabdā evaṃ vikrośanti eta bhavanto brāhmaṇā
16507 ayam asmākam artho grāhyo na anya iti kevalam anabhivyakta-
16508 artha-viśeṣa-saṃsargāḥ śrutim abhipatanti / tatra ekaḥ puruṣaḥ
16509 kaṃcid arthaṃ kalpayaty anyo aparam / na ca śabdānāṃ
16510 kaścit svabhāva-pratiniyamo yena ekam artham anurundhate na aparam /
16511 kevalaṃ samaya-vaśāt taṃ tam āviśanto dṛśyante / teṣām
16512 avidita-artha-niyamānām atyakṣa-āveśād avidvān eva doṣa-upaplavaḥ
16513 kaścit tattvaṃ vyācaṣṭe na apara iti na nyāyyam / atha
16514 kutaścid atiśayād buddhi-indriya-ādīnāṃ sa eva vetti na aparaḥ / tasya
16515 kuto ayam atīndriya-jñāna-atiśayaḥ / tathā anyo api draṣṭā deśa-kāla-
16516 svabhāva-viprakṛṣṭānām arthānāṃ kim asambhavī dṛṣṭaḥ / na
16517 hi tat-pratikṣepa-sādhanāni kānicid yāni na enam upalīyante /
16518 yathā ayaṃ tat-sādhana-sambhave apy asya viśeṣas tathā anyasya api
children.translated_text: Just as this [person] has a special capacity even when the means for accomplishing that are available, so too another might—

children.text: 16519 syād ity anabhiniveśa eva yuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: therefore non-attachment [to one's own interpretation] alone is appropriate.

children.text: 16520 yasya pramāṇa-saṃvādi vacanaṃ so arthavid yadi /
children.translated_text: One whose words accord with valid means of knowledge—if he is a knower of meaning,

children.text: 16521 na hy atyantaparokṣeṣu pramāṇasya asti sambhavaḥ //314//
children.translated_text: then for what is completely beyond the senses, there is no possibility of a valid means of knowledge. //314//

Indeed, these Vedic words do not proclaim thus: "Listen, O <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, this is our meaning to be grasped, not another." They merely fall upon the ear without revealing any specific connection to a particular meaning. There, one person constructs one meaning, another constructs a different one. Nor is there any natural restriction of words to

children.text:
16522 syād etan na vayaṃ puruṣa-prāmāṇyāt kasyacid vyākhyānam
16523 abhiniviṣṭāḥ / kiṃ tarhi / pramāṇa-antara-saṃvādād / bahuṣv api
16524 vyākhyātṛṣu yaḥ pramāṇaṃ pratyakṣa-ādikaṃ saṃsyandayati so
16525 anumanyate / tan na / atīndriyeṣv adṛṣṭa-ādiṣu pramāṇa-antara-avṛtteḥ /
16526 tad-asambhavād eva hy āgamas tat-pratipatty-artham upayācyate /
16527 anyathā saty api tasmin pramāṇa-antara-avṛttāv apratipatteḥ / tataś
16601 ca kevalād artha-pratipatter asādhanam eva āgamaḥ syāt / kevalād anyato
16602 apy atīndriyeṣv apratipattir iti cet / katham atīndriyaś ca nāma
16603 pratyakṣa-ādi-viṣayaś ca / te punaḥ sva-viṣaye apy āgamam apekṣya eva
16604 sādhakāś cet / anāgamād dhūma-āder agny-ādi-pratyayo na syāt /
16605 na vai pravṛtta āgame pramāṇa-antaram anviṣyate kiṃ tarhi
16606 sa eva āgama-pravṛttir na jñāyata iti cet / svayaṃ samarthasya prasādhane
16607 asya tad-āgama-upadhānaṃ kam atiśayaṃ puṣṇāti / asamarthaṃ
16608 tv āgama-pravṛttim api na eva sādhayiṣyati / sā ca atīndriya-
16609 artha-sambaddhā āgama-pravṛttir atīndriyā katham anyena
16610 siddhā / anyac ca evam āgama-lakṣaṇaṃ syāt / tathā hi /
16611 yasya pramāṇa-saṃvādi vacanaṃ tat-kṛtaṃ vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: One whose words accord with valid means of knowledge—that speech is made by him;

children.text: 16612 sa āgama iti prāptaṃ nirarthā apauruṣeyatā //315//
children.translated_text: that is <s>āgama</s> (scripture)—thus it follows that the non-personal origin [of the <s>Veda</s>] is purposeless. //315//

It might be said: "We are not committed to any interpretation based on the authority of a person. Rather, among many interpreters, the one whose [interpretation] agrees with valid means of knowledge such as perception is approved." That is not so. Because other valid means of knowledge do not operate regarding supersensible things such as <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit). Since those [valid means] are impossible [in that domain],

children.text:
16613 tulye apy āgama-vāde pramāṇa-balād āgamasya kvacid āgamatve
16614 pramāṇa-saṃvādo vacanānām āgama-lakṣaṇaṃ syāt / na apuruṣa-
16615 kriyā / tasyāḥ sarva-artheṣu tulyatve api pramāṇa-abādhanāt pratipatteḥ /
16516 tad-bhāve apy anyatra pramāṇa-asaṃvādiny aniṣṭatvāt /
children.translated_text: Even when that [agreement] is present, elsewhere where there is no agreement with valid means of knowledge, [that speech] is undesirable.

children.text: 16617 kiṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: 16618 yady atyantaparokṣe arthe anāgama-jñāna-sambhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: If regarding an object completely beyond the senses there is no possibility of knowledge without scripture,

children.text: 16619 atīndriyārthavit kaścid asti ity abhimataṃ bhavet //316//
children.translated_text: then it would be accepted that there exists someone who knows objects beyond the senses. //316//

Even if the claim of scriptural authority is equal, by the force of valid means of knowledge, the defining mark of <s>āgama</s> (scripture) should be the agreement of words with valid means of knowledge—not non-human authorship. Because even when that [non-human authorship] is equal in all matters, understanding arises from non-obstruction by valid means of knowledge.

children.text:
16620 yady āgama-anapekṣaṃ jñāna-ayāthātathyaṃ puruṣasya iṣyate parokṣe
16621 arthe santi puruṣā atīndriyārthadṛśa iti iṣṭaṃ syāt / pratyakṣa-
16622 pūrvakānāṃ pramāṇānām atad-darśane asambhavāt / pratyakṣa-
16624 pramāṇam āgamaḥ / pramāṇa-antara-vṛttis tu pratyakṣam
16625 anvākarṣati iti na puruṣa-atiśayo nivāryaḥ syāt / tasmān na asty atīndriyeṣu
16626 pramāṇa-antara-vṛttiḥ / ata eva āgamasya artha-viśeṣa-vṛtter
16627 aparijñānād ayaṃ jaiminir anyo vā
children.translated_text: Due to not fully understanding, this <s>Jaimini</s> or another,

children.text: 16628 svayaṃ rāga-ādimān na arthaṃ vetti vedasya na anyataḥ /
children.translated_text: being himself possessed of <s>rāga</s> (passion) and the like, does not know the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>, nor [does he know it] from another source.

children.text: 16701 na vedayati vedo api veda-arthasya kuto gatiḥ //317//
children.translated_text: The <s>Veda</s> itself does not reveal [its meaning]—so whence is the understanding of Vedic meaning? //317//

If it is accepted that a person's knowledge regarding hidden objects can be incorrect without depending on scripture, then it would follow that there exist persons who see objects beyond the senses—since valid means of knowledge preceded by perception are impossible when perception [of that object] is absent. Perception [as a] valid means of knowledge is scripture. But the operation of other valid means of knowledge draws in perception, so not [merely based on] a person's—

children.text:
16702 sarva eva hi puruṣo anatikrānta-doṣa-viplavas tam atīndriyam
16703 artha-viśeṣa-pratiniyamaṃ vyākhyātā na svayaṃ vetti / na apy enam
16704 anyo vedayati / tasya api tulya-prasaṅgatvāt / na hy andhena ākṛśyamāṇo
16705 andhaḥ panthānaṃ pratipadyate / na api svayaṃ vedaḥ
16706 svārthaṃ vivṛṇoti / upadeśa-vaiyarthya-prasaṅgāt / tad ayam aparijñāta-
16707 arthaḥ śabda-gaḍur evaṃ śalyabhūto asad-darśana-snāyu
children.translated_text: The meaning, thus like a ball trapped in words, with the sinew of wrong views as a barb,

children.text: 16708 vinibaddho duruddharo duḥkham āsayati /
children.translated_text: bound fast, is difficult to extract and painfully lodges [in one].

children.text: 16709 tena agnihotraṃ juhuyāt svargakāma iti śrutau /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the <s>śruti</s> (Vedic statement) "One who desires heaven should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>,"

children.text: 16710 khādec śvamāṃsam ity eṣa na artha ity atra kā pramā //318//
children.translated_text: versus "One should eat dog-meat"—what valid means of knowledge [determines] that "this is not the meaning" here? //318//

For every person, not having transcended the distortions of faults, as an interpreter does not himself know that supersensory specific determination of meaning. Nor does another reveal it to him, since the same problem applies to him too. For a blind man being led by a blind man does not find the path. Nor does the <s>Veda</s> itself disclose its own meaning.

children.text:
16711 kvacid apy arthe pratyāsatti-viprakarṣa-rahitasya agnihotraṃ juhuyāt
16712 svargakāma ity ādi-vākyasya bhūta-viśeṣe yathā-abhimataṃ
16713 ghṛta-ādi prakṣiped ity ayam arthaḥ na punaḥ śvamāṃsaṃ khāded
16714 iti na atiśayaṃ paśyāmaḥ / nanv ayaṃ sarvatra samānaḥ prasaṅgaḥ
16715 parokṣa-daiśikānāṃ vacanānām arthaṃ yathā-abhiprāyam idānīntanāḥ
16716 kiṃ samanuyanti āhosvid viparyayam iti / na / upadeṣṭuḥ
16717 sva-abhiprāya-prakāśanena sampradāya-sambhavāt / na hy
16718 ayam adaiśikānāṃ śabdānāṃ sambhavati / loka-pratyāyana-abhiprāyaś
16719 ca bruvāṇo loka-saṃketa-prasiddhim anupālayati iti tato api
16720 tad-artha-siddhiḥ syāt na apauruṣeyāṇāṃ śabdānām / tatra kasyacit
16721 samīha-abhāvāt / api ca nyāyam eva anupālayantaḥ paṇḍitā heya-upādeya-
16722 tad-āśrayeṣu saṃghaṭante na tu pravāda-mātreṇa iti na samānaḥ
16723 prasaṅgaḥ / tac ca yathāvasaraṃ pratipādayiṣyāmaḥ / nanu
16724 kaścil loka-saṃniveśa-ādir ayukti-viṣayo api sambhāvanīya-puruṣa-
16725 vacanād arthaḥ pratipadyate / na / apratyayāt / na hi kvacid
16726 askhalita iti sarvaṃ tathā / vyabhicāra-darśanāt / tat pravṛtter
16801 avisaṃvādena vyāpty-asiddheś ca / agatyā ca idam āgama-lakṣaṇam
16802 iṣṭam / na ato niścayaḥ / tan na pramāṇam āgama ity apy uktam /
16803 apauruṣeyānāṃ śabdānām artha-jñānaṃ na sampradāyān
16804 na yukter na lokād iti tatra apratipattir nyāyyā / tatra api /
16805 prasiddho loka-vādaś cet /
children.translated_text: If common popular discourse is [said to be] well-established,

children.text: 16806 pratipatti-hetuḥ /
children.translated_text: [and is] the basis of understanding—

children.text: 16807 tatra ko atīndriyārthadṛk /
children.translated_text: then who among them perceives supersensible objects?

children.text: 16808 aneka-artheṣu śabdeṣu yena artho ayaṃ vivecitaḥ //319//
children.translated_text: Among words with multiple meanings, by whom has this [particular] meaning been discerned? //319//

Regarding any object, for the statement 'One who desires heaven should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>' and the like—which lacks proximity to or distance from [any particular meaning]—[the Mīmāṃsaka might say:] 'One should throw <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter) and such things into a particular material substance—this is the meaning; but not that one should eat dog-meat.' We do not see what superiority [one interpretation has over the other]. [Objection:] But this is a problem common to all cases—do people nowadays seek the meaning of statements made by speakers in remote places and times according to those speakers' own intention, or do they [understand] the opposite? [Reply:] No [problem]. Because tradition (<s>sampradāya</s>) is possible through the teacher's disclosure of his own intention. For this [tradition] is not possible for non-personal words. Moreover, one speaking with the intention of making people understand preserves the well-known conventional usage (<s>loka-saṃketa</s>), so from that too the establishment of that meaning would follow—but not for non-personal (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) words, since in their case no one has any intention. Furthermore, learned people who follow reason alone converge on matters of what is to be rejected, what is to be accepted, and their bases—not merely on the basis of assertions. Therefore it is not a common problem. And we shall demonstrate that at the appropriate occasion. [Objection:] But some meaning concerning the arrangement of the world and such things, even though it is not a subject of reasoning, is understood from the words of a person deemed trustworthy. [Reply:] No. Because of the absence of conviction. For [the fact] that someone has not erred somewhere does not make everything so—because deviation is observed. Because invariable concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>) is not established by the mere non-deception of that [person's previous] conduct. And this defining mark of <s>āgama</s> (scripture) is accepted only for lack of any alternative. Therefore there is no certainty from it. Hence it has been said that <s>āgama</s> is not a valid means of knowledge. There is no understanding of the meaning of non-personal words—not from tradition, not from reasoning, not from common usage—so non-comprehension regarding them is justified. In that case too:

17005 vṛtter anyasya api śaṅkanīyatvāt / yad uktam agnihotraṃ
17006 juhuyāt svargakāma ity atra śvamāṃsa-bhakṣaṇa-deśanā-vikalpo
17007 bhavatv iti sa na bhavati / pradeśa-antareṣu tathā tasya carcanāt /
17008 na / tasya artha-aparijñānāt / pradeśa-antareṣv api tathāvidha-artha-
17009 kalpanāyā anivāryatvāt / yadi hi kvacid vidita-artho ayam apauruṣeyaḥ
17010 śabda-rāśiḥ syāt tadā tato artha-pratītiḥ syāt / te tu bāhulye
17011 apy andhā eva sarva iti yatheṣṭam praṇīyante / tasmāt /
17012 śabda-antareṣu tādṛkṣu tādṛśy eva astu kalpanā //320//
children.translated_text: For this common worldly usage is not [based] on a non-personal word-meaning connection. What then? [It is based] on convention—like the usage of <s>Pāṇinīya</s> grammar and the like, [which operates] by the convention of its own author. Because instruction is required. For instruction is not appropriate for that [word-meaning relation] which is non-personal, since no one is ignorant of it [if it were self-evident]. Because it is supersensible. If it were sensible, the unwanted consequence would be that one would understand it by oneself—like forms and such. And when persons who are autonomous give instruction, since the non-deception of their instruction regarding what is truly the case is not established, there is no confidence. [Objection:] Just as the <s>Veda</s> [is non-personal], so its commentary too is non-personal, having come down through unbroken tradition—from that the meaning is established. [Reply:] If that [commentary] too is of the nature of words, the same objection applies: 'How is its meaning known?' For a person, by whatever device—even a 'horn-grasping' (far-fetched) method—might at least make an ignorant person understand the meaning of words that he himself has composed. Thus there is a means for understanding the meaning of person-made words. But a non-personal word does not do this. And no one is capable of knowing any fixed meaning-connection of it. Therefore there is simply non-comprehension of its meaning. Moreover, the <s>Veda</s> or its commentary, when being taught by a person to a person, continues only with an unbroken tradition—so here too convention is the refuge. Because we do not see any composition otherwise made, [whether] by those who would corrupt the <s>āgama</s> (tradition) through arrogance, or through hatred of that [rival] school-system in order to deceive those who have accepted that [teaching], or through the vice of charlatanry, or from some other cause. Moreover, here you have clearly forgotten your own stated position out of attachment to your own doctrine: 'A person affected by passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like might speak even what is untrue, therefore his word is not a valid means of knowledge.' Why is that not examined here too—whether it applies or not? That very person who teaches, being subject to disturbance, might teach the <s>Veda</s> or the meaning of the <s>Veda</s> otherwise as well. For it is heard that certain branches [of the <s>Veda</s>] that had disappeared have been restored by certain persons. Even now some [branches] have few students. Likewise, even those with many students might at some time somehow be destroyed. And since there is no possibility of accepting [a return to] abundance from belief in [merely] reputed persons, and since those who propagate them—having sometimes studied and then forgotten—or others, might teach otherwise due to fear of loss of reputation and the like, and since the devotees of those [teachers] understand without critical examination from trust in them, and since abundant acceptance is seen from a reputed person among many students—from that too, some deception is possible. Moreover:

children.text: 17013 yādṛśy agnihotraṃ juhuyāt svargakāma ity asya vākyasya / api

children.translated_text: Furthermore,

children.text: 17015 prasiddhiś ca nṛṇāṃ vādaḥ pramāṇaṃ sa ca na iṣyate /
children.translated_text: Common discourse among men is [what constitutes] 'established usage,' and that [common discourse] is [itself] not accepted [by you] as a valid means of knowledge.

children.text: 17016 tataś ca bhūyo artha-gatiḥ kim etad dviṣṭa-kāmitam //321//
children.translated_text: From that [follows] further non-comprehension of meaning—what is this [self-contradictory] desire of those who hate [personhood]? //321//
In other similar words, let there be just such an [arbitrary] interpretation [as well]. //320//

children.text:
17017 na prasiddhir nāma anyā anyatra jana-pravādāt / te ca sarve janā
17018 rāga-ādy-avidyā-aparītatvād asambhāvanīya-yāthātathya-vacanāḥ /
17019 tad eṣāṃ pravādo na pramāṇam / na hi kasyacid api samyak-pratipatter
17020 abhāve bāhulyam artha-vad bhavati / pāraśīka-mātṛ-mithyā-
17021 cāra-vat / teṣām eva puruṣāṇāṃ vacanāt punaḥ parokṣa-artha-sampratipattir
17101 iti kathaṃ tad eva yugapad dveṣyaṃ ca kāmyaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: so how can that [popular discourse] be simultaneously despised and desired?

children.text: 17102 atha prasiddhim ullaṅghya kalpane na nibandhanam /
children.translated_text: And if, overstepping established usage, [you say] there is no basis for the interpretation—

children.text: 17103 prasiddher apramāṇatvāt tat-grahe kiṃ nibandhanam //322//
children.translated_text: since established usage is not a valid means of knowledge, what is the basis for accepting it? //322//

'Established usage' (<s>prasiddhi</s>) is nothing other than popular discourse. And all those people, not being free from ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) in the form of passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like, are persons whose words cannot be credited with truth. Therefore their discourse is not a valid means of knowledge. For in the absence of any correct understanding, mere numerousness does not become authoritative—like the Persian custom of intercourse with one's mother. From the words of those very same persons there is again understanding of a remote object—

children.text:
17105 prāpta-pratilomanena anyatra pravṛttir guṇa-doṣa-sandarśanena yuktā
17106 iti prasiddher anvaya iti cet / na / prāpteḥ pramāṇa-vṛtti-lakṣaṇatvāt /
17107 yat kiṃcana grahaṇaṃ hi prasiddhim apramāṇayatas
17108 tan-mukhena pratītiḥ / nyāyāt prāpti-pratiṣedhāt / tulyā sva-para-
17109 vikalpayor ubhayathā api vṛttir iti kaḥ prasiddhāv anurodhaḥ /
17110 api ca iyam
children.translated_text: Moreover, this very

children.text: 17111 utpāditā prasiddhyā eva śaṅkā śabda-artha-niścaye /
children.translated_text: doubt regarding the determination of word-meaning has been generated by established usage itself,

children.text: 17112 yasmān nānā-artha-vṛttitvaṃ śabdānāṃ tatra dṛśyate //323//
children.translated_text: since words are seen there [in common usage] to function with multiple meanings. //323//

[Objection:] Having encountered [established usage], activity elsewhere in opposition to it, guided by the observation of merits and faults, is justified—thus there is a [logical] connection with established usage. [Reply:] No. Because 'encounter' (<s>prāpti</s>) has the character of the operation of a valid means of knowledge. For whatever grasping [there is while] not treating established usage as a valid means of knowledge—through that [grasping] comes understanding. Because of the rejection of encounter by [the demands of] reason. The operation is equal in both alternatives—one's own and the other's—so what attachment is there to established usage?

children.text:
17113 na prasiddher eka-artha-niścayaḥ śabdānāṃ tata eva śaṅkā-utpatteḥ /
17114 nānā-arthā hi śabdā loke dṛśyante / loka-vādaś ca pratītiḥ / ata eva
17115 nānā-arthā iti tata eka-artha-niyamo na yuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: since they have multiple meanings, a restriction to one meaning from that [established usage] is not justified.

children.text: 17116 anyathā asambhava-abhāvān nānā-śakteḥ svayaṃ dhvaneḥ /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, in the absence of [proof of] impossibility [of multiple meanings], since the sound itself has multiple powers,

children.text: 17117 avaśyaṃ śaṅkayā bhāvyaṃ niyāmakam apaśyatām //324//
children.translated_text: doubt must necessarily arise for those who see no determining factor. //324//

There is no single-meaning determination of words from established usage, since doubt arises from that very [source]. For words are seen in the world to have multiple meanings. And common discourse is the [basis of] understanding. Therefore,

children.text:
17118 ity antaraślokaḥ / tasmād avidita-artha-vibhāgeṣu śabdeṣv ekam
17119 artham atyakṣa-saṃyogam anālambana-samāropaṃ viniścitya vyācakṣāṇo
17120 jaiminis tad-vyājena svam eva matam āha iti na tīrthakara-
17121 antarād asya viśeṣaṃ paśyāmaḥ / tathā hi / tad-artha-vacana-vyāpāra-
17122 śūnyasya tat-samāropeṇa abhidhānaṃ na sva-vacanam atiśete /
17123 tat-kāriṇā kevalaṃ mithyā-vinītatā eva ātmanaḥ samuddyotitā syāt
children.translated_text: By doing that, only a false humility has been displayed by him.

children.text: 17124 tathā hi /
children.translated_text: For example:

children.text: 17125 eṣa sthāṇur ayaṃ mārga iti vakti iti kaścana /
children.translated_text: 'This is a post, this is the road'—thus says some person.

children.text: 17126 anyaḥ svayaṃ bravīmi iti tayor bhedaḥ parikṣyatām //325//
children.translated_text: Another says 'I myself declare [it]'—let the difference between the two be examined. //325//

This is an intermediate verse. Therefore, among words whose meaning-distinctions are unknown, having determined one meaning—unconnected with perception, a superimposition without support—and expounding [it], <s>Jaimini</s>, under that pretext, states his own opinion. We do not see any difference between him and any other sectarian teacher (<s>tīrthakara</s>). For indeed: for one who is devoid of any activity of expressing that meaning, the attribution [of meaning] through superimposition does not surpass his own [personal] statement.

children.text:
17201 nirabhiprāya-vyāpāra-vacane sthāṇau samāropya-upadiśataḥ svatantrasya
17202 vā svayaṃ vacana-upagame na kaścid viśeṣo anyatra jaḍasya
17203 pratipatti-māndyāt / api ca eka-artha-niyame saty enaṃ jaiminir
17204 jānīyāt / sa eva śabdasya
17205 sarvatra yogyasya eka-artha-dyotane niyamaḥ kutaḥ /
17206 na hi śabdasya kaścid arthaḥ svabhāva-niyataḥ sarvatra yogyatvāt /
17207 ayogyatve ca tad-apracyuter avidheyasya puruṣāṇāṃ kvacid
children.translated_text: And in the case of incapacity, since [the word] does not depart from that [incapacity], for what is ungovernable, a person's leading toward

children.text: 17208 upanayana-apanayana-asambhavāt /
children.translated_text: or away from some [particular meaning] is impossible.

children.text: 17209 jñātā vā atīndriyāḥ kena vivakṣā-vacanād ṛte //326//
children.translated_text: Or by whom are supersensible [meanings] known, apart from a [deliberate] intention to speak? //326//

There is no difference between one who, superimposing upon a purposeless non-intentional word, teaches [a meaning], and one who independently accepts [that] the statement is his own—except that the foolish person's understanding is slower [in the first case]. Moreover, if there were a restriction to a single meaning, <s>Jaimini</s> would know it. That very restriction of a word—which is capable [of denoting] everywhere—to illuminating a single meaning: whence [does it come]? For no meaning of a word is determined by its inherent nature, since it is capable [of denoting] everywhere.

children.text:
17210 puruṣa-praṇīte hi śabde kayācid vivakṣayā sa tāṃ kadācit kvacin
17211 nivedayed api iti vivakṣā-pūrvakānāṃ śabdānām artha-niyamaḥ
17212 pratīyeta api / apauruṣeye tu vidyamāno apy artha-niyamaḥ kathaṃ
17213 vijñeyaḥ / svabhāva-bhedasya abhāvāt / sati vā pratyakṣasya svayaṃ
17214 pratīti-prasaṅgāt / apratyakṣe api kenacij jñātum aśakyatvāt /
17215 na ca asti kaścid viśeṣaḥ / sarva-śabdā hi sarva-artha- pratyāsatti-viprakarṣa-
17216 rahitāḥ / tatas teṣām
17217 vivakṣā niyame hetuḥ saṃketas tat-prakāśanaḥ /
17218 apauruṣeye sā na asti tasya sā ekārthatā kutaḥ //327//

children.translated_text: For in the case of a person-made word, someone might at some time disclose to someone that [he made it] with a certain intention—thus the restriction of meaning is understood for words preceded by intention. But for a non-personal [word], even if a restriction of meaning exists, how is it to be known? Because there is no difference of inherent nature [among words]. Or if there were [such a difference], the unwanted consequence would be that perception would comprehend it by itself. Even when imperceptible, because it cannot be known by anyone. And there is no distinguishing feature whatsoever. For all words lack proximity to and distance from all meanings. Therefore, of them—

children.text:
17219 vivakṣayā hi śabdo arthe niyamyate na svabhāvataḥ tasya
17220 kvacid apratibandhena sarvatra tulyatvāt / yatra api pratibandhas
17221 tad-abhidhāna-niyama-abhāvāt / sarva-śabdaiḥ karaṇānām abhidhāna-
17222 prasaṅgāt / tasmād vivakṣā-prakāśanāya abhiprāya- nivedana-lakṣaṇaḥ
17223 saṃketaḥ kriyate / apauruṣeye tu na vivakṣā na saṃketaḥ
17224 kasyacid abhiprāya-abhāvād iti na niyamo na taj-jñānam /
17225 svabhāva-niyame anyatra na yojyeta tayā punaḥ /
17226 yadi saṃketa-nirapekṣaḥ svabhāvata eva artheṣu śabdo nilīnaḥ
17227 syāt uktam atra apratibandhād aniyama iti / api ca / svābhāvike
17228 vācyavācakabhāve na punar vivakṣayā yatheṣṭaṃ niyujyeta /
17301 saṃketaś ca nirarthaḥ syād /
17302 na hi svabhāva-bheda indriya-gamyaḥ sva-pratītau paribhāṣā-ādikam
17303 apekṣate / nīla-ādi-bheda-vat / tad-apekṣa-pratītayas tu na vastu-svabhāvāḥ /
17304 kiṃ tarhi / sāmayikā rāja-cihna-ādi-vat / yaś ca sāmayikaḥ
17305 sa svabhāva-niyato ayuktas tasya icchā-vṛtteḥ / ata eva saṃketāt
17306 svabhāva-viśeṣasya
17307 vyaktau ca niyamaḥ kutaḥ //328//

17308 sva-icchā-vṛttiḥ saṃketaḥ sa iha eva kartuṃ śakyate na anyatra iti
17309 na uparodho asti / sa ca puruṣaiḥ sva-icchayā kriyamāṇas tam eva
17310 svabhāvaṃ vyanakti na anyam iti na niyamo asti /
17311 yatra svātantryam icchāyā niyamo nāma tatra kaḥ /
17312 dyotayet tena saṃketo na iṣṭām eva asya yogyatām //329//
17313 iti antaraślokaḥ /
17314 yasmāt kila īdṛśaṃ satyaṃ yathā agniḥ śīta-nodanaḥ /
17315 vākyaṃ veda-ekadeśatvād anyad apy aparo abravīt //330//

17316 anyas tv apauruṣeyam āgama-lakṣaṇaṃ parityajya anyathā prāmāṇyaṃ
17317 vedasya sādhayitukāmaḥ prāha avitathāni veda-vākyāni
17318 yatra apratipattir veda-ekadeśatvāt yathā agnir himasya
17319 bheṣajam ity ādi-vākyam iti / tasya idam /
17320 rasa-vat tulya-rūpatvād eka-bhāṇḍe ca pāka-vat /
17321 śeṣavad vyabhicāritvāt kṣiptaṃ nyāyavidā īdṛśam //331//

17322 svayam īdṛśam ācāryeṇa anumānaṃ naiyāyika-śeṣavad-anumāna-
17323 vyabhicāram udbhāvayatā tulya-rūpatayā phalānāṃ tulya-rasa-
17324 sādhana-vad eka-sthāly-antargamād dṛṣṭa-vad adṛṣṭa-taṇḍula-pāka-
17325 sādhana-vac ca asādhanam uktam / tad-asādhanatva-nyāyaś ca
17326 pūrvam eva uktaḥ / uktaṃ ca idam āgama-lakṣaṇam asmābhiḥ tat tu
17327 sarvasya śakya-vicārasya viṣayasya yathāsvaṃ pramāṇena vidhi-
17328 pratiṣedha-viśuddhau nāntarīyakatva-abhāve api śabdānām artheṣu
17401 varaṃ saṃśayitasya vṛttiḥ tatra kadācid avisaṃvāda-sambhavāt
17402 na tv anyatra dṛṣṭa-pramāṇa-uparodhasya puruṣasya pravṛttir iti /
17403 yaḥ punaḥ prākṛta-viṣayasya vahneḥ śīta-pratighāta-sāmarthyasya
17404 abhidhānaṃ satya-artham upadarśya sarvaṃ satya-artham āha
17405 śāstraṃ śakya-paricchede api viṣaye pramāṇa-virodhād bahutaram
17406 ayuktam api /
17407 nityasya puṃsaḥ kartṛtvaṃ nityān bhāvān atīndriyān /
17408 aindriyān viṣamaṃ hetuṃ bhāvānāṃ viṣamāṃ sthitim //332//
17409 nivṛttiṃ ca pramāṇābhyām anyad vā vyasta-gocaram /
17410 viruddham āgama-apekṣeṇa anumānena vā vadat //333//
17411 virodham asamādhāya śāstra-arthaṃ ca apradarśya saḥ /
17412 satya-arthaṃ pratijānāno jayed dhārṣṭyena bandhakīm //334//

17414 apracyuta-anutpanna-pūrvāpara-rūpaḥ pumān kartā krameṇa karmaṇāṃ
17415 karma-phalānāṃ ca bhoktā samavāyi-kāraṇa-adhiṣṭhāna-bhāva-ādinā
17416 ity āha vedaḥ tac ca ayuktam ity āvedita-prāyam nityatvaṃ ca
17417 keṣāṃcid bhāvānām akṣaṇikasya vastu-dharma-atikramād ayuktam
17418 apratyakṣāny eva hi sāmānya-ādīni pratyakṣāni janma-sthiti-
17419 nivṛttīś ca viṣamāḥ padārthānām anādheyaviśeṣasya prāg akartuḥ
17420 para-apekṣayā janakatvam niṣpatter akārya-rūpasya āśraya-vaśena
17421 sthānam kāraṇāc ca vināśa ity ādikam anyad api pratyakṣa-
17422 anumānābhyāṃ prasiddhi-viparyayam āgama-āśrayeṇa ca anumānena
17423 bādhitam agnihotra-ādeḥ pāpa-śodhana-sāmarthya-ādikam / tasya
17424 evaṃvādino vedasya sarvatra śāstra-śarīre pramāṇa-virodham
17425 apratisamādhāya sambandha-anuguṇa-upāya-puruṣa-artha-abhidhānāni ca
17426 śāstra-dharmān apradarśya-atyanta-prasiddha-viṣaya-satya-abhidhāna-
17427 mātreṇa prajñā-prakarṣa-duravagaha-gahane api niratyayatāṃ sādhayitukāmo
17428 bandhakīm api prāgalbhyena vijayate / kācit kila
17429 bandhakī svayaṃ svāminā vipratipatti-sthāne dṛṣṭvā upālabdhā / sā
17430 taṃ pratyuvāca / paśyata mātaḥ puruṣasya vaiparītyaṃ / mayi
17431 dharma-patnyāṃ pratyayam akṛtvā ātmīyayor na itara-abhidhānayor
17432 jala-budbudayoḥ / karoti / tena jaratkāṇena grāmya-kāṣṭha-hārakeṇa
17501 prārthitā api na saṃgatā / rūpa-guṇa-anurāgena kila mantri-mukhya-
17502 dārakaṃ kāmaye aham iti / evaṃjātīyakam etad api vahneḥ
17503 śīta-pratīkāra-vacanena dṛṣṭa-pramāṇa-virodhasya apy atyantaparokṣe
17504 arthe avisaṃvāda-anumānam /
17505 sidhyed pramāṇaṃ yady evam apramāṇam atha iha kim /
17506 na hy ekaṃ na asti satya-arthaṃ puruṣe bahu-bhāṣiṇi //335//

17507 yathā idam atiduṣkaram atyanta-satya-abhidhānaṃ tathā atyanta-asatya-
17508 abhidhānam api / tatra ekasya vacanasya kathaṃcit saṃvādena aviśiṣṭasya
17509 tad-vacana-rāśes tathābhāve na kaścit puruṣo anāptaḥ
17510 syāt / api ca /
17511 na ayaṃ svabhāvaḥ kāryaṃ vā vastūnāṃ vaktari dhvaniḥ /
17512 na ca tad-vyatiriktasya vidyate avyabhicāritā //336//

17513 na tāvad etad vacanaṃ vācyānāṃ svabhāvaḥ / na apy eṣāṃ kāryam
17514 tad-abhāve api vaktur vivakṣā-mātreṇa bhāvāt / na ca anyaḥ
17515 kaścit kasyacid avyabhicārī / vyabhicāre ca tato anyathā api
17516 tat-sambhavāt tad-bhāvāt tat-pratītir ayuktā /
17517 pravṛttir vācakānāṃ ca vācya-dṛṣṭi-kṛtā iti cet /
17518 syād etat kāryam eva vacanaṃ vācakasya vācya-darśana-vṛtter /
17519 evaṃ sati /
17520 paraspara-viruddha-arthā katham ekatra sā bhavet //337//

17521 yady eṣa pratiniyamo vācyaṃ vastv antareṇa śabdo na pravartata
17522 iti / bhinneṣu pravādeṣv ekatra vastuni viruddha-svabhāva-upasaṃhāreṇa
17523 vacana-vṛttir na syāt / na hy ayaṃ sambhavo asti ekaḥ
17524 śabdo niṣparyāyaṃ nityaś ca syād anityaś ca iti /
17525 vastubhir na āgamās tena kathaṃcin nāntarīyakāḥ /
17526 pratipattuḥ prasidhyanti kutas tebhyo artha-niścayaḥ //338//

17527 āgamaṃ pramāṇaṃ tad-ādarśita-artha-pratipattaye ajño janaḥ samanveṣate
17528 samadhigata-yāthātathyānām upadeśa-anapekṣaṇāt / ajñasya
17529 ca atīndriya-guṇa-puruṣa-vivecane asāmarthyāt / vacanānāṃ
17601 samīhita-artha-sattām antareṇa api vṛttiṃ paśyato bhavitavyam eva adṛṣṭa-
17602 vyabhicāra-vacasām api puruṣāṇāṃ vāci śaṅkayā kiṃ yathārthā
17603 na vā iti / tena na yuktam anena kasyacid vacanena kiṃcin
17604 niścetum /
17605 tasmān na tan-nivṛttyā api bhāva-abhāvaḥ prasidhyati /
17606 yad uktaṃ sarva-viṣayatvād āgamasya sati vastuny avisaṃvādena
17607 asya vṛttes tan-nivṛtti-lakṣaṇa-anupalabdhir abhāvaṃ sādhayati
17608 iti tad asya sarva-viṣayatve api vastv-antareṇa āvṛttau syāt / tac
17609 ca na asti / tataḥ pratipattukāmasya asiddhir ity uktam /
